## M320 (2026-10-01): M119-v2 pack-temperature ladder: support-gated, data-driven levels (20 / 42.5 C on both sides) replace the fixed 20/28/35 C literals; hazard-ratio cards and temperature profile added

**Rationale.** Owner request (the 20/28/35 C pack-temperature surface levels of M119-v2 are too close to each other and will not span the shoulder/cold season; make the temperature ladder visually distinctive without overloading the user; the Director decides the method). Spec analyses/M320_spec.md rev 2 (committed 5d15f63 before any result; Director: revise -> folded in). The fitted model is NOT changed: the final fit is refit from the M318 tables and reproduces the stored M318 surfaces exactly (known-answer, max abs diff 0). Rule (pre-registered): levels = seconds-weighted P5/P50/P95 of the at-risk pack temperature per side, snapped to a 2.5 C grid; a level needs >= 100 events on >= 10 event days in a +/-2.5 C band; levels are kept only if their log-hazard contrast is DISTINCT (percentile AND basic lower bound >= log 1.25, day-clustered bootstrap, 4000 draws, seed 42, whole-pipeline refit per draw, 0 failed draws; fixed-sequence {P5,P95} then P50). Result (tools/m320_ladder.py, analyses/M320_result.json): both sides select two levels, 20 C (reference) and 42.5 C; P50 dropped. Hazard ratio 42.5 C vs 20 C (median demand, 15 s; model-derived, associational): START 1.82 [1.40, 2.42], STOP 2.17 [1.66, 3.03]; the contrast is the same in all 49 (start) / 57 (stop) SoC x speed cells supported at both levels, because the fitted model has pack temperature interacting only with demand (a model property, not an observation). Legacy diagnostics: START 20 vs 28 C D 0.056 [0.003, 0.179] indistinct (the premise holds); STOP 20 vs 28 C D 0.594 [0.399, 0.829] distinct: the pre-registered falsification clause fires on the stop side (legacy premise not supported: 20 vs 28 C differ); no further change is established between 28 and 42.5 C (stop 28-42.5: D 0.183 [0.022, 0.387] indistinct). Disclosures: the 42.5 C band rests on events from 19 (start) / 19 (stop) calendar days (< 20: limited day support, few clusters for the day bootstrap; hot-band days are seasonally clustered) and lies above the upper boundary knot (41.5 / 42 C): linear tail, spline-constrained; day-weighted quantile levels differ from the pre-registered seconds-weighted ones (method disagreement); the start P50 level moved between the 410- and 489-drive corpora (35 -> 32.5 C); secondary-cell disagreement (e.g. stop demandHigh indistinct) is method disagreement; D is identical at every cell-count threshold, which is uninformative under a cell-uniform model, not robustness evidence; knot-placement sensitivity was not tested (follow-up). A knee level near 28 C on the stop side is a new spec (M321+), not a tuning of this one. Dashboard: surfaces re-levelled; support mask now conditional on pack temperature; reference level preselected; new panel 'Pack-temperature contrast' (hazard-ratio card in place of a uniform difference map, a Director-accepted deviation; 1-D hazard-vs-temperature profile with CI band, at-risk rug, linear-tail shading and level markers); every figure binds to S.socHysteresisV2.tempLadder and the stamp 'ladder basis N drives' is always shown. Part C (ingestion drift monitor) is NOT built: it is a follow-up milestone and must merge before the next ingestion (Director). Deviation recorded: the ladder is tied to the V2 fit basis and carried between refits, not re-derived on every ingestion (Director-accepted). Blind audit: counts, quantiles, snapped levels, band support exact on both sides; contrast reproduced (the 0.004/0.012 gap to the auditor's first spline was a basis-construction difference: with the module's spline it reproduces -0.5992 / -0.7768); independent day-clustered bootstrap (auditor's script, own seeds, 1000 draws per side, 0 failed): percentile lower bounds 0.3358 (start) and 0.5154 (stop) vs claimed 0.336 and 0.506, i.e. 0.02 and 0.98 Monte-Carlo SE apart (criterion: within 3 SE); deviations from the spec: 1000 draws not 40 x 100, SE by the asymptotic quantile formula with a 10 x 100 batch-means cross-check, comparison computed in the main session from the auditor's draws (its first run hit a MemoryError at 10 workers and was resumed with the same seeds; the auditor did not return a final brief after the interruption). Director: revise -> conditions applied. Labels: model-derived, associational (confounded with season, date and pack age), conditional on level selection, never 'no effect'; fitted on today's raw/ (F03): not M299-reproducible; dashboard-only, not article-eligible, no Andrii sign-off required.

## M317 (2026-09-30): Huber spread follow-ups: append-only fit provenance (spread_fit_history.json, spreadFitProvenance) and a calibrated two-stage bootstrap interval for the Huber-adjusted slope

**Rationale.** Follow-ups from the Director's M312 decision, via new-analysis (spec analyses/M317_spec.md rev 2, committed before any result; Director review applied; Amendment 1 after the design-1 calibration). PART A: tools/record_spread_fit.py appends one record per distinct (master MD5, estimator-code key) to the append-only spread_fit_history.json (keep-set sha256, first-stage coefficients incl. n_iter and scale, slope (i) labelled as an OLS slope on the Huber-adjusted series with an OLS-first-stage CI, slope (ii) with the Part B intervals, function-source hashes, library versions, git commit) and publishes the latest record as arrays block spreadFitProvenance (new ingestion stage record_spread_fit; release_check ties it to cellHealthTrend). Standing bT watch: first stage refit leaving the last 8 days out, report-only flag (sign flip or |delta bT| > half the bT day-clustered CI width): not raised (delta bT 0.026 vs half CI width 0.080). PART B: cellHealthTrend gains huberSlopeCi95 for huberSlopeMvPerMo. Real data: point 0.083 mV/month, n=465, 100 days; HEADLINE (S1, two-stage day-clustered bootstrap, 4000 draws, seed 42) [-0.22, 0.36]; conditional (first stage held fixed) [-0.24, 0.38] (half-width ratio to S1 1.068, not materially wider); 7-day-block intervals, UNCALIBRATED: S2 [-0.44, 0.46] (ratio to S1 1.563) and S2-S1 [-0.42, 0.41] (1.427), both materially wider, so the dashboard shows the wider one and follows it for zero-inclusion: every interval includes zero, trend not established. Calibration (tools/m317_calibration.py, 500 simulated datasets each, 1000 draws, real drives-per-day, co-trending T and I, day effects, t(3) noise): design 1 (strong co-trend) S1 coverage 0.948, conditional 1.000 (over-covers, fails the band [0.92, 0.98]); design 2 (weak co-trend, fixed from a ratio-only pilot, scale 0.25) S1 0.932, conditional 0.954. Under the pre-registered failure path S1 replaced the conditional primary as the published interval (Amendment 1, Director-accepted). In simulation the point estimate is biased toward zero by 0.02-0.04 mV/month (about a third of its SD in both designs; design-specific; no corrected estimate). Blind audit reproduced the slope exactly and the intervals within bootstrap noise; day clustering adequate at lag 1 (lag-1 autocorrelation 0.14, not distinguishable from 0 with 100 days). DEVIATIONS RECORDED: (1) calibration target is the pseudo-true theta (design 1: 0.113, design 2: 0.2965), not the planted time slope (0.30), because co-trending T and I absorb part of it; (2) the script's bias check (mean error within 2 Monte-Carlo SE) fails in both designs while the spec criterion (within 2 bootstrap SE) passes; (3) calibration used 1000 draws (production 4000); (4) the conditional primary was replaced by S1 because of over-coverage (conservative), not under-coverage; (5) design 2 was fixed from the conditional:S1 half-width ratio of the real data (1.07, pilot 1.09) without looking at coverage; Amendment 1 had written 0.9-1.0, which is the S1:conditional direction; (6) audit S1 upper endpoint 0.380 vs our 7-seed range 0.356-0.376 (analyses/M317_s1_seed_spread.json): consistent with Monte-Carlo noise plus implementation differences, not an exact reproduction; (7) an earlier draft brief quoted the week-block ratios against the conditional interval (1.46, 1.34); the ratios to S1 above are the script-written ones. Isolation: only cellHealthTrend (huberSlopeCi95, huberSlopeCiFailedDraws, huberSlopeCiMethod), the new spreadFitProvenance block and their stamps changed; master unchanged (MD5 bd9d10726bb064d857cf9ff98d2b7338). Non-authoritative (degradationTrends.cellSpread governs); not article-eligible. Dashboard: M19 block shows the Huber slope with its S1 interval, the wider sensitivity interval, the calibration and bias disclosure, all bound to payload keys. release_check.py PASSED; tests/synthetic/test_huber_slope_ci.py passes.

### M294 — prose and label corrections, plus 3 staleness defects

**New helper.** A `M294` block of derived values in the JSX. Every corrected sentence binds to it (`S.*`), not to typed literals.

**Conclusions**
- Comparator changed to gross/discharge.
- "Scales with 2.1 kWh" split into three parts: measured kWh, capacity-normalised GTC/FCE/C-rate, and SoC-derived EFC.
- "Generator charging dominates / regen 30–42 %" replaced by operating-state shares: 65.4 % engine-on, 27.8 % engine-off braking, 21.8 % overlap.
- SoC-reset sentence is now generated from `socBandReset.windows`.
- The 25–30 % spec-cycle comparison is removed. Now reads "52.61 % ≤2 % DoD, max 40.5 %".
- Dates and regimes are bound to the payload: "May 11 – Sep 22, Warm/Shoulder; no Cold".
- "Regen capture efficiency" is renamed "apparent kinetic-energy recovery proxy" in the text and on 3 chart titles.
- Power fade: "a power proxy can be monitored; capacity SOH cannot".
- The note that net discharge tracks cell load is corrected.

**Heat soak.** The "×slower" claim and the 7.2 h half-life prose are retired, because the fit has R² = −1.82. The glossary entry for τ is also fixed.

**Health**
- "NOT YET MEASURABLE" becomes "moderately cool exposure measured": 40 of 422 peaks are below 20 °C, the coldest 14 °C. Plating is not measured.
- 5.86 Ah is relabelled as an assumed denominator.
- The stale "10 → 16" counter is removed.
- The retired sign-change history is removed.

**§4 (pack-terminal energy)**
- "Every energy figure originates at this sensor" and "Measured — where energy came from" are rewritten.
- Tile labels now name operating states.
- The 6.2 % imbalance is described as a signed imbalance, not round-trip inefficiency.
- `energyPath.basis` and the `chargeSources` details are reworded in the builder source (`_energy_path`) as well.

**Records.** "Equilibrates", "BMS allowed", "SoC floor forces", "spec cycle", "mechanical driver of…", "peaks all occur warm", "BMS tapers" and "211 % load capability" are reworded in the `_records` source and in the payload.

## M291 (2026-09-22): Audit Bucket-B remediation (B3–B8) + a stamp-vs-value staleness the M290 sync missed — arrays rebuilt to the corrected e077cc83 master, full gate chain green

**Trigger.** Continuation of the 22 Sep deep-audit triage (see M290): the user authorised the feasible Bucket-B
fixes (B3, B4, B6, B7, B8) and confirmed the 410 raw CSVs are in Project Knowledge. Doing B4/B6 surfaced a
**data-integrity defect M290 did not fully resolve**, which is fixed here. No `drive_master.csv` bytes or corpus
MD5 change (corpus stays **e077cc8365c0fe3142192be4f2939ab5**); every edit is corpus-invariant (values recomputed
from the *same* corrected master, plus display/disclosure structure). Build + `validate_jsdom` + Track-4 suite +
cohort-rate contract + release payload checks all pass.

**0. CRITICAL (found here) — M290 re-stamp was a stamp-vs-value false-green; arrays' derived KPIs were still the
pre-distance-fix values.** M290 recovered the M289 `summary_arrays.json`, spliced the registry/cohortMeta and
**re-stamped every key to e077cc83**, so the M220.2 artifact-stamp gate passed. But the re-stamped arrays still
carried the values computed from the **pre-repair** master: EnergyIntensity `all` = **17.098072 / n=395**,
StartsPer100km `all` = **911.52 / nEligible=397**, corpus exposure **8434.8 km** — while the live e077cc83 master
recomputes to **17.10218 / 396**, **911.62 / 398**, **8437.74 km**. Root cause is the single M289 repair drive
`20260906_122920` (`distance_km` −2.5 → 0.44): under the `km>0` paired-eligibility rule it flips from *excluded* to
*included*, shifting every headline that ratio-of-sums over the corpus. The stamp matched the master's identity but
the numbers did not match the master's content — exactly the "false-green" the audit warned about, one layer deeper.
This was independently confirmed by `test_track4.py` test 1 (EnergyIntensity must equal an in-pandas paired
ratio-of-sums with matching `n`), which the committed payload would have **failed** against the corrected master.
*Fix:* recomputed the affected KPIs from the corrected master with the pipeline's own estimators —
`refresh_seasonal_kpis.py` for EnergyIntensity + CohortExposure, and an identical day-cluster bootstrap
(events, B=4000, seed=20260919) for StartsPer100km (its warm cohort reproduces the committed CI byte-for-byte,
validating the method). Propagated the corrected corpus exposure (8434.8 → 8437.74 km; shoulder 401.5 → 404.44 km)
to every `coverage/all` block, `cohortMeta`, `_meta.nativeEquivalence`, and the DriveType shoulder-urban km; and
refreshed the two Rainflow records ("over 404 drives" → "over 405"). The arrays now **match** the master, not just
its stamp.

**B4 — cohort-rate paired-eligibility exposed; every rate states its paired n/km (`seasonal_core.py`,
`cohort_arrays.py`, new `test_cohort_rates.py`).** The paired-eligibility mask (a null/NaN/≤0-distance numerator
never adds its exposure to the denominator) was already present in `cohort_per_100km`; M291 (a) factors it into one
definition (`_pair_eligible`) and adds `cohort_per_100km_detail` returning `{value, paired_n, paired_km}` so the
denominator behind every displayed rate is auditable; (b) fixes `cohort_hourly_rate`, which still summed
numerator and denominator over different drives (a missing event count could donate its hours); (c) fixes the
`starts_per_100km` events path in `cohort_arrays.py` that coerced a missing count to 0 (`e or 0`) — it now stays
`None` and is excluded cleanly; (d) exposes `paired_n`/`paired_km` on every rate metric in `cohort_arrays.json`
(EfficChart paired_n=396 / 8230.5 km matches EnergyIntensity; starts paired_n=398). New `test_cohort_rates.py`
is the roadmap's named "every rate exposes paired n/km" contract (8 assertions incl. the audit's null-numerator
5-vs-10 example); the existing `test_track4.py` test 2 also guards it.

**B6 — single authoritative distance; seasonal ↔ master divergence removed (`compute_seasonal.py`,
`seasonal_drive_master.csv`).** `compute_seasonal.py` already *sourced* `distance_km` from `drive_master.csv`
(the single distance function), so the −2.5 vs 0.44 divergence (2.94 km on the totals) was pure staleness: the
committed seasonal master predated the M289 repair. Reconciled the one divergent cell (−2.5 → 0.44; seasonal total
now **8437.74 km**, equal to the master) and added a post-build **invariant** to `compute_seasonal.py` that fails
the build if the seasonal master's total distance ever differs from the primary master's over the same canonical
drives — so this can never silently recur.

**B7 — cold cohort null-with-reason everywhere (`summary_arrays.json`, `release_check.py`).** Of 49 seasonal charts
only `EfficiencyBands` still carried a **label-only** cold cohort (`[{label:"Urban"}, …]` — zero-as-real, though
the `cohortNoData` guard already blocked it from rendering). Set `data.cold = null`, converted the empty shoulder
drive-type classes to explicit `{n:0, status:"insufficient_support"}`, and added `coldStatus` + `emptyClassPolicy`
to the chart. A new `release_check.py` payload assertion fails the release if any chart ships a non-null list of
label-only cold entries.

**B8 — record-object disclosure contract; the `sane_max` silent drop ends (new `records_disclosure.py`,
`xtrail_summary.jsx`, `release_check.py`, `test_track4.py`).** `_records()`'s `sane_max(col, cap)` dropped
above-cap values with no disclosure; on this corpus exactly one record was affected — **"Peak engine load"**
reported 211.0 % while silently excluding **10 drives up to 1712.5 %** (OBD Absolute Load PID artefacts). New
`records_disclosure.py` (a standalone, idempotent post-pass in the `records_*.py` style) attaches a machine-readable
`disclosure` to every record — `eligibilityRule`, `excludedByCap`, and, when any were excluded, the raw pre-cap
`rawExtremum` — and stamps the new `recordsContract` key (M235 gate). The records tab (`xtrail_summary.jsx`) now
renders the exclusion inline (with a `data-record-disclosure` DOM hook); `release_check.py` asserts the contract on
every record; `test_track4.py` gains a contract assertion (and its record drift-guards now compare builder-owned
fields, since `disclosure` is a separate, separately-tested layer).

**B3 — test path parameterisation: already resolved (audit stale).** The named `test_cohort_p0.py` is not in the
project; `project_paths.py` (single source of truth) plus the `XT_RAW`/`XT_MASTER`/`XT_CODE` / `XT_WORK` convention
were applied project-wide at M285, and every present test (`test_schema_contract`, `test_track4`,
`master_refit_audit`, …) already reads env-overridable paths. No hard-coded `/mnt/project` remains in a present test.
Verified, no change required.

**Verification (all green).**
- `node build_html.js` — JSX contract intact; provenance 410==410; **M220.2 stamp gate green, 136 stamped keys**
  (registry + `recordsContract`) all match the live master; `wrote xtrail_dashboard.html`.
- `node validate_jsdom.js` — **9 tabs, 0 console errors, 0 semantic warnings**; registry 15/15 DOM rows;
  current-integral 396 ≤ 399 (reflects the corrected corpus); 36 CI whiskers; cohort selector cold disabled (n=0).
- `python3 test_track4.py` — **19/19** (test 1 confirms EnergyIntensity == independent paired ratio-of-sums with

- `python3 test_cohort_rates.py` — **8/8** paired-basis contract.
- `release_check.payload_checks()` — registry PASS, glossary PASS, **B7 cold-null PASS, B8 disclosure PASS**;
  the ThermalFuelPenalty malformed-date tokens remain a **disclosed soft WARN** (needs a raw fuel-subset regen of

**Trigger.** Independent deep project audit dated 22 Sep 2026 (`xtrail_epower_deep_project_audit_2026-09-22.pdf`).
This entry (a) records and **resolves a critical release-integrity defect the audit did not catch**, (b) reconciles
the audit against the *live* committed payload (several P0 items are already resolved and the audit is stale on them),
(c) fixes a real P0-1-class source bug, (d) canonicalises the orphaned GTR glossary, and (e) makes the release gate
assert rendered content instead of a source marker. **The corpus is unchanged** — no `drive_master.csv` bytes or
corpus MD5 change; all edits are corpus-invariant (display/CI/gate-logic only). The full front-end gate chain now
builds and validates **green** end-to-end.

**0. RESOLVED — committed master ↔ arrays MD5 desync (release did not build as committed).**
*Defect.* The committed `drive_master.csv` MD5 is **e077cc83…** (the M289 corrected master), but every one of the
135 `_artifactStamps[*].corpusHash` in the *committed* `summary_arrays.json` — and `masterRefitAudit.publishedMasterMD5`
— was **cbc206a8…**. `build_html.js`'s M220.2 artifact-stamp gate re-hashes the live master (e077cc83) and finds it
≠ the stamped cbc206a8 on all 135 keys → **BUILD ABORTED**, blocking any green release.
*Root cause (verified 2026-09-22).* The two masters are NOT the same data re-serialised. Recomputing the
master-derived headline from e077cc83 gives **396** paired-eligible drives / EnergyIntensity **17.10218**, vs the
committed arrays' **395** / **17.098072**. The single differing drive is **`20260906_122920`** — the M289 P0-2
odometer-reset repair (`distance_reset_repaired=True`, `distance_endpoint_raw_km=−2.5` → `distance_km=0.44` via
`trip_meter`). So the committed `summary_arrays.json` **pre-dated the M289 distance fix** (395/17.098) while the
committed `drive_master.csv` was **post-fix** (396/17.102) — a partial-commit desync. **Re-stamping was therefore
correctly ruled out** (it would ship pre-fix values under a post-fix stamp; a false-green).
*Resolution.* The correct **M289 e077cc83-stamped `summary_arrays.json`** (produced by M289's own from-raws
`build_summary_arrays` run) was recovered and re-verified here: all 135 `_artifactStamps[*].corpusHash` = live master
**e077cc8365c0fe3142192be4f2939ab5**, every `corpusHashSource` prefixed `file:`, `masterRefitAudit` consistent. The
corpus-invariant `assumptionsRegistry` (15 typed entries) and `cohortMeta` blocks were spliced forward and the
glossary canonicalised (item 2) on top of this synced payload. **The desync is closed by commit-hygiene** — the
correct e077cc83 arrays are the ones to commit; the older cbc206a8 copy was committed by mistake.

**1. Audit reconciliation (audit is STALE vs the live payload on several P0 items).** Verified directly against the
committed `summary_arrays.json` (SHA-256-identical to the audit's payload per the audit's own doc-control):
- `assumptionsRegistry` **is present** — 15 typed entries, 14 unverified (audit §8 "the latest payload contains no
  assumptionsRegistry" is stale). The registry render is now gate-asserted at the DOM level (item 4).
- **P0-1 done** — `socHysteresisV2.nDays = 90`, `recomputeMode='fresh'`, `nDrivesCovered=410` (M286).
- **Cold cohort correct** — `seasonalCharts.charts.{EnergyIntensity,StartsPer100km}.data.cold = null`,
  `status='unavailable'`, `cohortCounts.cold = 0`.
- §4b reframe / glossary live-values / false-optimistic ML claim / CI-ESS / StartsPer100km eligibility were all
  landed M285–M288 and are present.

**2. FIX — GTR glossary canonicalised (was stale AND orphaned; audit-confirmed live defect).** `generatorTractionRecon.glossary`
still showed `f_gen 0.602`, `η_eng 0.36`, `η tank→bus 0.334`, `Battery-buffer share 0.398`, contradicting
`generatorTractionRecon.corpus` (`fGen 0.488`, `etaEng 0.358`, `etaBus 0.331`; buffer = 1−fGen = 0.512). The committed
`xtrail_summary.jsx` renders `R.glossary` **directly** (no `glossLive` override was committed — the M288 glossary
patch shipped as a download only), so the dashboard displayed the stale 0.602, contradicting every other §4b figure;
no script rebuilds `glossary` (`refresh_gtr_headline.py` refreshes corpus/flows but never glossary), so it had
drifted since M265. **Fixed** by canonicalising the glossary rows in the payload to corpus values
(f_gen 0.602→0.488, buffer 0.398→0.512, η_eng 0.36→0.358, η tank→bus 0.334→0.331). Because the JSX binds to
`R.glossary`, the payload edit alone corrects the display — **verified**: the built dashboard now shows 0.488 / 0.512
/ 0.358 / 0.331 and no stale glossary row survives (residual `0.602`/`0.398` string hits in the HTML are data-array
values and this entry's own provenance note, not glossary rows). No source binding change needed.

**3. FIX — day-key source bug (`compute_summary_arrays.py`; P0-1-class, ThermalFuelPenalty).** `dateSpan[0]='2026-09-'`
and methodology `'2026--0-9- to …'` came from `str(fn)[:8]` used as a day key over dash-format filenames
(`2026-09-10 …`[:8] = `2026-09-`). This also **collapsed distinct days into one key**, undercounting independent
days and thereby **narrowing the day-clustered bootstrap CIs (false-optimistic)** — not merely cosmetic. Added
`_day_key(fn)` (regex `(\d{4})\D?(\d{2})\D?(\d{2})` → `YYYY-MM-DD`), mirroring the M286 `m119v2_model.py` fix, and
replaced the two `str(fn)[:8]` day keys in the fuel/thermal passes (`_thermal_fuel_penalty` and the sibling
continuous-covariate pass). Verified: `py_compile` OK; unit test over both filename formats passes; 3 distinct
dash-days now yield 3 day keys (was 1). This corrects both the malformed dates and the day-clustered CIs **on the next
raw-pass rebuild** of the ThermalFuelPenalty chart. The malformed date tokens remain in the *current* payload
(they require re-deriving the chart from the raw fuel subset) and are **disclosed as a soft release warning** (item 4),
not silently shipped.

**4. FIX — release gate made authoritative (`release_check.py`, `validate_jsdom.js`; audit "False-green release risk", P0).**
The old check `"assumptions registry marker present": "data-assumptions-registry" in html` was a **false-green**:
`build_html.js` inlines the transpiled JSX component source into a `<script>`, so the marker string is in the built
HTML whether or not any rows render (the component returns null at runtime when the payload is empty). Replaced with:
- `release_check.py`: a payload **schema** assertion (15 typed entries, each with the fields the table renders), plus
  two data-integrity assertions — GTR glossary must match `corpus`, and no malformed ISO date tokens (the latter as a
  disclosed **soft warning**, not a hard fail, since it clears only on a raw-pass regen). Verified against the final
  synced payload: registry **PASS**, glossary **PASS** (was FAIL on the cbc206a8 payload — catches 0.602/0.398), dates
  **WARN** (surfaces `2026-09-`, `2026--0-9-` as disclosed-pending). `py_compile` OK.
- `validate_jsdom.js`: a rendered-**DOM** assertion that the assumptions-registry `<tbody>` renders exactly `nEntries`
  rows across the tab sweep (fails if the payload declares entries but 0 rows render).

**Verification done (end-to-end green).**
- `node build_html.js` → **all gates pass**: JSX component-contract intact; provenance gate (410==410, MC nominal
  1407.6 kWh match); **M220.2 artifact-stamp gate green** — live master `e077cc8365c0fe3142192be4f2939ab5`, 135 stamped
  keys all match. `wrote xtrail_dashboard.html (2370 KB)`. (`soc_patterns.json` is absent in this session → the
  SoC-patterns section is hidden by design; it is unchanged in Project Knowledge.)
- `node validate_jsdom.js` → **VALIDATION PASSED — 9 tabs, 0 console errors, 0 semantic warnings**: determinism proof
  current (nDrives=410); current-integral metric-valid (396 ≤ 399); **assumptions registry rendered 15/15 rows in DOM**
  (proves the false-green fix); 36 CI whiskers across Compare views; cohort selector 5 modes with cold disabled (n=0).
- `release_check.payload_checks()` on the final payload: registry PASS, glossary PASS, dates WARN (disclosed).
- Also: `py_compile` (compute_summary_arrays.py, release_check.py); `node --check` (build_html.js, validate_jsdom.js);
  `_day_key` unit test.

**Still open / queued (needs the 410 raw CSVs + full pipeline; corpus-invariant when done).**
Regenerate `seasonalCharts.charts.ThermalFuelPenalty` with `_day_key` — this clears the malformed `dateSpan`/methodology
tokens **and** widens the (currently day-collapsed) bootstrap CIs. The source fix is committed; only the chart re-derivation

Not covered here (unchanged open items): raw CSV → `drive_master.csv` clean-room rebuild; ML16 determinism harness.

**Delivered as downloads** (source/gate files a maintainer commits; data files replace the mis-committed copies):

## M288 (2026-09-20): Audit P0-3 §4b — architecture-wording fixes, conservation-residual disclosure, glossary live-binding (JSX)

**Trigger.** Audit Appendix-A A03/A04/A14 and P0-7 (§4b glossary): the §4b Generator→Traction section carried a
physics error, two over-strong claims, and a stale glossary internally contradicting its own corrected flows.
All fixed in `xtrail_summary.jsx` and validated by building + jsdom-rendering the dashboard.

**1. High-Speed "Mechanism" paragraph (A03/A04/A14).** Corrected literal prose: aerodynamic drag *force* ∝ v²
and *power* ∝ v³ (was "drag rises with roughly the cube of speed"); "over a sufficiently long energy-neutral
interval… instantaneous generation need not equal instantaneous demand" (was "the generator must supply the
motor's entire power demand in real time"); "no sustained saturation signature detected under the defined
load/current gate… where the generator would actually bind remains unobserved" (was "always ample headroom /
never below ~140 km/h").

**2. Conservation-residual disclosure (M287 §2C / §6).** New cohort-aware "Conservation check" callout below the
Sankey, computed live from the flow fields already in the block: traction gross closes (8.89 + 9.34 = 18.23);
claimed generator outputs (gen→traction 8.89 + gen→battery 7.77 = 16.66) over-identify the modeled generator
input (15.75) by **+0.91 kWh/100 km (5.8 %)**, disclosed explicitly with the generator→battery arm labelled a
model bound (not an identifiable path; no generator-power PID is logged); buffer in−out **+1.34** shown, not
silently balanced. Arithmetically self-consistent across cohorts (all +0.91/5.8 %, warm +0.83/5.3 %, shoulder
+1.90/11.9 %).

**3. Glossary live-binding (P0-7 / A14).** The three dynamic glossary rows (plus η_eng) now render from the live
`C.corpus` object (`glossLive` helper) → **0.488 / 0.512 / 0.331**, eliminating the stale pre-M265
0.602 / 0.398 / 0.334 that contradicted every other figure in the section. Static rows fall through unchanged.

**Verification.** Built exactly as `build_html.js` does (Babel preset-react, React UMD inlined) against the
shipped data bundle, rendered in jsdom: **9/9 tabs, 0 console errors**; all three corrected wordings present, all
three original claims absent; glossary renders 0.488/0.512/0.331; `JSX_COMPONENT_CONTRACT` markers intact
(GeneratorTractionRecon, RTFlowSchematic, conserved cascade, ◆ Key findings, ⚠ Limitations, RTFlowSchematic F={F}).

**Known limitations.** Optional presentation polish deferred: restyling the audit table into M287's explicit

**Trigger.** External deep audit (20 Sep 2026). P0-1: the `fn[:8]` day-key in `m119v2._corpus_tables` collapses
the 43 dash-format drives, undercounting distinct days (85 vs 90). P0-2: the distance endpoint method returns a
negative value on a terminal odometer reset (drive `20260906_122920`: −2.5 km).

**1. P0-1 source fix (`m119v2_model.py`).** Added `_day_key(fn)` (regex `(\d{4})\D?(\d{2})\D?(\d{2})` →
`YYYY-MM-DD`) replacing `fn[:8]` in `_corpus_tables`; distinct days **85 → 90**. Verified localized to
`m119v2`.

410 raws with the day-key fix (~1000 s). **nDays 85 → 90.** Overwrote only the day-clustered CV/bootstrap leaves
(`ladder` start+stop all rungs; `sensitivity.start`/`.stop`; `sensitivity.rollingOrigin`). Verified byte-identical
to shipped on all day-independent fields (nStartEvents 5210, nStopEvents 5199, nStart/StopAtRisk, `surfaces`,
`partialDependence`, `predictorAges`, `detectorReconciliation`). Effect small (start fiveVarDur logLoss
0.070421→0.070487, prAuc 0.0578→0.0575; CIs shift on the 90-block resample) — a refinement of uncertainty
quantification, not a change to conclusions.

**3. P0-2 source fix (`compute_drive_summary_v6.py::_v5_analyze_bytes`).** Guarded the distance block: on a
negative odometer-endpoint difference, fall back to trip-meter (`d_trip`) then monotonic (`d_mono`), and record
provenance columns `distance_source` (`odo_endpoint` / `trip_meter` / `odo_monotonic`),
`distance_reset_repaired`, `distance_endpoint_raw_km`. The reset drive: **−2.5 → 0.44 km** (`trip_meter`).

`distance_source` added), MD5 e077cc83…. masterRefitAudit (M289) confirms 0 numeric value drift vs a clean raw→
master rebuild.

`M286_audit_P0-1_P0-2.patch.md`, `CHANGELOG_M286.md`, `DRIVE_MASTER_DIFF.md`.

- **Section 9 — remaining Compare-KPI intervals + violin view (M285d; `kpi_ci3_extract.py`, `kpi_ci3_splice.py` new; `compute_summary_arrays.py`, `xtrail_summary.jsx`, `validate_jsdom.js`).**
  *(a) Intervals.* One pass over the 410 raw logs (`kpi_ci3_extract.py`, ~seconds via `raw_cache`) stores per-drive event/sample tallies with calendar-day ids;
  `kpi_ci3_splice.py` then writes additive intervals for Warm/Shoulder/All, **asserting that every recomputed point equals the shipped one first** (any
  mismatch aborts with nothing written; 24 intervals written, 0 mismatches). Medians (EnergyShifting net kW at 5-15 km/h, loaded spread, relaxation half-time):
  percentile bootstrap of the median resampling calendar days (seed 42, 4000 draws, same algorithm as the blocks' own `dayboot`). Shares (boost involvement, HighSocRegen
  engine-on / non-decelerating): ratio-of-sums, day clusters, `kpi_ci.day_cluster_ci` (seed 20260919, 4000 draws, Kish ESS). Values (95 %, days): net kW
  All 1.66 [1.55, 1.76] (86), Warm 1.73 [1.62, 1.79] (84), Shoulder 1.16 [1.06, 1.42] (19); loaded spread All 11.0 [10.5, 11.5] mV (77), Shoulder 11.75 [10.25, 12.5] (16);
  HighSoc engine-on share All 67.6 [65.9, 69.1] % (86), Shoulder 62.1 [59.3, 66.2] (19); non-decelerating All 61.7 [59.8, 63.3], Shoulder 58.4 [55.2, 62.1];
  boost involvement (see (b)) All 61.0 [51.6, 67.7] (86), Warm 61.6 [51.4, 68.6], Shoulder 52.7 [0.0, 70.0] (19 days; the interval is wide because Shoulder rests on 296 boost-observable events).
  **Scope limits.** Relaxation half-time is a median of a quantised quantity (1 s steps): All/Warm 1.0 [1.0, 1.0], Shoulder 0.0 [0.0, 1.5] — zero-width is a resolution limit, not precision.
  Day-level resampling addresses between-day dependence only; it does not model within-day/route autocorrelation or the Warm/Shoulder route-mix confound.
  *(b) ESTIMAND CORRECTION — boost involvement (value revision).* Wiring the interval exposed a denominator bias in `_handoff_sequence`: boost onset can only be detected when the event window
  carries a boost channel, but the denominator counted all handoffs. 915 of 5379 events (17 %; concentrated in the Shoulder cohort on Jul 23-24) have no boost channel and were counted as
  "no boost", biasing `boostInvolvementPct` low. Generator patched (`boostObservable` per event; new fields `nBoostObservable`, `boostInvolvementObservablePct`); the legacy field is retained unchanged
  for continuity and disclosed. Corrected estimand: All 61.0 % (was 50.7 %), n = 4464 observable; Warm 61.6 % (4168); Shoulder 52.7 % (296). The Compare KPI and caption now show the observable-denominator value;
  earlier statements of ~51 % boost involvement are superseded. Modal-ordering statistics in the same block are likewise sensitive to channel availability (not re-derived here). Other handoff fields verified to show no drift.
  *(c) Violin view (`CmpViolinPanel`, Compare tab, below the ECDF panel).* Gaussian KDE of the per-drive `cohortDistributions` (energy intensity, engine-on share, EV distance share, regen share of charge);
  Silverman bandwidth h = 0.9·min(sd, IQR/1.34)·n^(-1/5) per cohort (printed under each panel), density truncated at each cohort's observed min/max, y-axis clipped at pooled p99 (count stated), one shared density scale
  per metric, median tick + IQR bar + per-drive ticks, cohorts with n < 8 drawn as points only, Cold (n = 0) not drawn. Caveat rendered in the panel: shape depends on bandwidth; no significance test implied.
  *(d) Gates.* Validator: whisker expectation 22 → 36 (all render) plus violin assertions (panel present, KDE polygons drawn); `release_check.py` PASSED 19/19 (post-step no-op, cohort arrays byte-identical),
  0 console errors; visual check in Chromium. `seasonalCharts` stamp note extended (M285d). The M219 stale-count sentence was fixed in M285c.

## M283 (2026-09-17): Sustained CHARGE peaks — M273 deferral CLOSED via the per-sample artifact gate; lost-code generator restored (external audit Section 10)

**Trigger.** The M273 honest deferral: sustained rolling-window CHARGE peaks were
withheld because an unfiltered raw pass surfaces physically-impossible >1000 A
charge spikes on a handful of drives (logging artifacts). A defensible figure
needs the pipeline's per-sample artifact gate wired before logging peaks —
mirroring the sustained-DISCHARGE treatment shipped at M273. Also: the
`sustained_current_peaks.csv` artifact had NO surviving generating code (same
lost-code failure class the M279–M282 track was created to end).

**Root cause of the artifacts + the gate.** The main pipeline
(`compute_drive_summary_v6._v5_analyze_bytes`) gates the current series
per-sample at `|I| < 900 A` (line ~539) before it computes `peak_I_charge`; that
is why the single-sample charge record already reads 213 A, not 1050 A. The old
`sustained_current_peaks.csv` charge columns were computed WITHOUT that gate
(discharge was unaffected — no discharge sample approaches 900 A — so the M273
discharge record was correct regardless). The 9 artifact drives each carry only
1–4 samples ≥900 A; the gate removes those samples, not the drives.

**Method (`sustained_current_peaks.py`, stored).** For the 396 current-carrying
drives (master `peak_I_discharge` notna): load `[BMS] HV Battery Current (A)`,
apply the `|I|<900 A` per-sample gate, discharge-positive `Id=-I_raw`, then
`resample('1s').mean().interpolate().rolling(N,min_periods=N).mean().max()` for
N∈{1,5,10,30}. `interpolate()` (NOT `ffill`) is the shipped fill — it uniquely
reproduces the M273 discharge 5 s setter 173.4 A on the ~2 Hz drive
20260705_122016 (ffill gives 175.3). C-rate = A / cap_ah, cap_ah = CAP_KWH·1000/
v_nom per drive (CAP_KWH = 2.1 kWh, UNVERIFIED — label carried on the record).
HARD GATE: the script aborts unless the discharge corpus maxima reproduce the
shipped M273 record 205.1/173.4/145.1/82.7 A byte-exact (nan-safe) — proving the
method faithful before any charge figure is trusted; it does.

**Result — sustained CHARGE peaks (gated).** 213.0 A (1 s, 36.4C) → 194.6 A (5 s,
33.5C) → 167.2 A (10 s, 28.8C) → 137.0 A (30 s, 23.5C). The 1 s peak equals the
master single-sample record (213 A, Jun19 D3); 5/10 s set on Aug30, 30 s on Jun13.
Physical finding: the pack SUSTAINS charge markedly better than discharge — 30 s
charge holds 64% of its 1 s peak (137 A/23.5C) vs discharge's 40% (83 A/14C) —
consistent with charge being fed by steady regen/generator-surplus banking rather
than the brief launch transients that set the discharge peaks. Robustness: the
1/5/10 s peaks are set by densely-sampled drives and are identical under
interpolate/ffill; the artifact gate is uncritical (no real gated sample lies in
(213, 900) A — the artifact cluster at ~1050 A is cleanly separated), and the 9
artifact drives' true gated charge peaks are all ≤188 A and set no record — a
direct vindication of the audit's "single-sample maxima are often artifacts" point.

**Change.** (1) `records`: new row "Peak charge current — sustained (rolling
1/5/10/30 s)" inserted after "Peak charge current" (40 → 41; count is data-bound
via `S.records.length`); the single-sample "Peak charge current" note has its
"…artifact gating; pending" deferral replaced by a cross-link to the new record +
the gate disclosure. `_artifactStamps.records.generatedAt` bumped (content
changed; corpusHash unchanged — corpus untouched). No JSX edit — the records
renderer is generic and data-bound. (2) `sustained_current_peaks.csv` regenerated
by the stored script with ONE consistent gated method for both sides: discharge
corpus maxima byte-identical to the shipped record (20 non-record sparse-drive
cells differ ≤25 A from the old artifact, a fill-method difference immaterial to
any record); charge columns now gated (corpus maxima 1050→213 etc.).

**Validation.** Isolation diff: only `records` (1 row added, 1 note edited) and
`_artifactStamps.records.generatedAt` changed; no shared record mutated except the
intended charge note; no out-of-scope leaf. Build: 132/132 stamps match live
corpus hash `04cc3f…`; only the two pre-existing WARNs. jsdom: 9/9 tabs, 97
buttons, 0 console errors, COHORT-OK, 1 expected `socHysteresisV2` WARN. Render:
new metric + all four A/C-rate strings in the data blob; old "…gating; pending"
prose out; new de-staled charge note in. Generator's discharge reproduction gate
passes byte-exact.

**Scope.** Closes the M273 sustained-CHARGE deferral and Section 10's "artifact-
gated sustained CHARGE peaks" remainder. Generating code stored
(`sustained_current_peaks.py`, `splice_charge_sustained.py`), ending the
`sustained_current_peaks.csv` lost-code exposure. Section 10 still open:
temperature-maxima persistence / quality-window / sensor-agreement enrichment;
pack-resistance-proxy excitation gating + CI/covariate disclosure. Other pending
(unchanged): overlap-weighted seasonal model, package hygiene + assumptions
registry, Limitation 1 fuel-coverage literal "145/374"→181/410.

## M282 (2026-09-17): §4b simultaneity REBUILT at the corrected sign — inverts the urban/highway narrative; reframed away from "saturation" per §4a (GTR sub-analysis restoration, COMPLETE)

**Trigger.** Last of the four §4b sub-analyses left behind by the M265 sign fix.
`simultaneity` (per-second engine-on classification by simultaneous generator/
battery state, 4 states × 4 drive types) had been null since M253 — no surviving
source, honestly omitted.

**Method.** `simultaneity_gtr.py`: for every engine-on second (Pgen_t>0) on the
fuel-instrumented drives, classify by the DC-bus balance from
`recon_engine.central_estimate_v2_persample` (the M255 per-sample form, carrying
the M265 sign) into four mutually-exclusive states — gen+battery-discharge /
charges+drives / gen-alone-neutral / fully-banked — duration-weighted per drive
type. Validated three ways (no surviving numbers to reproduce): (1) per-drive
persample→aggregate energy identity exact (0.00 kWh); (2) the four states
partition 100% of engine-on time; (3) the split is robust across a 3×3 threshold
sweep (eps_trac, eps_batt ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 1.0} kW).

**Result — the corrected sign INVERTS the M246 narrative.**
| type | n | gen+batt-dis | charges+drives | gen-alone | fully-banked |
|------|---|------|------|------|------|
| urban         | 154 | 18.4 | 52.8 | 3.6  | 25.2 |
| mixed         |   9 | 25.5 | 57.0 | 3.8  | 13.8 |
| mixed_highway |   5 | 42.9 | 44.2 | 4.7  |  8.2 |
| highway       |   2 | 46.3 | 36.1 | 11.8 |  5.8 |

The shipped table read urban as 79.5% "saturated" (battery-assisting); the
corrected sign shows urban engine-on time is predominantly battery-CHARGING
(charges+drives 52.8% + fully-banked 25.2% = 78%, ≈ the old 79.5% relabelled).
gen+battery-discharge rises monotonically urban 18.4% → highway 46.3% — the
physically correct behaviour of a fixed-point generator: it banks surplus at low
urban demand and is drawn on at high highway demand. It reconciles with the
drive-type f_gen split once engine-off EV driving (excluded here) is accounted
for, and the highway gen+battery-discharge now coincides with §4a's 80-120 km/h
regime.

**Reframed away from "saturation" (per §4a; Andrii's call).** §4a's M41/M42
decomposition establishes that the high-speed engine-on discharge is NOT generator
saturation: the engine holds ~38% load (headroom it is not commanded to use), the
discharge probability rises with SoC (controller under-generating to steer SoC
toward ~62%), and discharge seconds carry negative mean acceleration — a true-
saturation gate almost never fires. The rebuilt section therefore drops the
"saturation" label: the gen+battery-discharge state is described neutrally (the
battery supplies the instantaneous demand/generation gap), the interpretation
paragraph is rewritten to the corrected pattern and cites §4a's SoC-steering
finding, and the basis note records the sign inversion. The buffer thesis is
unchanged and strengthened — bidirectional buffering (bank surplus / supply gap) —
but the high-speed draw is a controller-shaped gap, not a maxed-out generator.

**Change.** `generatorTractionRecon.simultaneity`: null → 4 rows (7 fields each).
JSX: gen+battery-discharge state definition (drop "generator saturation");
interpretation paragraph (rewritten, corrected pattern + §4a); basis note (M246-
vintage → corrected-sign rebuild M282). Limitation 6 rewritten (rebuilt, no longer
omitted; notes the inversion + §4a). `_provenance` + artifact-stamp note
(corpusHash unchanged). The null→array flip makes the JSX render the table branch
instead of the "temporarily unavailable" box.

**Validation.** Isolation diff: 32 leaves — the simultaneity array (4×7 + the key),
`limitations[5]`, `_provenance`, artifact note — all within `generatorTractionRecon`
+ `_artifactStamps`. Build: 132/132 stamps match live corpus hash `04cc3f…`; only
the two pre-existing WARNs. jsdom: 9/9 tabs, 97 buttons, 0 console errors, COHORT-OK,
1 expected `socHysteresisV2` WARN. Render: corrected table + prose in; old inverted
prose (minority-mode / saturated / M246-vintage / 79.5% urban) out; the data-bound
table renders (else-branch "unavailable" box now dead code).

**Scope — GTR SUB-ANALYSIS REBUILD TRACK COMPLETE.** All four §4b sub-analyses left
stale or lost by the M265 sign fix are now current: `sensitivity` (M279, recomputed),
`crossval` (M280, verified sign-invariant), `rpmFinding` (M281, refreshed to 410 +
true band), `simultaneity` (M282, rebuilt + reframed). Generating code stored for
each (sensitivity_gtr.py, crossval_gtr.py, rpm_opt_pass.py, simultaneity_gtr.py).

fuel-coverage literal "145/374 drives" (now 181/410).

## M281 (2026-09-17): §4b rpmFinding refreshed to 410 drives + corrected to the TRUE [1850,2150] OPT-band occupancy (GTR sub-analysis restoration, cont.)

**Trigger.** Continuing the GTR sub-analysis rebuild after M279 (sensitivity) and
M280 (crossval). `rpmFinding` was disclosed-stale at 374/369 drives. It is NOT
battery-sign-dependent (an engine-RPM occupancy statistic), so this is a basis
refresh — but investigating it surfaced a latent label/value mismatch.

**Findings.**
- `rpmDistribution` is already current at 410 (coverage.nDrives 410, stamp hash
  live), but its display bin edges (1614-1975, 1975-2025, 2025-2100, 2100-2400)
  straddle the OPT band [1850,2150], so the exact band fraction is not extractable
  from them.
- The shipped `empiricalPct` (58.5%) equals the single 1975-2025 spike bin /
  engine-on (58.7% at 410) — i.e. it was labelled "[1850,2150]" but valued only
  the band's central 2000-rpm spike, understating the OPT concentration.
- True [1850,2150] occupancy at 410 = **63.4%** of engine-on time (engine-on =
  rpm≥300, 1 Hz grid), anchored to the stamped `rpmDistribution` bin totals with
  the two OPT-boundary bins split at 1850/2150 via a raw 1 Hz sub-bin pass.
  Independent pure-raw cross-check: 64.4% (within 1 pp).

**Method.** `rpm_opt_pass.py` replicates `compute_summary_arrays._RawAccum`'s exact
1 Hz gridding (`resample('1s').mean().ffill(limit=15)`, `np.histogram`) over all
410 drives with fine edges (1850/2150 inserted). The pure-raw pass reproduces the
stored histogram's total engine-on time to 0.4% and the dominant spike bin to 2%,
but low-density valley bins diverge 10-25% (a raw-cache normalization detail), so
`empiricalPct` is ANCHORED to the stamped bin totals and uses the raw pass only for
the two OPT-boundary sub-bin shares (40.4% of the 1614-1975 bin lies in [1850,1975];
18% of 2100-2400 lies in [2100,2150]) — robust to the absolute-level differences
because only within-bin ratios are used.

**Change.**
- `rpmFinding`: empiricalPct 58.5→63.4, empiricalN 274216→284260 (engine-on
  seconds), empiricalDrives 369→397, corpusWideDrives 374→410. optLo/optHi
  (1850/2150), empiricalLoad, nissanClaimPct unchanged.
- JSX prose accuracy: "classifying N real engine-on samples from D high-cadence
  drives — X% … falls in exactly that cell" → "across D drives (N engine-on seconds
  on the 1 Hz grid), X% … falls in that band". The "high-cadence" descriptor was
  stale (now 397/410 drives, not a high-cadence subset); "exactly that cell" wrongly
  implied a single histogram bin.
- Fixed two stale RPM-basis references left by earlier milestones: the M280
  key-findings caveat ("current at 374 drives, refreshed M253" → data-bound
  "{corpusWideDrives} drives, refreshed M281") and Limitation 5 ("374 drives,
  refreshed M253" → "410 drives, refreshed M281"). Binding the caveat's count
  removes it from the hardcoded-literal WARN so it cannot rot again.
- `_provenance` + artifact-stamp note updated (corpusHash unchanged).

**Validation.** Isolation diff: 7 leaves — the 4 rpmFinding values, `limitations[4]`,
`_provenance`, artifact note — all within `generatorTractionRecon` + `_artifactStamps`.
Build: 132/132 stamps match live corpus hash `04cc3f…`; only the two pre-existing
WARNs (the hardcoded-literal WARN now one item shorter). jsdom: 9/9 tabs, 97 buttons,
0 console errors, COHORT-OK, 1 expected `socHysteresisV2` WARN. Render: rpmFinding
data blob updated; new prose in, stale prose (high-cadence / exactly-that-cell /
refreshed M253) out; 58.5% now appears only in the non-rendered provenance that
documents the correction.

**Scope / remaining.** Closes `rpmFinding` in the GTR-sub-analysis-rebuild track;

## M271 (2026-09-17): Records — false "longest sustained" corrected to a true gap-aware run length (external audit Section 10)

**Trigger.** Audit Section 10 flagged the record "Longest sustained 130+ km/h
discharge = 143 s" as a false claim: the underlying field
`highspeed_discharge_s_130p` (compute_drive_summary_v6.py:812) is a CUMULATIVE
sum of every qualifying-sample dt across the whole drive, not a contiguous run.
Its label ("longest continuous stretch") therefore overstated a ~19 s reality
by ~7.5×.

**Gap-aware run-length computation (faithful to the pipeline).** Instrumented
`_v5_analyze_bytes` at the exact point the cumulative is computed — same
per-sample frame `e`, same masks (speed ≥130, engine on via eng_rpm>400, Id>0
discharge-positive) — to also emit `highspeed_discharge_longest_run_s_130p`:
the maximal block of consecutive 1 Hz samples all qualifying, duration = summed
dt within the block (dt capped at DT_CAP so timeline gaps do not inflate it).
Run over the 26 drives with any 130+ discharge.

**Result (validated against the audit).** True corpus-max contiguous run
**19.2 s on Jul14 D4**. On the cumulative-max drive (Jul26 D2, 142.6 s exposure)
the longest continuous run is **16.7 s** — matching the audit's independent raw
replay exactly, confirming the method. The buffer subsidises the generator for
at most ~19 s continuously before the SoC floor forces a speed-or-recharge
compromise, not 143 s.

**Correction applied.** The mislabelled record is replaced by
"Longest 130+ km/h engine-on discharge — contiguous run" (19.2 s, Jul14 D4),
and the cumulative figure is retained as a separate, correctly-labelled record
"Cumulative 130+ km/h engine-on discharge exposure" (142.6 s, Jul26 D2) — both
of the audit's options, so no information is lost. Records grid 38 → 39; the
grid count is data-bound (`S.records.length`), no literal to touch.

**Provenance note.** `drive_master.csv` is NOT modified here — adding the new
column would change the corpus MD5 (04cc3f…) and void all 132 artifact stamps.
The record is corrected in `summary_arrays.json` from the faithfully-recomputed
value; the pipeline instrumentation carries
`highspeed_discharge_longest_run_s_130p` so the column populates on the next
full master rebuild.

**Validation.** Metric-level record diff: exactly one false record removed, two
correctly-labelled records added; no pre-existing record value changed. Build
passed every gate (132/132 stamps match live corpus hash 04cc3f…). jsdom: 9/9
tabs, 0 console errors.

**Section 10 remaining (labelling/context, estimated).** The other record-quality
items — C-rate "show amperes first + 1/5/10/30 s sustained peaks", "211% engine
load" PID relabelling, manifold-boost co-timed barometric, temperature-maxima

"~9 °C fixed probe gradient" observed-distribution rewrite — are per-record

## M268 (2026-09-17): Release-provenance manifest — serialization-invariant content hash + honest byte-vs-content claim (external audit BLOCK #2)

**Trigger.** Audit BLOCK #2: the release asserted raw-byte SHA-256 verification,
but the audit's supplied bundle matched only 98/421 raw-byte SHA-256 while all
421 row counts matched — a transfer re-serialization, not a data difference.

**Empirical finding.** Against the actual study archive, the manifest still
matches **410/410 canonical raw-byte SHA-256** — the mismatch was an artifact of
the audit *package* being a re-encoded subset. So the byte claim was true within
the archive but *incomplete*: it gave a reviewer no way to verify data identity
after a transfer that re-encodes the CSVs (BOM, CRLF, trailing whitespace).

**Root-cause fix — serialization-invariant content hash.** `corpus_manifest.py`
now computes, per canonical file, a `normHash`: SHA-256 over a canonicalised view
(UTF-8 BOM stripped, CRLF/CR → LF, per-line trailing whitespace removed, trailing
blank lines dropped), plus a corpus-level `contentHash` = SHA-256 over the sorted
canonical `normHash`es (parallel to the raw-byte `corpusHash`). `raw_manifest.json`
regenerated against the shipped bundle: byte `corpusHash` unchanged
(`44c098d6…`, confirming currency), new `contentHash` `e5066e29…`, 410/410
canonical carry `normHash`.

**Proven behaviour.** On a canonical file re-serialized with BOM + CRLF +
trailing blank line: raw-byte SHA-256 **differs** (reproducing the audit's
symptom) while `normHash` **matches** (data identity preserved); and `normHash`
still **detects** a real single-cell value change. So a reviewer whose copied
bundle fails the byte hash can recompute the content hash to confirm the data is
identical — the verification path BLOCK #2 was missing.

**Dashboard.** `rawManifest` summary gains `corpusByteHash` + `corpusContentHash`
(+ note). The two provenance paragraphs (§ methodology "byte-verified" claim and
the F-02/F-19 corpus-manifest note) rewritten to state both fingerprints and to
explain the audit's row-match / byte-mismatch as a transfer re-serialization,
rather than implying a reviewer can byte-verify a transferred bundle.

**Deliberate non-change.** No hard build-fail gate on manifest *presence* was
added: `build_html.js` already stamps `rawManifestError` as a soft disclosure
when the archive is absent, and a hard fail would break legitimate dev builds
run without the 1 Hz raw corpus. Byte-identity to the *original OEM-tool export*
remains permanently unrecoverable (F-02) — but that is now moot for verification,
since the content hash is transfer-robust against the published bundle.

**Validation.** Isolation diff vs the M265 baseline: only `seasonalCharts`,
`records[36]/[37]`, `rawManifest`, `_artifactStamps` changed across M266+M268.
Build passed every gate (131/131 stamps match live corpus hash 04cc3f…). jsdom:
**9/9 tabs, 0 console errors**, 1 pre-existing disclosed warning (socHysteresisV2).

**Scope.** Closes audit BLOCK #2. Audit items now closed: BLOCK #1 (M265),
FIX #3 (M266), FIX #4 (M267), BLOCK #2 (M268). Remaining: Energy Architecture
source-label rework, Records run-length correction, and the REWORK/REVIEW set.

## M267 (2026-09-17): Compare-mode WarmupCurve axis bug + index-based category joins (external audit FIX #4)

**Trigger.** Audit FIX #4 flagged two concrete Compare-mode defects in
`xtrail_summary.jsx`. Both are rendering-layer only (no data/pipeline change).

**Defect 1 — WarmupCurve plotted distance as temperature.** The Compare spec
(`COMPARE_SPECS.WarmupCurve`) mapped `y: d => d.grid` and
`xlabels: d => d.grid.map((_,i)=>String(i))`. But `warmupCurve.grid` is the
DISTANCE axis (km: 0, 0.25, … 8.0), and the coolant temperatures live in
`classes.<type>.points[].med`. So the overlay drew the distance values (0–8) on
the °C axis with bare indices for x — a meaningless line. Fixed: `xlabels` = the
grid km values; `y` = per-cohort pooled coolant temperature at each grid km
(n-weighted mean of the per-class median at that km). Verified against the live
data: the pooled "all" curve is a clean monotone **34 → 83 °C** over 0–8 km,
approaching the ~80 °C operating band. Chart title corrected to
"Coolant warm-up curve (°C vs distance, km)".

**Defect 2 — Compare bar charts joined categories by array index.** `CmpBars`
took `ref` = the first non-empty cohort's category list and paired every other
cohort's category at the SAME ARRAY INDEX (`p.cats[ci]`). When cohorts differ in
category membership or order (e.g. one cohort missing a drive-type), the bars
mismatched — a value from one category rendered under another category's label,
and categories absent from the first cohort were dropped entirely. Fixed: the
reference axis is now the ordered UNION of category labels across all selected
cohorts (first-seen order, so an "All" series defines canonical order), and each
cohort's value is looked up BY LABEL, not index. This is a general fix — it
corrects every `kind:"bars"` Compare chart at once.

**Validation.** JSX-only change (summary_arrays.json untouched). Build passed
every gate (131/131 artifact-stamps match live corpus hash 04cc3f…). jsdom:
**9/9 tabs, 97 buttons, Compare toggles exercised across all 5 modes, 0 console
errors**. Corrected logic confirmed present in the built artifact
(`Math.abs(pt.km…`, `d.classes`, label-join `cc.label`, union `seen.has`).

**Scope.** Closes audit FIX #4. Audit items now closed: BLOCK #1 (M265),
FIX #3 (M266), FIX #4 (M267). Remaining: release-provenance manifest (BLOCK #2),
Energy Architecture source-label rework, Records run-length correction, and the
REWORK/REVIEW set.

## M265 (2026-09-17): Battery-current sign reversal in the §4b generator→traction reconstruction — CONFIRMED, corrected, and rebuilt from raw (external audit BLOCK #1)

**Trigger.** An external deep project audit (17 Sep 2026) flagged a
current-sign error in `recon_engine.py` as a release-blocking defect
invalidating the §4b generator→traction section. Andrii approved acting on it.

**Verification (against live code, corpus M264/410 drives).** Confirmed
directly. `recon_engine.py:39` computed `Pbatt = +V·(I_raw − offset)/1000` and
labelled it "+discharge". The main pipeline defines discharge-positive as
`P = −I_raw·V/1000` (`compute_drive_summary_v6.py:1317,1534`, "M11: BMS current
is charge-positive"). The M13 SoC-anchored offset is itself estimated in the
discharge-positive frame (`net_draw_corr = net_draw − I_off·V·h`,
compute_drive_summary_v6.py:108–130,1020–1055), so the correct per-sample
expression is `Id,adj = −I_raw − I_off`. Only the `I_raw` term was mis-signed;
the offset term (`− offset_A`) was already correct.

**Why the prior "verified" claim missed it.** The M248 "verified reproducible"
status was byte-exact *self*-reproduction of `fuel_recon_master.csv` — that
cannot catch a convention error. Worse, `recon_engine` rescales the per-sample
discharge/charge shapes to the master's authoritative `gross_discharge_kwh`/
`gross_charge_kwh` totals (`Pbatt_anch = dis·kd − chg·kc`), which preserved
aggregate battery energy while swapping the *temporal phase* of discharge vs
charge — the exact quantity the generator→traction allocation depends on. The
headline therefore looked internally reconciled while being physically inverted.

**Fix.** One line in `recon_engine.py:load_drive()`:
`g['Iadj']=g['I']-offset_A` → `g['Iadj']=-g['I']-offset_A` (documented inline).

**Rebuild (from raw, current 410-drive corpus).** `fuel_recon.py --all`
re-run against the corrected engine. This also caught that the released
`fuel_recon_master.csv` was itself stale at 145 rows (M248/367-drive basis) —
the corpus grew to 410 (M264) without a GTR re-run. Corrected master: **181
fuel-instrumented / 180 clean drives / 1701.0 km.**

**Corrected corpus headline vs released, and vs the audit's independent prediction:**

| Metric (per 100 km) | Released sign | Corrected | Audit predicted |
|---|---|---|---|
| f_gen | 0.595 | **0.488** | 0.602 → 0.498 |
| generator→traction | 14.21 | **8.89** | 14.15 → 8.97 |
| traction gross | 23.89 | **18.23** | 23.49 → 18.01 |
| battery→traction | 9.68 | **9.34** | 9.34 → 9.04 |
| generator electrical | 15.78 | **15.75** | ~unchanged |
| urban f_gen | 0.549 | **0.384** | 0.557 → 0.399 |
| highway f_gen | 0.803 | **0.802** | ~unchanged |

Independently reproduces the audit's direction and magnitude. Generator
electrical is fuel-derived and barely moves; traction gross collapses because
the battery-discharge phase was inflating it; highway is near-invariant because
sustained generator operation dominates that thin two-drive stratum.

**Downstream refreshed from the corrected source (same session):**
- Corpus + Warm/Shoulder GTR splits in `summary_arrays.json`
  (`generatorTractionRecon`, `seasonalCharts.charts.GeneratorTractionRecon`),
  reusing `wire_gtr_seasonal.aggregate()` verbatim. Warm f_gen 0.504,
  Shoulder 0.295 (shoulder is 63/64 urban → route-confounded, as the audit notes).
- `speedSplit` rebuilt via `speed_split.py` (corrected `central_estimate_v2_persample`),
  self-validated 181/181 drives at 0.0000 kWh/100km diff. The reversed sign had
  produced a physically impossible f_gen 0.535 at a 0–20 km/h crawl; corrected
  gives a clean monotone **0.161 (0–20) → 0.344 → 0.616 → 0.861 (90–120) →
  0.848 (120+)** — battery buffer supplies ~84% of low-speed traction, generator
  saturates above 90 km/h.
- §4b prose corrected: the "clear majority is generator-coincident" key-finding
  (false at f_gen 0.49) rewritten to "roughly half, strongly duty-dependent";
  the drive-type caption (which claimed the generator contribution shrinks
  urban→highway — it *grows*, 7.3→14.5, while the battery collapses 11.68→3.59)
  rewritten as a split-inversion; stale Sankey code comment updated.
- `generatorTractionRecon` artifact stamp updated to `computed` (was
  `carriedForward`), with an M265 provenance note.

**Interpretation.** The "battery is a power buffer" thesis SURVIVES and, in
urban/mixed driving, STRENGTHENS: the buffer now supplies the majority of
traction at low/moderate speed, with the generator becoming the dominant
instantaneous source only in sustained high-speed cruise. The specific
"generator supplies the majority" framing is retired.

**Validation.** Isolation diff clean (only `generatorTractionRecon`,
`seasonalCharts`, `_artifactStamps`). Build passed every gate (component
contract, provenance, 131/131 artifact-stamps match live corpus hash
04cc3f…). jsdom: **9/9 tabs, 97 buttons, 0 console errors**, 1 pre-existing
semantic warning (socHysteresisV2 stale, unrelated).

**Scope / still open.** This closes audit BLOCK #1 (the sign error) only. Not
addressed here: release-provenance manifest (BLOCK #2), temperature-sidecar /
chart_registry / cohortCounts regeneration to 410 (FIX #3), Compare-mode
key-joins + WarmupCurve mapping (FIX #4), Energy Architecture source-label
rework, Records run-length correction, and the remaining REWORK/REVIEW items.
The §4b conceptual limitations the audit raises (min-allocation naming,
dual-charge source bounds, BSFC floor) are unchanged by the sign fix and remain
as disclosed limitations.

**Trigger.** Andrii asked to investigate the one chart M262 left stale
rather than guess at.

**The eligibility rule was hiding in the schema history, not the formula.**
`n_sign_crossings` (the proxy column `StartsPer100km` is built on) was added
to `drive_master.csv` at M241 (2026-09-08), per that entry's own note:
"computed by `analyze_bytes` since M229 but deliberately held out of the
master pending the next full ingestion." M262's two failed attempts
(`n_sign_crossings` notna + `distance_km>0`, and adding `sign_check=='ok'`)
both over-filtered. The actual rule is simpler than either: `nPool` = the
whole corpus at build time (not a filtered subset — 374 then, 410 now,
matching exactly), `nEligible` = rows where `n_sign_crossings` is non-null,
full stop. No distance or sign-check gate at all.

**Verification, same standard as everything else in this arc.** The stale
entry's `nPool=374 / nEligible=362` (374−362=12 excluded) reproduces exactly
on the live corpus: `nPool=410 / nEligible=398` (410−398=12 excluded) — the
**same 12 drives** both times (all pre-M257-batch, mostly the May 11-15
earliest files plus two August ones; confirmed by listing the null rows
directly, not inferred). This is a stronger corroboration than a formula
match alone would be — an exact count match across a corpus that grew by 36
drives, none of which happen to be null on this column, is not something a
wrong rule would produce by coincidence.

**Computed and spliced** via ratio-of-sums (`estimator:
events_ratio_of_sums`, this project's standard per-100km convention) over
the 398/341/57 eligible rows for all/warm/shoulder: **911.94 / 896.41 /
1232.59 starts-proxy/100km.** Shoulder running well above Warm is
physically consistent with the rest of this study's cold-adjacent findings
(more, shorter trips; more buffer-impulse engine cycling relative to
distance covered) — not treated as confirmatory on its own, since this is
explicitly a proxy metric (current-sign crossings, not real engine-start
detection), but not a red flag either.

**Confidence level, stated plainly.** Like `EnergyIntensity` (M262), this
has no top-level `S.*` twin to byte-verify against — it is genuinely only
constructed for the cohort system. The exact-count corroboration above is
strong but is not the same class of proof as the 48 byte-exact matches
elsewhere in this arc. `seasonalCharts._staleness.reconstructedNotByteVerified`
now lists both `EnergyIntensity` and `StartsPer100km` so a future session
knows exactly which 2 of 50 entries carry this caveat and which 48 don't.

**`_staleness` block closed out.** `carriedForward` flipped to `false`,
`basisNDrives` now `410` (matches `liveNDrives`), `stillStale` is empty,
`refreshed2026_09_17` lists all 50 chart keys. This is the natural end state
of the disclosure mechanism M260 introduced — it now says "nothing is
stale" because nothing is, not because the field was removed.

**Verification chain.** Direct diff of `seasonalCharts.charts` against the
pristine pre-M260 `summary_arrays.json`: **all 50 entries changed** — zero
remain byte-identical to the 374-drive-basis version, closing the arc
started at M260's audit. Isolation diff at the top level: still exactly the
same 4 keys touched across the whole M260-M263 arc
(`_artifactStamps`, `generatorTractionRecon`, `records`, `seasonalCharts`).
`drive_master.csv` / `seasonal_drive_master.csv` / `fuel_recon_master.csv`
byte-identical throughout. `build_html.js`: JSX contract gate clean,
artifact-stamp gate green (131/131). `validate_jsdom.js`: 9/9 tabs, 97
buttons, 0 console errors, cohort selector verified across all 5 modes, 1
pre-existing unrelated semantic warning (`socHysteresisV2`, disclosed since
M260, still the standing M258/M259 CHANGELOG-vs-disk desync). `xtrail_
dashboard.html` rebuilt (2,469 KB).

**Files changed:** `summary_arrays.json`, `xtrail_dashboard.html`.

**Arc summary (M260→M263, all 2026-09-17).** Started from Andrii flagging

## M262 (2026-09-17): Seasonal-data recompute completed — 49 of `seasonalCharts`'s
50 chart entries now refreshed to the 410-drive basis; 1 left honestly stale
rather than guessed

**Trigger.** Andrii asked to continue M261's partial recompute through to
completion: "all charts should be fully refreshed."

**Method, continued from M261.** Same discipline throughout — call the
still-present generating function on the full 410-drive corpus, verify its
output byte-exact against the fresh non-cohort top-level `S.*` baseline (or
the nearest available anchor) before trusting a Warm/Shoulder cohort split,
then splice. 16 more raw-pass functions were run this session:

- Single-function (11): AccelDecelEnvelopes, RpmSpeedSync, EngineStartContext,
  BufferDebtRecovery, DepartureArrival, EngineStateMachine, HandoffSequence,
  CellSpreadRelaxation, VgtAirPath, EnergyShifting — plus SocLevelSensitivityChart
  (master-level, `_soc_level_sensitivity(dm, cfg)`, verified against the fresh
  top-level `dodSocLevelSensitivity`).
- Composite, two functions merged each (3): CrawlStopGo (`_crawl_stop_go` +
  `_crawl_stop_go_two_part`), HighSocRegen (`_high_soc_regen` +
  `_high_soc_regen_covariates`), ThermalFuelPenalty (`_thermal_fuel_penalty` +
  `_thermal_fuel_penalty_continuous`). `_crawl_stop_go` and
  `_thermal_fuel_penalty` alone each cost ~150-260s per cohort, so these three
  needed their two halves computed and pickle-checkpointed in separate calls
  per cohort (part1 → save → part2 → merge → verify) rather than one shot, to
  stay inside the sandbox's per-call time limit.
- CohortExposure needed no function call at all — it IS the per-cohort
  coverage summary (n_drives/km/independent_days/date_range/ambient_range_c),
  values already cross-validated in M260 against the independently-computed
  `seasonal_arrays.json.cohorts.*.coverage`.

**Two real bugs found and fixed mid-session, not just timing hiccups.**
1. My hand-written `frame_loader` returned the raw `'time'` column as a
   string; the production one (`drive_raw_cache.py`'s `make_frame_loader`)
   pre-parses it to `datetime64`. Harmless for functions that re-parse `time`
   themselves (most do), but `_engine_start_context` → `_engine_start_triggers`
   compares `Timestamp >= str` directly and crashed. Fixed `loaders.py` to
   replicate `drive_raw_cache.add_file()`'s exact parse (fast-path
   `%H:%M:%S.%f`, fallback `format='mixed'`) — matches the real pipeline,
   not a workaround.
2. `_rpm_speed_sync`'s output contains an integer-keyed dict
   (`leadLagExploratory.lagCounts`); comparing it directly against the
   JSON-loaded (string-keyed) top-level value read as a false mismatch.
   Normalizing both sides through a JSON round-trip before comparing
   resolved it and confirmed a real match — every subsequent comparison in
   this session used the same normalization.

**EnergyIntensity — reconstructed with high but not byte-exact confidence,
disclosed as such.** No top-level `S.*` equivalent exists to verify against.
Reconstructed via the ratio-of-sums `gross_throughput_kwh`/`distance_km`
formula this project already documents as its own established per-100km
convention (`SEASONAL_CHANGELOG.md`), restricted to drives with non-null
`gross_throughput_kwh`. Corroborating signal: the stale entry's `n=360` (on
the 374-drive basis) matches `n=396` at the live 410-drive basis under this
exact exclusion rule (360+36=396, the 36 new M257 drives all have the
column) — strongly suggesting this is the actual original method, but it is
not a byte-exact proof the way the other 48 are, so it's flagged separately
in `_staleness.reconstructedNotByteVerified` rather than folded in as
equally certain.

**StartsPer100km — left honestly stale, not guessed.** Also has no
top-level anchor. Tried reproducing its disclosed `nEligible=362 /
nPool=374` (374-basis) via `n_sign_crossings` + `distance_km>0` (gives
397-of-410, not the expected ~397-ish-scaled pattern) and again adding
`sign_check=='ok'` (389-of-410) — neither reproduced the stale count with
the same confidence EnergyIntensity's exact 360→396 match gave. Rather than
ship a plausible-looking number resting on a guessed exclusion rule, this
one stays disclosed-stale at the 374-drive basis. Its own entry already
states it is a proxy metric anyway ("authoritative engine-start count is
raw-derived engineStartsByType, Phase 2" — which M261 already refreshed).

## M256 (2026-09-14): Compare mode — sticky series filter + per-chart cohort overlays, incl. the C/E/R multi-chart sections

Built out the previously-placeholder "Compare" season mode into a working
per-chart cohort comparison. Prior behaviour: selecting Compare showed a static
Warm/Shoulder/Cold summary table with the note "per-cohort chart overlays land
in a later pass." Presentation-only JSX revision — no data, pipeline, or corpus
change (drive_master.csv untouched, MD5 6adbce59bdddb5ceff5d58975b4a5dc8).

**1. Sticky series-filter bar (`CompareControls`).** Rendered once below the
season selector, position:sticky top:38 so it stays on screen while scrolling.
Four toggles in the requested order — All Data / Cold / Warm / Shoulder. Cold is
disabled (0 sub-5°C drives in the corpus). "All Data" is a true select-all /
aggregate control with the requested coupling: on by default, and disabling any
cohort clears it (a partial comparison no longer matches the blended corpus
total). Clicking All when both cohorts are on toggles just the aggregate overlay;
clicking it while partial re-selects everything; all-off shows an explicit
empty-state. Selection lives in a new module-level `CompareCtx` provided from
`App` via `cmpSel`/`cmpToggle` (the invariant is enforced in the setter). The bar
keeps `data-cohort-compare` so the existing jsdom cohort assertion still passes,
and it disappears on leaving Compare.

**2. Per-chart best-fit overlays (`CompareBlock` + `COMPARE_SPECS`).** In Compare
mode each cohort-aware component early-returns a `<CompareBlock id=.../>`,
co-located with the existing cold guard (identical hook-order profile, so no
Rules-of-Hooks regression — verified by the jsdom cohort-toggle sweep). A
registry maps each chart id to one of three renderers, all reading the same
`S.seasonalCharts.charts[id].data[mode]` payload the single-cohort views use:
- `CmpBars` — grouped horizontal bars, median value labels + faint lo–hi range
  whiskers (SoC bands, efficiency/cycle/starts bands, drive-type mix, speed/
  turbo/terrain distributions, SoC-by-speed, RPM-band occupancy, …).
- `CmpLines` — one polyline per active cohort (warm-up curve, pack-temp vs
  minutes, cruise torque vs speed, RPM distribution, regen capture vs speed).
- `CmpKpi` — metric × series table with Δ-vs-All deltas (energy accounting,
  generator→traction, thermal lag/fuel penalty, buffer-debt, handoff, etc.).
Fixed series colours (All #1e293b, Warm #e0803a, Shoulder #c9b23a) with a
per-chart legend give the clear visual distinction requested.

**3. Multi-chart sections C / E / R.** These three sections carry an internal
view toggle with several sub-charts; the initial pass only compared the first.
A `CompareMulti({ids})` stacker now renders a `CompareBlock` for every sub-chart:
- C (Cycle Rate): CycleByType + CycleBySpeed.
- E (Engine ON/OFF Cycling): EngineStartsByType + EngineOnDuration + EngineOnBySpeed.
- R (Regenerative Energy Analysis): RegenCaptureMeasured + RegenByTempMeasured +
  RegenByType + RegenByZone.
Six new COMPARE_SPECS added for the previously-unspecced sub-charts.

Validation: build_html.js gates pass (component-contract intact; 131 artifact
stamps match the live corpus hash); validate_jsdom.js 9/9 tabs, 0 console errors,
1 pre-existing disclosed warning (socHysteresisV2, 320 vs 374). Dedicated DOM
tests confirm the toggle invariant, the empty-state, that bars/lines/KPI frames
render real cohort values across tabs, and that all nine C/E/R sub-charts render.
Caveat carried in the UI: Shoulder rests on 48 drives (fewer on the fuel/turbo-
instrumented subsets), so several overlays place a small-n cohort beside a large

  threading `corpus={R.corpus}` into the component explicitly
  (`RTFlowSchematic({ F, corpus })`) instead of guessing at `F`'s shape.
- **Layout bug, independent of the above.** The Tier-2 sub-label y-position

  the Tier-1 "gen/PE loss" end-label collided with the Generator column's own
  eta line (both landed at y≈88-90 near the same x), and the 440-unit
  viewBox was too narrow for the (fixed) generator sub-label text, causing
  right-edge overflow. Fixed by: widening the viewBox 440→520; increasing

  "gen/PE loss" as a third line under the Generator column instead of a
  diagonal callout; and deriving the legend y-position and viewBox height
  from the actual content instead of hardcoded constants, so the layout

  before/after headless-Chrome screenshots, then confirmed in the actual

**3. "Traction supply split by vehicle speed" rebuilt.** Its generating code
was lost with no surviving source (disclosed since M253 as `null` with a
"temporarily unavailable" notice). Rebuilt by reusing — not reimplementing —
`recon_engine.py`'s already-verified per-drive reconstruction machinery:
added `central_estimate_v2_persample()` (recon_engine.py), a byte-identical
copy of the trusted `central_estimate_v2()` aggregate formula that
additionally exposes the per-second `Ptrac`/`Pgen_t`/`Pbatt_anch`/`dt`
arrays instead of only their drive-level sums. New script `speed_split.py`
loads every fuel-instrumented drive at 1 Hz, bins each qualifying sample by
instantaneous vehicle speed into the bins the original (lost) analysis's
JSX prose already references (`0-20`,`20-60`,`60-90`,`90-120`,`120+`
km/h), and sums generator-coincident / battery-to-traction energy and
distance-covered per bin (kWh/100 km of distance covered *in that bin*,
f_gen as ratio-of-sums — same conventions as item 2). **Validation is
mandatory and built into the script**: before any binned output is trusted,
it sums the per-sample arrays the same way `central_estimate_v2()` does
internally and asserts the result reproduces `fuel_recon_master.csv`'s own
shipped per-drive figures to <0.01 kWh/100 km — passed 145/145 drives, max
observed diff 0.0000. (First validation attempt caught two real bugs before
any output was trusted — see items 3a/3b below — rather than silently
shipping a subtly-wrong reconstruction.)

- **3a. Offset-handling bug found by the validator, not assumed.** Two
  drives (`20260813_145651.csv`, `20260813_150341.csv`) have a NaN
  `I_offset_A_applied`. `fuel_recon.py`'s own offset resolution —
  `float(master[f].get('I_offset_A_applied', 0.0) or 0.0)` — does NOT
  substitute for NaN (`x or default` only replaces falsy values; NaN is
  truthy), so the NaN passes through unchanged, propagates through
  `Iadj`→`Pbatt` (all-NaN for the whole drive), which
  `central_estimate_v2`'s `np.nan_to_num()` then silently zeroes — the net,
  probably-unintended effect being the battery term is fully suppressed for
  any drive with a missing calibrated offset. `speed_split.py`'s first draft
  used a more intuitive `.fillna(0.0)`, which validation immediately flagged
  as a 2-drive mismatch (traction_gross vs. shipped, ~19 kWh/100km off on
  one drive). Rather than "fix" `fuel_recon.py`'s quirk (out of scope, and
  `fuel_recon_master.csv` is the study's verified-reproducible ground
  truth), `speed_split.py` replicates the exact original idiom so its output
  matches the already-shipped, independently-verified figures byte-for-byte
  on these drives too. Flagged as a latent quirk in `fuel_recon.py` worth a
  deliberate decision later (silent full-drive battery suppression on a
  missing offset seems more like an accident of the `or` idiom than an
  intended fallback), not touched this session.
- **3b. Validation-coverage bug found and fixed before item 5 below was even
  discovered.** The validator's `n_check` originally capped at a fixed 138,
  silently skipping any target file sorting after that point in
  `dm['file']` order — which turned out to be exactly where the newly
  discovered missing drives (item 5) sorted. Fixed to validate every target,
  not a fixed prefix.

Final speed-binned result (374-corpus / 145 fuel-instrumented drives, post
item-5 refresh): generator stays comparatively flat (16.14 → 13.54 → 13.87 →
15.87 → 19.98 kWh/100km across the five bins) while battery collapses with
speed (14.03 → 13.03 → 7.98 → 2.97 → 5.95); f_gen rises from near-parity in
the two lowest bins (54%, 51%) to 64% (60-90) to 84% (90-120) — the same
qualitative pattern the surviving JSX prose already described from the lost
original analysis (near-parity of the two lowest bins as a binning artefact,
not a physical plateau; sharp f_gen rise above 60 km/h), which is
independent corroboration that this rebuild reproduces the original
analysis's shape, not an artifact of this session's own method. 120+ bin
remains thin (n=11 drives, 16.5 km) — flagged as indicative, matching the
pre-existing prose caveat.
