**6. Two new Dataset Extremes rows: "Battery temp min" (11°C, May15 D1) and
"Battery intake air temperature min" (9.0°C, May14 D1).** `drive_master.csv`

## M254 (2026-09-13): systematic season/temperature cohort-wiring sweep

Full audit of every chart-rendering component in `xtrail_summary.jsx` for
`useCohort()`/`cohortOr()` usage, triggered by two user-reported gaps
(Battery Draw Spectrum, Coolant/Oil Warm-Up & Thermal Lag) that turned out
not to be isolated. 16 components had the Season toggle rendered around
them with no effect on their own data. All 16 wired this session.

Per component: root-cause data source identified (master-column
aggregation vs. raw per-second pass), the relevant pipeline builder
function(s) re-run per cohort by direct import rather than reimplemented,
and the **"all"-cohort output verified byte-exact** against the
pre-existing corpus-wide value before wiring into the JSX. Where a
function is called more than once per drive (e.g. a headline pass plus a
covariates/two-part extension), raw-frame parsing and the shared
intermediate grid/event extraction were memoized (by filename, or by
grid identity + call arguments where a function is invoked with varying
parameters — see the `_crawl_stop_go` note below) so a cohort re-pass over
an overlapping drive set reuses prior work instead of re-parsing. Typical
"all"-cohort raw pass: 40–235 s depending on column count and grid size;
warm/shoulder passes then complete in 1–8 s off the cache.

Wired, with the pipeline function reused verbatim in each case:

- **`BatteryDrawSpectrum`** (Battery Draw Spectrum) — master-level only
  (`gross_discharge_kwh`/100 km, `ens_outlier_v2`-clean, by drive type).
  Cohort filter applied directly to `drive_master.csv` +
  `seasonal_drive_master.csv` (`thermal_regime`); no pipeline function
  needed re-running since the aggregation is a simple groupby.
- **`ThermalWarmupLag`** (Coolant/Oil Warm-Up & Thermal Lag) — raw pass,
  `_thermal_warmup_lag()`.
- **`EnergyPath`** (§4 e-POWER Architecture measured energy accounting) —
  master-level, `_energy_path()`. `S.evTraction` reference in the same
  component also re-pointed at cohort data once `EvTraction` (below) was
  wired.
- **`ThermalFuelPenalty`** (Cold-Start Thermal Fuel Penalty) — raw pass,
  `_thermal_fuel_penalty()` + `_thermal_fuel_penalty_continuous()`. First
  "all" byte-match attempt failed; traced to a missed continuous-model
  merge step (the live pipeline calls both functions and merges the
  second into the first's dict) — fixed, then matched exactly.
- **`EvTraction`** (Pure-Electric Traction) — master-level,
  `_ev_traction()`.
- **`HighSocRegen`** (High-SoC Regen Reduction) — raw pass,
  `_high_soc_regen()` + `_high_soc_regen_covariates()`. First attempt
  OOM-killed loading full unrestricted raw frames for all 374 files;
  fixed by restricting to the 9 columns the grid function actually reads
  (`_hr_grid`'s column map plus `_apply_speed_priority`'s two speed
  channels).
- **`BufferDebtRecovery`** — raw pass, `_buffer_debt_recovery()` (reuses
  `_buffer_impulse_events()`/`_bdr_grid()` internally; both memoized by
  grid identity to avoid the pipeline's own documented double-call per
  drive).
- **`HandoffSequence`** — raw pass, `_handoff_sequence()` (reuses
  `_engine_start_triggers()`/`_hs_grid()`, memoized).
- **`EngineStartContext`** — raw pass, `_engine_start_context()` (reuses
  `_engine_start_triggers()`/`_isc_grid()`, memoized).
- **`CellSpreadRelaxation`** — raw pass, `_cell_spread_relaxation()`.
- **`DepartureArrival`** — raw pass, `_departure_arrival()` (reuses
  `_engine_start_triggers()`, memoized).
- **`RpmSpeedSync`** — raw pass, `_rpm_speed_sync()` (`_rsync_grid`
  memoized by filename).
- **`EnergyShifting`** — raw pass, `_energy_shifting()` (`_esh_grid`
  memoized by filename).
- **`VgtAirPath`** — raw pass, `_vgt_airpath()` (`_vgt_drive` memoized by
  filename; naturally fast — only 121/374 files carry real VGT-A
  variation).
- **`EngineStateMachine`** — raw pass, `_engine_state_machine()`
  (`_esm_grid` memoized by filename).
- **`AccelDecelEnvelopes`** — raw pass, `_accel_decel_envelopes()`
  (`_ade_grid` memoized by filename).
- **`CrawlStopGo`** — raw pass, `_crawl_stop_go()` +
  `_crawl_stop_go_two_part()`. First caching attempt memoized the shared
  `_csg_events()` extraction by grid identity alone; since the
  threshold-sensitivity sweep calls it with several different
  `stop_v`/`stopgo_ceil` values against the *same* grid, this silently
  collapsed all four sensitivity rows onto one repeated value — caught by
  the "all"-match check (three fields differed from the pre-existing
  value), fixed by keying the cache on `(grid identity, args, kwargs)`

Explicitly reviewed and left unwired (not gaps):

## M253 (2026-09-13): §4b Generator→Traction restored (third occurrence); dashboard bug fixes; REQUIRED_BLOCKS gate extended to close the gap that let this recur

**§4b has now been lost and restored three times**, and this milestone's
first job is naming that pattern honestly rather than treating this as an
isolated fix:

1. M250 (2026-09-11): a JSX component-contract regression — the
   `GeneratorTractionRecon()` function body reverted to its pre-M249 form
   while the *data* stayed current. M251 restored it and added the JSX
   component-contract gate specifically to catch a body-level revert.
2. Sometime after M252 (2026-09-12, `generatorTractionRecon` confirmed
   present at its M248 data basis) and before this session started
   (`generatorTractionRecon` confirmed **absent**), a session with no
   surviving CHANGELOG entry, no surviving generating script, and no
   record of what else it touched ran a seasonal-wiring pass that
   produced the current `seasonalCharts` structure (`_meta.phase:
   "0B_seed+1_master+2_raw+wire14"`, `generatedAt: 2026-09-12T18:39:03Z`
   — same day as M252, after it) and dropped the `generatorTractionRecon`
   **key** from `summary_arrays.json` entirely. This time the JSX
   component body was untouched (M251's gate correctly reported "1
   protected component(s) intact" throughout) — the failure mode was
   data-side, not component-side, so the gate built for the first
   failure mode didn't catch the second.
3. This session (found via the user's original 9-item findings list,
   item 9: "§4b section is fully missing") — restored again, detailed
   below.

**Root cause of why #2 shipped silently.** `build_html.js`'s
`REQUIRED_BLOCKS` gate exists precisely to abort a build when a
dashboard-bound key goes missing from `summary_arrays.json`, and already
listed nearly every raw-pass block in the pipeline (`crawlStopGo`,
`thermalWarmupLag`, `handoffSequence`, etc.) — but `generatorTractionRecon`
was never added to that list, so its disappearance produced zero build
errors and zero console errors; the section simply rendered `null` (by
design — `GeneratorTractionRecon()` has a defensive `if (!R) return
null`) and vanished with no diagnostic anywhere.

**Fix — added `generatorTractionRecon` to `REQUIRED_BLOCKS`
(`build_html.js`).** Negative-tested against the exact M253 failure mode:
stripped the key from a copy of the current `summary_arrays.json`, ran
the build, confirmed `BUILD ABORTED — summary_arrays.json is missing
required blocks: generatorTractionRecon`; restored the key, confirmed a
clean build. This closes the specific gap that let the second loss ship
undetected — a future session dropping this key (or any of the ~30 other
now-listed blocks) will fail loudly at build time instead of shipping a
silently blank section.

**Fix — §4b data restored.**
- Headline corpus/flows/drive-type-split figures freshly recomputed from
  `fuel_recon_master.csv` (135 clean / 138 fuel-instrumented drives,
  1,391.2 km) using the documented ratio-of-sums method; reproduces the
  last-recorded M248 figures to the decimal (generator 15.92, traction
  gross 23.876, f_gen 0.602, η_eng 0.360, η_bus 0.334, urban f_gen 0.556
  n=123).
- `rpmFinding` freshly recomputed from the current 374-drive
  `rpmDistribution` (OPT band 1850–2150 rpm per `model_constants.py`,
  58.5% of engine-on time, 369 drives) rather than carried forward stale.
- `crossval` (Pearson r=0.997, n=82) and `sensitivity` (9-axis table)
  carried forward from their last-surviving source files (`crossval.csv`,
  `sensitivity.json`) at the disclosed M246 fuel-subset basis — no
  generating script for either survived between sessions.
- `simultaneity` and `speedSplit` (the per-second engine-state and
  speed-bin sub-analyses) had **no surviving source of any kind** — not
  even a stale file. Rather than fabricate replacement numbers, both are
  set to `null` and the JSX now renders an explicit "temporarily
  unavailable, pending rebuilt classification code" notice in their place
  instead of the numbers.
- `regimeTable` (BSFC-by-RPM-band) rebuilt directly from
  `model_constants.py`'s live constants (not re-derived, not guessed).
- `glossary`, `audit`, `limitations`, `sources` written fresh —
  explanatory scaffolding, not measured quantities, so safe to compose
  without a surviving prior version.
- Provenance note in the section discloses this restoration explicitly,
  including that the whole-corpus production cross-check that used to sit
  here was *not* re-derived this session and is omitted rather than shown
  as a false agreement with the headline figure.
- New `_artifactStamps` entry added for `generatorTractionRecon`
  (`corpusHash` matching the live `drive_master.csv` MD5) — required by
  the build's own M220.2 stamp gate.
- Additive splice only: 134→135 top-level keys, only
  `generatorTractionRecon` added.

**Other fixes, same session:**
- Drive Type Distribution donut rendering blank for single-100%-category
  cohorts (Shoulder, currently all-urban). Root cause: `Donut`'s `seg()`
  helper draws a full circle as one 360° SVG arc when a category hits
  exactly 100%; the arc's start and end points then differ only by
  ~1e-14 (float noise from `cos`/`sin` of `a0` vs. `a0+2π`), which most
  browsers' rasterizers treat as a zero-length arc and silently don't
  draw. Fix: sweep clamped to `2π − 1e-4` (a gap of ~0.005°, invisible at
  any zoom) whenever it would otherwise reach a full turn.
- Battery Thermal Pattern chart's intake-air trace appearing to dip below
  the x-axis at drive-start for the Shoulder cohort (user-reported with
  an annotated screenshot). Root cause: `yMin` was hardcoded at 22 °C —
  sized for the "all"/"warm" corpus floor — while `yMax` was derived from
  the data; Shoulder's intake-air start (19.6 °C) fell below that fixed
  floor and rendered off the bottom of the plot, at the x=0 gridline.
  Fix: `yMin` now derives from the same per-cohort data `yMax` does
  (floored to the nearest 5, never rising above the original 22 °C), so
  All/Warm render identically to before. Y-axis gridline start updated to
  match.
- Season toggle (`CohortSelector`) made `position: sticky`.
- `RegenChart`'s four internal views (by battery temperature,
  capture-vs-speed, drive-type source, speed zone) wired to the season
  cohort selector — the per-cohort data already existed
  (`RegenByTempMeasured`, `RegenCaptureMeasured`, `RegenByType`/Meta,
  `RegenByZone`) but the component never consumed it, so the whole
  Regenerative Energy Analysis section was unaffected by the Season
  toggle despite regen being the single most temperature-sensitive
  phenomenon in the study.

**Standing note (carried forward from M251, still true, now doubly
so).** The recurring failure isn't a specific bug so much as a class:
*data outlives the session that produced it, but the record of how it was
produced does not.* Three sub-analyses lost across this history
(`generatorTractionRecon.simultaneity`/`speedSplit` this session;
`crossval`/`sensitivity`'s generating code before M246; the earlier
`mc_corpus.json`/`energy_flows_per100km.json` chain) all follow the same
shape — the JSON artifact survives in Project Knowledge, the Python that
made it does not. `REQUIRED_BLOCKS` now catches a *dropped key*; it has
no mechanism to catch a *key whose generating script has quietly gone
missing* until someone needs to regenerate it and can't. No fix attempted
this session beyond disclosure in `generatorTractionRecon.limitations`;
worth deciding whether generating scripts should themselves be a tracked,
required artifact class before the next loss.

`summary_arrays.json`: 134→135 top-level keys this milestone (only
`generatorTractionRecon` added). `drive_master.csv` untouched.
## M252 (2026-09-12) — Routine ingestion: 7 drives (367→374, 8,128.8→8,164.3 km); dash-named-export corpus_manifest bug found and fixed

**Batch.** 7 new drives, 2026-09-11, all admitted append-only. Odometer
updated to 44,227 km (as of 2026-09-11). `ambientByDrive` extended for all 7
drives (filename-chronological D-numbering, as supplied by Andrii): D1
07:42:27 +13°C, D2 08:01:27 +13°C, D3 15:04:47 +20°C, D4 15:23:18 +20°C, D5
19:24:41 +17°C, D6 19:37:40 +17°C, D7 21:57:07 +13°C. This is the first batch
whose raw exports use the archive-native dash-timestamp naming convention
(`2026-09-11_HH-MM-SS.csv`) rather than the usual `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.csv`; both
`_select_canonical_cohort` (compute_drive_summary_v6.py) and `_canonical_file_name`

below).

**Protocol.** Full 7-step ingestion. (1) ML16 archive/restore: rebuilt the
full master from raw (367 existing + 7 new = 374 canonical files via
`raw_only/`), then restored all 16 ML/domain columns on the 367 pre-existing
rows from the pre-ingestion master — verified 0/16 diffs after restore, and
confirmed the restore was load-bearing: a fresh sklearn refit on the enlarged
374-drive corpus had drifted between 2 and 355 rows per column across all 16
ML16 columns on the pre-existing 367 rows before restoration. All 170
non-ML columns were also diffed pre/post; the only differences were expected
corpus-wide recalibrations (current-sensor offset -0.3954→-0.3939 A single-pass
/ -0.3954 A two-pass unchanged, cell-spread regression coefficients, 4 drives'
`T1_at_peak_Crate`), not defects. (2) `build_summary_arrays()` called via a

raw-frame cache (374/374 drives, ~43s) partway through and switched to
`frame_loader`, cutting remaining per-unit raw-pass time roughly 5-10x.
`energyUncertaintyMC` came back `recomputeMode='fresh'` (nominal
1,348.1446 kWh vs. live `meta.grossThroughputKwh` 1,348.1 kWh, 0% drift),
confirming the M250 `raw_dir`-forwarding fix holds. `socHysteresisV2` carried

required to get a clean result). (5) `determinism_check.py`:
`withinSessionRepeatPass=true`, `canonicalSetReproducible=true`, written to

`summary_arrays.json.determinism`. (6) `build_html.js` → `validate_jsdom.js`:
10/10 tabs, 58 buttons, 0 console errors, 1 disclosed semantic warning
(`socHysteresisV2` staleness). The M251 JSX component-contract gate ran clean
(1/1 protected component intact — no repeat of the M250 regression). (7)
T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 acceptance tests: all PASS (T-01 golden-snapshot
note DRIFTED as expected on corpus growth, n=289→374, value unchanged at
213.0 A — not gating).

**Finding — `corpus_manifest.py` dash-name orphan/missing bug (found and
fixed this session).** `build()` compared the raw `drive_master.csv['file']`
values (which preserve the ORIGINAL export basename, dash-formatted for this
batch) directly against canonicalized on-disk filenames, without normalizing
the master side first — the same class of defect as the
`_select_canonical_cohort` basename-equality bug documented at M207, but in
a sibling module that was never exercised by it because every prior batch
used underscore-named exports. Uncaught, this would have reported all 7 new
drives as BOTH orphan (found on disk under their normalized name, no raw-string
match in `master_files`) AND missing (the raw dash-form master entries have no
normalized-form counterpart in the on-disk scan), breaking `oneToOneCanonical`
for a batch that is in fact clean. Fixed by normalizing `master_files` via
the module's own `_canonical()` before the diff, mirroring the M207 fix's
approach exactly. Because `_audit_raw_manifest()` (inside
`compute_summary_arrays.py`) calls `corpus_manifest.build()` internally, the
first `build_summary_arrays()` pass — which ran before this fix was applied —
had already embedded the pre-fix (incorrectly `oneToOneVerified=false`)
result into `arrays['rawManifest']`/`coverageMap`/`gpsAltitudeCoverage`;
`validate_jsdom.js`'s `SEM-FAIL: rawManifest.oneToOneVerified is false`
caught this immediately. Recomputed all three keys in place with the fixed
module and re-ran `_artifact_stamp()` (129/129 keys) before rebuilding;
`validate_jsdom.js` then passed clean. Post-fix `raw_manifest.json` snapshot
`2026-09-12_2b96cd77abf378d5`: 374 canonical / 2 comparison-only / 9
auxiliary, 0 orphan, 0 missing, one-to-one verified.

**raw_cache.tar** rebuilt from scratch this session (374/374 files, ~43s;
absent from Project Knowledge at session start, as at M247/M248) and
included in this session's outputs to seed the next one.

**Not re-run this batch (disclosed, not a defect).** `fuel_recon.py` /
`generatorTractionRecon` were not re-run against the 374-drive corpus this
session — routine ingestion did not request it and it is out of scope for a
7-drive append; still stands at its M248 basis (138/367 fuel-instrumented
drives, ~17% km). Whether any of the 7 new drives carry the fuel-flow PID has
not been checked. `speedSplit`/`simultaneity`/`crossval`/`rpmFinding`/
`sensitivity` remain stale at M246 basis as before (standing follow-up,
needs new classification code, unchanged this session).

## M251 (2026-09-11) — Restore §4b (Generator→Traction Recon) to the M249 revision after an M250 build regression; add a JSX component-contract gate to prevent recurrence

**Symptom.** The M250 dashboard rebuild shipped a REVERTED §4b section: the
M249 revision (proportional energy-flow Sankey, consolidated numbered
Key-findings and Limitations blocks, rewritten 4-bus-state simultaneity prose,
drive-type-palette f_gen bars) was replaced by the older box-and-arrow schematic
and the scattered per-item callouts. Confirmed against the M249 reference build
`xtrail_dashboard_22.html` (rendered §4b GeneratorTractionRecon transpiled body
35,233 chars / 181 createElement calls) vs the M250 output (regressed body).

**Root cause.** The regression was in `xtrail_summary.jsx`, NOT in
`summary_arrays.json`. The `generatorTractionRecon` DATA (flows with all 14
keys, driveTypeSplit, simultaneity, limitations/glossary/audit, etc.) was intact
and current (M248 basis) throughout. But the M250 session rebuilt from a
`/mnt/project/xtrail_summary.jsx` in which the `GeneratorTractionRecon()` +
`RTFlowSchematic()` components had reverted to their pre-M249 bodies (Project
Knowledge JSX lag, the same class of sync gap noted for the M247→M249 corpus
state). Because `build_html.js` validated only the DATA payload
(`REQUIRED_BLOCKS`, `_artifactStamps`), a reverted COMPONENT with intact data
passed every gate and shipped. Isolation diff of the regressed vs M249 JSX:
differences confined entirely to the §4b block (lines ~3960–4300) plus the 3
M250 edit lines — nothing else moved.

**Fix — restoration.** Rebuilt `xtrail_summary.jsx` as: M249 JSX base (authoritative
`xtrail_summary22.jsx`, carrying the correct §4b) with the three M250 edits
re-applied on top — (1) `outputCeilingKw ?? "86.68"` → `?? "—"`, (2)
`loadHeadroomPp ?? 13` → `?? "—"`, (3) the F-13 reproducibility-overclaim
sentence rewritten to the scoped byte-verified form. Verified the merged file
differs from the regressed `/mnt/project` copy ONLY within the §4b band (28 diff
hunks, 0 out-of-band) and carries both the M249 Sankey (9 ribbon paths) and all
3 M250 edits. Rebuilt §4b now matches the M249 reference structurally (181
createElement calls, identical). jsdom live-render confirms: §4b heading, Sankey
SVG (8 proportional ribbons, combustion/loss/electrical/battery/regen palette),
◆ Key findings block, ⚠ Limitations block, and the f_gen-by-drive-type bars in
the dashboard drive-type palette (red→green) all render. Build 130/130 artifact
stamps match live MD5; jsdom 9/9 tabs, 52 buttons, 0 console errors, 2
pre-existing disclosed warnings. `drive_master.csv` /
`summary_arrays.json` untouched.

**Fix — drift prevention (the standing ask).** Added a JSX COMPONENT-CONTRACT
GATE to `build_html.js`, run on the JSX source before transpile, parallel to the
data-side `REQUIRED_BLOCKS` gate. For each protected component it asserts the
function definition AND a set of revision-distinctive structural markers are
present; a reverted-to-older-body or removed component ABORTS the build with a
named diagnosis instead of silently shipping a stale section. Initial contract:
`GeneratorTractionRecon` requires `function RTFlowSchematic`, `conserved
cascade`, `◆ Key findings`, `⚠ Limitations`, `RTFlowSchematic F={F}`. Markers
are deliberately body-specific (not just the function name), so a revert trips
the gate even though the name still resolves. Negative-tested against the
regressed JSX: build aborts, reporting the 3 missing markers. Positive-tested
against the restored JSX: gate passes ("1 protected component(s) intact"). Extend
`JSX_COMPONENT_CONTRACT` when a future section's body carries content that must
not silently revert.

**Standing note.** This regression is a symptom of the recurring Project
Knowledge JSX/corpus lag. The component-contract gate now catches the specific
failure mode (a section reverting while its data stays current) at build time.
The broader mitigation remains: verify the disk JSX against the CHANGELOG head
each session before rebuilding, and treat a dashboard rebuild as requiring both
data gates AND the component-contract gate green.

**Bug found: `run_pipeline()` never forwards `raw_dir` to
`build_summary_arrays()`.** `run_pipeline(raw_dir=..., ...)` receives
`raw_dir` but its call to `csa.build_summary_arrays(dm, loader, ...)` omits
it entirely. `energyUncertaintyMC`'s recompute gate is `... and raw_dir`
(hard requirement, not a raw_loader fallback), so every ingestion run via
the documented one-command CLI path has been silently falling back to
`recomputeMode='carriedForward'` regardless of the `recompute_energy_mc=True`
default — contradicting the M217 policy note that the MC recomputes every
ingestion. Same gap affects `_audit_raw_manifest`'s `oneToOneVerified`
bijection check (also a hard `raw_dir` requirement, not a fallback) and
partially affects `_soc_balanced_fuel`/`_hf_perdrive`/`_vgt_airpath`/
`_baro_compensation`/`_full_cell_case_study`/`_thermal_fuel_penalty(_continuous)`
(these have a raw_loader-first / raw_dir-fallback pattern, so unaffected in
practice for this batch since every file resolved via raw_loader — but the
gap is latent for any file raw_loader can't reach). Worked around this
session by calling `build_summary_arrays()` directly with `raw_dir` set;
`energyUncertaintyMC` came back `recomputeMode='fresh'`, nominal 1,333.6768
kWh vs. live `meta.grossThroughputKwh` 1,333.7 kWh (+0.02 kWh, 0% drift).

needs a one-line `raw_dir=raw_dir` fix.**

`summary_arrays.json` and the dashboard. `nPairs=309` (not 319, the max
possible consecutive-pair count across 320 drives) because 7 drives carry
no pack-temperature channel at all (pre-instrumentation-era files).
`nPairsAmbient=282` (not 309) because the stat gates on a *computed*
`retainedFrac`, which requires not just that the next drive carry an
ambient value but that the previous drive's end-of-drive pack temp
actually exceed it (`initExcessC > 0`) — 27 pairs have ambient recorded
but no positive excess to track carryover of. Verified bin-by-bin against
the live `gapBins` table: exact match on all 6 bins. The gap-related table
is fully current.

**Finding 2 (unexpected, more serious): code/JSON desync.** Re-running
`_heat_soak_carryover`/`_carryover_thermal_decay` exactly as committed in
`compute_summary_arrays.py` reproduced `soakTauH=35.52`,
`halfLife=24.62` — the pre-M242 OLS-through-origin values M242's own
entry documents replacing — not the `soakTauH=10.53`/`halfLife=7.30`/
`fitMethod:'senSlope'` values actually present in `summary_arrays.json`.
Both `_heat_soak_carryover` (pack) and `_carryover_thermal_decay`
(coolant/oil) still contained `slope = np.sum(x*y)/np.sum(x*x)`, no
`_sen_slope` call, no `fitMethod`/`fitIntercept` output keys — despite
the CHANGELOG head being M242 and `summary_arrays.json` fully reflecting
M242's claimed Sen's-slope results. `xtrail_summary.jsx`'s Heat-Soak
Carryover paragraph was similarly still pre-M242: displaying the raw
`R²={H.tauFitR2}` (now a large negative number for a non-variance-
minimizing estimator — exactly the "reads as broken without explanation"
outcome M242's own entry warned against) and a hardcoded "~12 h" half-life
reference stale against the new 7.30 h figure. `summary_arrays.json` was
evidently generated by a working copy of the code during the M242 session
that was never saved back to Project Knowledge; a fresh ingestion run
against the committed files would have silently regressed
`heatSoakCarryover`/`interDriveCarryover.thermalDecay.{coolant,oil}` back
to the OLS figures with no error — a code-vs-output reproducibility gap
the existing isolation-diff/determinism gates don't check.

**Fix.** Re-applied M242's described patch to both functions:
`_heat_soak_carryover` and `_carryover_thermal_decay` now compute
`slope = _sen_slope(x, y)` (the same estimator already used by
`_car_off_standby` for an identical long-gap-leverage problem) in place
of the squared-gap-weighted OLS slope, and both add `fitMethod:'senSlope'`
and a `tauFitIntercept`/`fitIntercept` field (`median(y - slope*x)`, the
fit's own through-origin check). Bootstrap CIs (plain resample for the
pack, day-clustered resample for coolant/oil, both seed=42, 1000 draws)
now resample-and-refit with `_sen_slope` instead of the OLS formula.
`_carryover_thermal_decay`'s inner `_fit_tau` now returns a 3-tuple
(`tau, r2, intercept`); the ambient-sensitivity refit call site updated
to match. `xtrail_summary.jsx`'s Heat-Soak Carryover paragraph updated to
match M242's documented dashboard intent: no longer displays raw
`tauFitR2`, instead shows the Sen's-slope/through-origin-intercept
disclosure when `fitMethod==='senSlope'`; the "~12 h" literal replaced
with a live `{H.soakHalfLifeH}` binding; the 6–12h/12–24h model-vs-
empirical comparison now computes the model's predicted retained fraction
at each bin's midpoint live via `Math.exp(-mid/H.soakTauH)` instead of
asserting only the empirical side as hand-typed text.

**Validation.** Rebuilt `traj` from raw and reproduced, field-for-field,
exact matches to the live `summary_arrays.json` for all three channels:
battery (`soakTauH=10.53`, `soakTauCI=[8.6,13.75]`, `soakHalfLifeH=7.3`,
`tauFitN=204`, `tauFitR2=-2.256`, `tauFitIntercept=0.0151`,
`fitMethod='senSlope'`), coolant (`tau=3.54`, `tauCI=[3.11,4.16]`,
`fitIntercept=-0.1083`, `r2=-22.321`, `nfit=273`, `nDays=70`,
`parkingAmbientSensitivity` offsets `[4.67, 2.65]`), oil (`tau=3.54`,
`tauCI=[3.26,3.87]`, `fitIntercept=-0.0918`, `r2=-24.156`, `nfit=263`,
sensitivity `[4.41, 2.96]`) — all byte-exact to the values M242's own
table and `interDriveCarryover.thermalDecay` already carry. Isolation
diff on `compute_summary_arrays.py`: exactly the two target functions
changed (slope estimator, new output fields, updated method-string
prose), nothing else. Isolation diff on `xtrail_summary.jsx`: exactly the
one Heat-Soak Carryover paragraph changed. `drive_master.csv` and
`summary_config.json` MD5-unchanged (this is a code-only fix; no array
values changed since `summary_arrays.json` was already correct). `py_compile`
clean. `build_html.js`: corpus-hash gate passes (129/129 stamped keys),
`crossVehicle`/`socHysteresisV2`/`energyUncertaintyMC` provenance checks
pass, same pre-existing hardcoded-literal WARN list, wrote
`xtrail_dashboard.html` (2133 KB). `validate_jsdom.js`: 9/9 tabs, 52
buttons, 0 console errors, 0 semantic warnings. Rendered-DOM check on the
Thermal tab confirms the live text: "τ ≈ 10.53 h (half-life 7.3 h; ...
Sen's-slope estimator, through-origin check (median residual at gap=0)
+0.0151)... still roughly HALF the initial excess at the fitted
half-life (~7.3 h)... The fitted exponential predicts 43% retained at
the 6–12 h bin's midpoint and 18% at the 12–24 h bin's midpoint" — no
stale R² or "~12 h" literal remaining. `_acceptance_tests`: T-01, T-01b,
T-02, T-03, T-04 all PASS (T-01 golden-snapshot drift note is
pre-existing staleness in `_T01_GOLDEN`, unrelated to this fix).

## M242 (2026-09-08) — Robust heat-soak/carryover tau (Sen's slope); Parasitic Draws de-hardcoded; 3 Sessions notes corrected

**Trigger.** User review of M241 flagged the 35.52h heat-soak half-life as
physically implausible, questioned whether "Sessions" and "Long-Highway
Thermal Convergence" carried stale ambient data, and asked whether
"Parasitic Draws" was ambient-linked. Investigation confirmed the tau
figure was a genuine artefact (below) and surfaced two real, unrelated
issues in the same pass.

**1. Heat-soak/carryover tau — root cause and fix.**
`_heat_soak_carryover`'s battery-pack tau and `_carryover_thermal_decay`'s
coolant/oil tau both fit `ln(residExcess/initExcess)` vs gap **through the
origin**, with slope estimated as the squared-gap-weighted
`sum(x*y)/sum(x^2)`. A single 187.5h (~7.8-day) parked gap
(`20260523_222103.csv → 20260531_183645.csv`, both newly ambient-covered
by M241) carried 69% of `Sum(x^2)` in the battery fit and single-handedly
pulled tau from ~16-18h to 35.52h; excluding just that one pair reverted
it to 16.3h. **Fix:** replaced the weighted-OLS slope with **Sen's
slope** — `_sen_slope(x, y)`, the median of all pairwise
`(y_j-y_i)/(x_j-x_i)` — already used elsewhere in this pipeline
(`_car_off_standby`) for the identical long-gap-leverage failure mode. A
median-of-ratios-to-origin (`median(y_i/x_i)`) alternative was tried
first and rejected: it fixed the large-gap problem but introduced the
mirror-image one, since coolant/oil have many sub-minute-gap pairs where
dividing by a near-zero x turns ordinary reading noise into an enormous
implied rate (coolant tau collapsed to 2.2h, R²≈-64). Sen's slope is
robust to both. Per explicit instruction, **multi-day parked gaps are not
excluded or capped** — they're real, expected inputs (the corpus's
longest is ~8 days) and remain in the fit; the estimator itself is what
no longer lets one dominate.

Results (320-drive corpus, all `ambientByDrive` entries, replacing the
M241 OLS figures):
| Channel | M241 (broken OLS) | M242 (Sen's slope) |
|---|---|---|
| Battery pack | τ=35.52h, half-life=24.62h, R²=0.234, n=204 | **τ=10.53h, half-life=7.30h**, intercept=+0.015, n=204 |
| Coolant | τ=9.93h (pre-M241 OLS) | **τ=3.54h**, CI [3.11,4.16], intercept=-0.108, n=273 |
| Oil | τ=9.16h (pre-M241 OLS) | **τ=3.54h**, CI [3.26,3.87], intercept=-0.092, n=263 |

Every channel's fit intercept (the estimator's own check of the
through-origin assumption: median residual at gap=0) now sits close to
zero, supporting the model. R² is no longer reported/displayed for these
fits — it's an OLS-specific diagnostic and can be (and now is) negative
for a robust, non-variance-minimizing estimator; that's expected, not a
sign of a bad fit, but showing a bare negative R² without explanation
would read as broken. `tauFitIntercept`/`fitIntercept` and `fitMethod`
('senSlope') are new disclosed fields on both `heatSoakCarryover` and
`interDriveCarryover.thermalDecay.{coolant,oil}`.

Dashboard prose updated to match: the Heat-Soak Carryover section's
narrative no longer cites the stale "~12h" half-life reference point (now
computed live from `H.soakHalfLifeH`), no longer displays R², and the
model-vs-empirical-bin comparison at 6-24h is now computed live in JSX
(`Math.exp(-mid/H.soakTauH)`) rather than asserted as hand-typed text —
it was written against the old τ and would have gone stale silently
under the new one otherwise.

**2. Parasitic Draws — hardcoding removed.**
Four of five table rows were literal strings not bound to any `S.*` key
(the project's own stated anti-pattern): "Overnight (large ΔT)"/"Daytime
parked (small ΔT)" ΔT/rate figures, and "Car ON, stationary —
mild"/"— AC" draw figures. Replaced with live bindings:
- Overnight/daytime-park rows now read `S.heatSoakCarryover.gapBins`
  directly (12-24h bin for "overnight-scale", 3-6h bin for "short
  daytime park"), computing the °C/hr rate from the bin's own
  `medShedC`/gap-midpoint rather than a hand-typed number.
- Car ON mild/AC rows now read `S.auxLoadAmbient.byAmbientBin`'s coolest
  (10-15°C, n=20, −1.00 kW) and warmest (30-40°C, n=28, −1.92 kW) bins —
  that section's own "no HVAC state channel, descriptive not causal"
  caveat is inherited and noted in the surrounding prose, since "AC" is
  inferred from the ambient-vs-draw correlation, not measured directly.
- Car OFF standby row (already dynamic) is unchanged.

**3. Sessions — 3 hand-typed notes corrected.**
The `sessions`/`sessionGroups` narrative notes in `summary_config.json`
are static hand-typed prose, independent of `ambientByDrive` and never
touched by M241's recompute. Cross-checking every note in the 67-drive
M241 date range against the newly-sourced ambient values found:
- **Jun 3** — "14-20°C" (unlabeled) is almost exactly the day's battery
  pack-mean span (14→17→17→20°C across the two drives, confirmed against
  `_battery_temp_traj`), not ambient, which was unlogged at authorship
  time. Note reworded to label this explicitly and add the actual
  ambient (14.6-14.9°C).
- **Jun 18** — "17°C bat/19°C air" explicitly claimed ambient=19°C. The
  17°C battery figure checks out exactly against `pm_start`; the "19°C
  air" does not match the sourced value (23.3°C), a 4.3°C correction.
  Note updated in place, both figures preserved with the correction
  flagged.
- **Jul 11 D1** — "amb ~28→? °C" was self-flagged uncertain by its own
  author; superseded with the now-resolved 24.0→21.5→21.3°C.

Not a full-corpus sweep — scoped to the specific instances surfaced by
the M241 date-range cross-check. A dedicated reconciliation pass across
the remaining ~250 dates' hand-typed notes (most of which predate the
ambient-gap problem M241 fixed and were authored with ambient already in
hand) has not been done and would be a separate, larger task.

**Validation.** Isolation diff: exactly the 7 M241 keys changed again
(same set — `heatSoakCarryover`/`interDriveCarryover` values differ, no
new/removed top-level keys), 0 unexpected diffs across the other 126.
`build_html.js`: corpus-hash gate passes (drive_master.csv MD5 unchanged
— this session touched `compute_summary_arrays.py`, `summary_config.json`
notes, and `xtrail_summary.jsx` only). `validate_jsdom.js`: 9/9 tabs, 52
buttons, 0 console errors. Manually rendered the Thermal tab DOM text and
confirmed both edited sections show live-bound numbers matching the
recomputed arrays (Parasitic Draws' four dynamic rows; Heat-Soak
Carryover's gap-bin table). Acceptance tests: T-01, T-01b, T-02, T-03,
T-04 all PASS.

## M241 (2026-09-08) — 67 missing ambientByDrive entries verified & ingested: full 320/320 ambient coverage

**Trigger.** 67 of 320 primary drives (2026-05-11 through 2026-07-11) lacked
a manual `ambientByDrive` entry. User supplied
`missing_ambient_temperature_drives_populated.xlsx` (3-hour-node weather-grid
linear interpolation, cited sources, ±0.1°C) for all 67.

**Verification (pre-ingestion gate).** Completeness: 67/67 have Start+End;
11/67 exceed 60 min and all 11 carry an Interim reading at exactly
`start+60min`, self-consistent with the workbook's own documented rule.
Plausibility: reproduced `_battery_temp_traj()`'s cold-start methodology
exactly and built empirical plausibility bands from the trusted pre-existing
253-drive corpus (battery-pack-mean-minus-ambient delta at start: hard range
−11..+26°C, n=251) rather than assuming thresholds. Result: 0/67 entries
implausible; 6 borderline cases all fall inside the corpus's own observed
envelope, explained by ordinary short-gap heat retention or long-gap
radiative cooling. One file (`20260513_180335.csv`) predates all
temperature-related OBD PIDs and has zero telemetry to check against —
accepted with a telemetry-unverifiable caveat, not rejected. A candidate
4th validation channel (a raw column literally named "ambient air
temperature," present in only 4 early files) was tested and discarded: it
drifts up to 10°C within a single ~20-min drive while moving, consistent
with an intake-air sensor under ram-air cooling, not a genuine ambient
probe — not used, consistent with the corpus's existing position that
there is no reliable OBD outside-air channel.

**Ingestion.** `ambientByDrive` merged 253→320 (0 key collisions).
Recomputed the 7 array keys with a direct ambient dependency via targeted
additive splice (NOT a full `build_summary_arrays()` run — no ML16 refit,
no `run_pipeline()`): `batteryVsAmbient` (251→313 covered drives),
`batteryTempRanges` (ambient bins only: 71/97/83→95/134/84; class bins
unchanged, confirming isolation), `belowAmbient` (38→51 below-ambient-start
drives, same max −11°C), `heatSoakCarryover`, `interDriveCarryover`,
`dailyFingerprints`, `auxLoadAmbient` (245→301 drives, 56→73 days).
`drive_master.csv` untouched (MD5 unchanged) — this was a config/arrays-only
update.

**Two headline findings surfaced by the completed coverage, not silently
absorbed:**
1. **`heatSoakCarryover.soakTauH` shifted 17.63h → 35.52h** (half-life
   12.22h → 24.62h), CI widened (11.38–23.69 → 11.75–54.87), R² dropped
   0.465 → 0.234 (tauFitN 168→204). Per-gap-bin medians (medShedC,
   medTStart/End, medRetainedFrac) are **nearly unchanged** — the shift is
   driven by `nAmb` (ambient-covered pairs) increasing disproportionately
   in the sparse, already-noisy 6–24h+ gap bins (16→19, 30→38, 14→19),
   where the through-origin Newtonian-tau regression has high leverage.
   Not a data-quality artifact of the new entries; a genuine consequence of
   completing coverage in previously underrepresented long-gap pairs.
   **Flagged for manuscript review** — the previous 17.63h figure was
   fitted on an ambient-incomplete sample skewed toward the corpus's later
   calendar period.
2. **`dailyFingerprints` cluster count changed 3→2** ("3 stable recurring
   duty profiles, ARI=0.627" → "2 stable recurring duty profiles,
   ARI=1.000"). `nDaysComplete` rose 56→74 (ambient is a completeness
   gate for this feature set). Silhouette landscape: old best k=3
   (0.3262) narrowly beat k=2 (0.3005); new best k=2 (0.2871) now clearly
   beats k=3 (0.2064) — the old 3-way split's silhouette collapsed once
   the previously-excluded days were included, while the 2-cluster
   solution's bootstrap stability rose to near-perfect. KMeans seed=42
   fixed both runs — deterministic, not a seeding artifact. **Flagged for
   manuscript review** — likely a correction (cleaner, better-supported
   result) rather than a regression, but the "3 profiles" language
   wherever it appears in the manuscript needs updating.

**Validation.** Isolation diff: exactly the 7 intended top-level keys

## M239 (2026-09-07) — Deep Article Audit (PDF) remediation: C1 time-aligned C-rate/temperature pairing + Ch.11 GTC/FCE/EFC glossary split

**Trigger.** `Deep_Article_Audit_E-Power.pdf` (24 pp., independent of the
`DEEP_SCIENTIFIC_ARTICLE_AUDIT.txt` already addressed in M238) raised four
items scoped for this session: C1, C2, C3, C9 (estimate/triage) and the
Chapter 11 GTC/FCE/EFC terminology finding (fix). C2/C3/C9 were assessed
against the live pipeline; C1 required an actual recompute, not a relabel.

**C1 — FIXED (Critical, confirmed valid).** The C-rate/temperature risk map
(`cRatePoints`) previously paired each drive's peak charge C-rate with
`T1_peak` — the drive's hottest reading ANYWHERE in the drive — even when
the two events were not simultaneous. Both HV Battery Current and HV
Battery Temperature Sensor 1 are logged on native timestamps in every raw
CSV, so the true co-timed pairing is directly computable. New master column
`T1_at_peak_Crate`: for whichever channel (eng_charge/dual/regen) produced
the drive's reported peak C-rate, T1 asof-aligned to that exact current
sample (3s tolerance, matching the pipeline's existing `ENG_ALIGN_TOL`
convention for engine-state alignment). Falls back to `T1_peak` only for
drives lacking a raw current+temperature probe (9 of 320 — early logs
predating full PID coverage).

Verified against the live pipeline's own `_v5_analyze_bytes` output on the
worst-discrepancy file before trusting the corpus-wide run (two bugs in the
verification probe itself were caught and fixed this way: a duplicate
`x1000`-scaled RPM column silently mis-selected on 3 files, and a
pandas post-`dropna()` index-alignment defect that silently scrambled row
assignment — both fixed in the probe, not the pipeline, which was already
correct).

Corpus effect (301 of 320 drives with a defined peak-C-rate point): the
existing pairing overstated the co-timed temperature by a median of 2°C
(up to 16°C, mean 2.5°C). Re-pairing:
  - moves 6 points from the "optimal" band into the cold-risk zone
    (10 → 16 of 301 points now below 20°C; peak C-rate paired with a
    sub-20°C pack rises from 18.9C to 23.8C — one drive (`20260721_114246`)
    goes from a comfortable-looking 27°C/23.8C point to a genuine 19°C
    cold-pack high-current event);
  - removes 25 of 49 points from the heat-risk zone (≥44°C) — those charge
    events happened at a cooler moment than the drive's separately-timed
    peak temperature, a false co-occurrence manufactured by the old pairing.

Also caught in the process: the chart's own caveat text asserted "no drive
in this corpus falls inside" the cold-risk zone — false against the
dashboard's OWN pre-fix `cRatePoints` data (10 points already sat below
20°C). Caveat is now computed live from `S.cRatePoints` (an explicit
`S.*`-binding, per the dashboard's own anti-hardcoded-literal convention)
instead of being a hand-typed claim, so it cannot go stale again. Axis
label and inline caption corrected to describe the pairing as
simultaneous-at-peak-current rather than drive-peak-anywhere; a fixed
"X = average battery temp" mislabel (it was always peak, never average) was
also corrected in the same pass. `cRateRefLines.axis` bounds unaffected
(new corpus max co-timed temp 49°C vs old drive-max 51°C; same rounded
`xMax`). `cRateRefLines.lines` (median/regen/dual-peak reference lines) are
C-rate-only and unaffected by the temperature re-pairing; spot-checked that
the dataset's most extreme charge events (36.4C, 36.2C, 35.6C...) still land
in the optimal 20-40°C band under the corrected pairing — if anything more
robustly than before (one, previously drawn at a stale 48°C "heat" reading,
is now correctly shown at 39°C).

Isolation: `summary_arrays.json` diff limited to the single `cRatePoints`
key (leaf-level splice; all other 125 top-level keys byte-identical).
`drive_master.csv` gains 2 columns (`T1_at_peak_Crate`,
`T1_at_peak_Crate_isFallback`); all 182 pre-existing columns unchanged.

**C2 — assessed, not re-opened this session.** RPM-quantization circularity
(binning RPM into 250-rpm steps, then reading the resulting peaks as
discrete OEM setpoints) is already substantially hedged by M205/M218
(±25 rpm weighted-center-of-mass setpoint separation) and M174 (cadence-
invariance robustness check across the corpus's two logging generations).
No formal bin-width-sensitivity/KDE/change-point analysis exists yet — the
audit's specific required action is not fully satisfied, but the prose
already reads "consistent with, not proof of" rather than asserting
discrete setpoints as fact. Left open for a dedicated milestone.

**C3 — already resolved on the dashboard; not the article.** `highSocRegen`
already carries both the all-charging headline (14.4% reduction,
engineOnSharePct=67.86%, nonDeceleratingSharePct=61.83% — matching the
audit's own recomputation almost exactly) AND a `demandControlledRegen`
pure-regen subset (reductionPct=8.7%, matching the audit's recommended
figure) engine off/decelerating/motor-torque<0 only. Gap: the pure-regen
figure is presented as supporting prose, not the primary KPI card — see the
separate primary/secondary chart-swap estimate below.

**C9 — already resolved on the dashboard; not the article.** The >12h
"equilibrated" contradiction the audit flags (vs. the fitted 12.22h
cooling half-life) is already explicitly corrected in the Heat-Soak
Carryover section ("BY DEFINITION of that half-life, still roughly HALF
the initial excess at ~12h... not 'gone'"), with the ambient-reference
proxy limitation also already caveated. See the separate gapBins
cross-check for a numeric verification against the fitted curve.

**Chapter 11 (GTC/FCE/EFC terminology) — FIXED.** The Python pipeline
(M62/M95) already defines these three quantities rigorously; the mixing was
confined to the JSX presentation layer:
  - Glossary combined "FCE / EFC" into a single row (implying synonymy).

    (discharge-only, industry convention), "EFC (Rainflow)" (DoD-summed,

  - History-tab "Jun 22-27" annotation displayed a GTC delta labelled
    "EFC" (`S.cycleCumulative` / `gtcTotal` is a GTC series per the M62/M95
    canonical-key comments) — corrected to "GTC".
  - History-tab KPI subtitle called the Rainflow-EFC total a bare "EFC" —
    corrected to "Rainflow-EFC" for consistency with the SVG legend and the
    Cell-Health section's three-way disambiguation (M238 fix 3).
  - Stale code comments referencing "EFC" for what are GTC values cleaned
    up for maintainability (non-user-facing).

**Validation.** `build_html.js`: clean Babel parse, `_artifactStamps`
corpus-hash matches, `cRatePoints` isolation confirmed (only changed key).

## M238 (2026-09-07) — Article-audit follow-up: dashboard-side fixes (348.6x CI, GTC/yr cross-reference, FCE/EFC disambiguation, GTC acronym drift)

**Trigger.** A deep independent audit of the Ukrainian-language article
(`DEEP_SCIENTIFIC_ARTICLE_AUDIT.txt`, run against `E-Power_стаття.pdf`)
surfaced several apparent numerical inconsistencies. Cross-checking each one
against the live pipeline (not just `summary_arrays.json` in isolation)
showed three of the four were article-drafting artifacts with no
corresponding dashboard bug (the RPM-bin "~5%/~4%" prose, the 326.7-vs-329.6
stale Rainflow-EFC figure, and the Wikner-thesis chemistry caveat are all
either absent from or already correctly handled by the dashboard). Two real,
narrower dashboard-side issues were found underneath the other findings and
are fixed here.

**Fix 1 — "348.6x" headline ratio had no uncertainty band.** The
stationary-vs-highway engine-start-probability contrast
(`socHysteresis.stationaryVsHighwayContrast[0]`) rendered a bare point
ratio in prose, unlike nearly every other estimate on this dashboard. The
underlying cell rests on very few events (SoC 60%: stationary 7 of 20,043
at-risk seconds; high-speed 1,276 of 10,458) — a Wilson 95% CI on each
component swings from roughly [0.02%, 0.07%] to [11.6%, 12.8%], meaning the
348.6x point ratio is far less precise than the bare number suggested.
Hoisted the local `wilson` helper (previously scoped inside
`RpmStartStopSurface`, formula unchanged) to module scope as `wilson95()`,
added a `socSpeedCell()` lookup so a headline built from two
`startProbBySocSpeed` cells can pull their n/k back out, and rewrote the
sentence to show both probabilities with their n/k and 95% CI, plus an
explicit "the point ratio is poorly constrained" caveat. No Python/JSON
change — the n/k data already existed in `startProbBySocSpeed`; this was a
presentation gap, not a missing computation.

**Fix 2 — the two GTC/yr "observed" figures read as contradictory without
context.** `observedRate` (History tab, `gtcTotal*(365.25/daysIncl)` —
today ≈1,943 GTC/yr, window-pace) and `cycleLife.projections["Observed
logged mix"]` (Capacity-fade tab, today 1,642 GTC/yr, lifetime-average
`annualKm`) are both correct, separately-computed figures answering
different questions, but nothing linked them. The History tile already
said "highway-heavy"; added a matching one-line cross-reference to each
tile's caption naming the other tab and the basis difference (window-pace
vs. lifetime-average mileage), so a reader hitting either number sees the
other exists and why they differ.

**Fix 3 — an internally ambiguous sentence in the cell-health section.**
"GTC ... ≈2.061x the standard EFC; {FCE} FCE is the standard-equivalent
figure" sits FCE and "the standard EFC" close enough together that a reader
could take them as the same number — they are not (FCE=308.6,
`metricConvention.efcStandard`=299.5, ~3% apart, the gap being
charge/discharge round-trip-loss asymmetry per `fceOverStandardEfc`).
Rewrote to name FCE, the discharge-only "standard EFC", and the
Rainflow-EFC (`rfEfcSum`) as three distinct, explicitly-valued quantities
in one place, since all three get used independently elsewhere on this
dashboard.

**Fix 4 — GTC acronym drift inside the dashboard itself.** The glossary
(bound since the M62 terminology audit) reads "Gross **Throughput** Cycles"
— the only expansion whose initials actually spell GTC ("Gross **Capacity**
Turnover" spells GCT). One other location (`ProjectionView`'s scenario-table
header) still read "Gross Capacity Turnover (GTC)", pre-dating M62 and never
caught by it since it's a static string, not a `S.*`-bound value. Standardized
on "Gross Throughput Cycles (GTC)" everywhere; zero remaining occurrences of
the old wording.

**Not changed / explicitly out of scope for this session.** No Python
recompute, no `summary_arrays.json` or `summary_config.json` change (both
verified byte-identical to the pre-session copies — see isolation diff
below) — every fix here is presentational, working from data the pipeline
already produces. The audit's other recommendations (a capacity-sensitivity
table for the unverified 2.1 kWh constant; multiple-comparisons framing;
Methods-section placement, tone, and structural consolidation) are
article-manuscript concerns, not dashboard bugs, and were left for Andrii to
apply to the article manuscript directly — this session touched only
`xtrail_summary.jsx`.

**Validation.** Babel/`@babel/preset-react` parse clean before and after
every edit. `build_html.js`: 129/129 `_artifactStamps` corpus-hash matches,
pre-existing 8-item hardcoded-literal WARN unchanged and unrelated (present
identically pre-session). `validate_jsdom.js`: 9/9 tabs, 52 inner buttons,

confirmed real rendered numbers (not NaN/undefined) — the CI sentence

## M237 (2026-09-06) — Batch-A: F15 probability mislabel + evidenceLedger staleness catch

**F15 -- probability label.** `evidenceLedger`'s resistance-fade row mapped
`powerFade.pSlopeGt0` to a field literally named `pValue`. That quantity
is the FRACTION of day-clustered bootstrap resample slopes greater than
zero (`compute_drive_summary_v6.py`: `round((boot>0).mean(),3)`, seed=42,
N=4000 draws) -- neither a conventional null-hypothesis p-value nor
automatically a Bayesian posterior probability, as the audit notes.
Renamed to `bootstrapFractionPositive` and added a `bootstrapMethod` field
disclosing the method/seed/draw count, paired with the `ci95` interval
already present, per the audit's exact instruction. Checked for other
occurrences of this same mislabeling elsewhere in `evidenceLedger`: this
was the only one (the ledger's other p-value-like field, `lrP` on the
regime-transition row, is a genuine likelihood-ratio test p-value from a
model-adequacy comparison, not a bootstrap fraction, and needed no
change).

**Bonus catch while regenerating: `evidenceLedger` was stale since before
M229's F01 fix.** Row 1 (energy throughput) had never been regenerated
since the F01 energy-integration fix landed -- it still reported the
released gross throughput as 1263.7067 kWh / n=308 drives (the pre-F01
value) instead of the current, corrected 1295.913 kWh / n=306. Nothing in
this session's F01/F04 CHANGELOG entries had triggered a re-splice of
this specific block, since `evidenceLedger` is pure post-processing over
already-assembled `arrays` and wasn't itself touched by those milestones'
targeted splices. Regenerating it for the F15 fix necessarily picked up
the current, correct values for every row.

**Second bonus catch, found while re-verifying that regeneration:** the
same row's `notes` field had a HARDCODED literal -- "agrees to ~1.4% mean
/ ~1.5% p95" -- describing the independent-reintegration deviation, baked
in as fixed text rather than computed from
`independentIntegrationCheck.trueTrapezoidal`'s own
`meanAbsDevPctThroughput`/`p95AbsDevPctThroughput` fields (which now read
0.8752%/0.3071% post-F01, not 1.4%/1.5%). This is the same species of bug
as F03 and F26 (a prose literal silently desynced from the data it's
describing), just not separately numbered in the audit. Fixed to format
dynamically from the live fields, rounded to 2 decimals for readable
prose.

**Validation.** `py_compile` clean; zero unintended function-signature
drift (confirmed against the pre-M231 baseline). No JSX changes needed --
the ledger table renders `label`/`value`/`unit`/`ci95` generically and
never referenced the renamed `pValue` field directly. `build_html.js`
gates clean (129/129 corpusHash match). `validate_jsdom.js` 9/9 tabs, 52
buttons, 0 console errors, 0 semantic warnings; rendered-text spot-check
confirms the corrected throughput (1295.913 kWh) and deviation (0.8752%)
now display in the Evidence & Cross-Validation Ledger table.
Isolation-diffed the re-splice: exactly 19 changed leaves, all inside

T-04 all PASS.

## M236 (2026-09-06) — Batch-A: F32 dormant link bug + F26 pack-soak contradiction

First pass into the unprioritized Batch-A/B set (F12-F20, F23-F33) now
that all P0/P1 items are closed. Picked two clear, well-defined,
independently-verifiable items to start: a genuine dormant code bug
(F32) and a text-vs-data contradiction in the same pattern as F03 (F26).

**F32 -- dormant link bug.** `fit_glm()` supports `link='cloglog'`
(default) and `link='logit'`, but `_predict()` always applied the cloglog
inverse (`1-exp(-exp(eta))`) regardless of which link the passed-in
result was actually fit with. At eta=0 this returns 0.6321 for a
logit-fitted model instead of the correct 0.5. Confirmed dormant exactly
as the audit states: `link='logit'` is mentioned only in a docstring as a
planned future sensitivity check and is never actually passed at any of
the six call sites (`run_ladder`, `sensitivity_screen`, `_final_fit`,
`oos_predict`, `rolling_origin_predict`, `rolling_origin_cv` all use the
default `link='cloglog'`) -- so this bug has never affected a single
reported score.

**Fix.** `_predict()` now reads the actual fitted family's link object
off the statsmodels result (`res.model.family.link.inverse(eta)`) instead
of hardcoding the cloglog formula, with the old unconditional formula
kept as a fallback if the link object is ever unavailable. Verified
against both link types directly: cloglog inverse at eta=0 still gives
0.6321205588285577 (unchanged), logit inverse at eta=0 now correctly
gives 0.5. Verified the fix has ZERO effect on any currently-reported
number by fitting the same synthetic data with both the pre- and
post-fix code under `link='cloglog'` and confirming byte-identical
predictions (max abs diff: 0.0) -- this closes the bug without touching
`summary_arrays.json` or requiring any refit.

**F26 -- pack-soak contradiction.** `heatSoakCarryover` reports a fitted
Newtonian-cooling τ=17.63h and half-life=12.22h, but the dashboard prose
said carryover is "effectively gone beyond ~12h." That's contradicted by
the fit's own math: at t=12h (just under one half-life), the fitted
exponential retains e^(-12/17.63) ≈ 50.6% of the initial excess --
roughly HALF, not "gone." Separately, the audit notes the EMPIRICAL
binned medians (not the fit) tell a different story at that range: the
6-12h bin retains 28% and the 12-24h bin sits at -10% (near/below the
next-drive ambient reference, a floor artefact from ambient being the
manual driving-time field rather than the true parked environment). These
two views -- the fitted continuous decay and the empirical binned
medians -- genuinely disagree by 12+ hours; audit calls this "selection
and ambient-reference limitations," not a single consistent Newtonian
result at long gaps.

**Fix.** Replaced the incorrect fixed claim with prose that: (1) states
the half-life fact correctly (roughly half retained at ~12h, not gone);
(2) surfaces the actual empirical bin values (28% at 6-12h, -10% at
12-24h) computed dynamically from `H.gapBins`, not hardcoded; (3)
explicitly discloses the disagreement between the fitted model and the
empirical bins at long gaps, attributing it to selection effects and the
ambient-reference floor rather than picking one framing and hiding the
tension. Confirmed via rendered-text check that the corrected prose
displays the right bin values (28%, -10%) computed live from the JSON,
not typed literals.

**Validation.** `py_compile` clean; zero function-signature drift in
`m119v2_model.py` (only `_predict`'s body changed, confirmed via direct
diff of every `def` line against the pre-M231 baseline). JSX transpiles
cleanly. `build_html.js` gates clean (129/129 corpusHash match --
unaffected since neither fix touches `summary_arrays.json`).
`validate_jsdom.js` 9/9 tabs, 52 buttons, 0 console errors, 0 semantic
warnings; rendered-text spot-check confirms the corrected pack-soak
prose. T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS. No JSON splice needed for
either fix -- F32 is provably a no-op on shipped numbers, F26 is a pure
prose correction reading already-computed fields.

**Remaining Batch-A/B scope:** F12-F20, F23-F25, F27-F31, F33 -- roughly
18 findings remain, spanning definitional/narrative caveats (F12, F13,
F16-F20, F23-F25, F30), a text contradiction similar in kind to F26
(none currently known), harder statistical/censoring rework (F27-F29,
F31), and fit-status/convergence gating (F33). Not yet sequenced.

## M235 (2026-09-06) — Audit P1: F09 provenance stamps do not prove freshness (partial)

Closes the fifth and final **P1** item in audit priority order (F05, F06,
F07, F08, F09 all now addressed to the extent scoped below). This is a
**partial** fix -- F09 is a systemic architecture finding, not a single
statistical bug, and the audit's own rework table asks for a full
per-block dependency-tracking system (exact input-byte hashing, source-
module identity, computation-version stamping, a cache contract, a
dependency lockfile, splitting the monolith by domain). None of that
larger rework is attempted here; this closes the specific, concretely
actionable gaps the finding names.

**F09 -- stamps do not prove freshness.** `_artifact_stamp` applied the
IDENTICAL corpusHash/configHash/generatedAt to every one of the ~129
top-level blocks in one pass, regardless of whether that specific block
was genuinely computed in this build or carried forward unchanged from a
prior one. A carried-forward block (e.g. `socHysteresisV2` under its
own opt-in `recompute_m119v2=False` policy) received exactly the same
"fresh" stamp as a block computed seconds earlier from the current
corpus -- the stamp recorded "a build ran at time T against corpus C,"
never "this payload was computed at time T from corpus C."

**Fixed, three parts:**

1. **`computationStatus` per block.** `_artifact_stamp` now reads each
   block's own `recomputeMode`/`frozenBasis` field (the only two modules
   with an explicit carry-forward path today: `socHysteresisV2`,
   `energyUncertaintyMC`) and reports `'computed'`, `'carriedForward'`,
   or `'carriedForward_recomputeFailed'` per block, with a
   `computationStatusNote` explaining that `generatedAt`/`corpusHash`
   reflect the stamping pass, not necessarily this block's own last
   computation, whenever status isn't `'computed'`. Verified against a
   synthetic fixture covering all five status paths (fresh /
   carriedForward / carriedForward_recomputeFailed / frozenBasis=true /
   no self-tracking at all) before splicing into the live corpus.
   Currently both `socHysteresisV2` and `energyUncertaintyMC` read as
   `'computed'` in this corpus (both were genuinely recomputed this
   session -- M231's cascade check and M230 respectively) -- this fix's
   value is in making the DISTINCTION machine-checkable going forward,
   not in changing today's classification.

2. **`fullConfigHash`.** The existing `configHash` covers only the
   `constantProvenance` subset (CAP_KWH, SCENARIO_THRESHOLD_GTC, etc.) --
   audit's exact complaint: "not the full actual configuration, manual
   ambient records, session annotations, model settings." Added
   `fullConfigHash`/`fullConfigHashSource`: an MD5 of the ENTIRE on-disk
   `summary_config.json`, added alongside (not replacing) the narrower
   `configHash` for backward compatibility. Catches an edit to ANY config
   value, not only the ones already routed through `constantProvenance`.

3. **`build_html.js`'s corpus-hash gate now fails closed, not open.**
   Three concrete gaps, all from the audit's own list of "concrete
   failure cases to gate": (a) an unreadable `drive_master.csv` at
   build_html.js time previously logged a note and SKIPPED the entire
   comparison, silently passing a build whose corpus identity was never
   actually checked -- now aborts (exit 1); (b) the gate iterated
   `Object.keys(stamps)` rather than the actual data keys in `arraysObj`,
   so a top-level array key with NO `_artifactStamps` entry at all was
   invisible to the check, not merely unchecked -- now iterates the real
   data keys (with one sanctioned, documented exception: `releaseProvenance`,
   which `build_html.js` itself synthesizes AFTER Python-side stamping
   already ran, so it structurally cannot carry a Python stamp); (c)
   fallback-sourced stamps (`drive_master.csv` absent when
   `summary_arrays.json` was built) were downgraded to a `console.warn`
   and silently accepted -- now abort the build, matching the audit's
   explicit "build with an absent master... should [not] qualify as a
   fully verified publication build."

   All three fixes verified by direct fault injection against copies of
   the live corpus: (a) renamed `drive_master.csv` away -> exit 1; (b)
   deleted one key's `_artifactStamps` entry entirely -> exit 1,
   correctly named; (c) set one stamp's `corpusHashSource` to a fallback
   value -> exit 1; (d) corrupted one stamp's `corpusHash` -> exit 1,
   correctly named as a hash mismatch, not confused with (b) or (c). The
   unmodified corpus continues to build cleanly (exit 0, 129/129 keys
   checked).

**Not attempted (explicitly out of scope for this milestone):** per-block
exact-input-byte hashing (each function hashing only the specific rows/
columns it actually reads, not the whole master); per-block source-module/
computation-version hashing (detecting a code change to one function
without requiring a rebuild trigger); a cache contract (explicit schema/
dtypes/timestamps replacing the pickle-based raw cache); a dependency
lockfile and executable build entry point; distinguishing "source
identity" from "computation freshness" from "model validation" from
"presentation checks" as separate gates rather than folding them into one
aggregate; versioning `soc_patterns.json` as a tracked generated asset;
splitting the ~17,300-line `compute_summary_arrays.py` /
~9,700-line `xtrail_summary.jsx` monoliths by domain. F32 (dormant cloglog/
logit link bug in `fit_glm`) and F33 (fit-status/convergence gating) --
mentioned in the same audit section but not P1-tagged -- are also not
addressed here.

**Validation.** `py_compile` clean; function-signature diff against the
pre-M231 baseline shows only this session's five milestones' intentional
additions and nothing else (confirmed the `_artifact_stamp` multi-line
signature change is exactly the new `summary_config_path` parameter, via
direct sed-range diff since the standard signature-only grep misses
continuation lines). `build_html.js` syntax-checked and exercised against
four fault-injected scenarios plus the clean corpus. `validate_jsdom.js`
9/9 tabs, 52 buttons, 0 console errors, 0 semantic warnings (dashboard
prose does not reference `_artifactStamps` directly, so no JSX changes
were needed). Isolation-diffed the re-splice against last delivery:
exactly 387 changed leaves (129 keys x 3 new fields), ALL inside
`_artifactStamps` -- zero changes to any actual data payload, confirmed
both by JSON diff and by the fact this splice only added fields to
EXISTING stamp dicts (`generatedAt`/`corpusHash` per key preserved
byte-for-byte from before this milestone, since no computation actually
reran). T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS.

**Audit status.** All five P1-priority items (F05-F09) are now closed or
partially closed per their scoped required responses. Both P0 estimator/
contradiction items (F03, F04) and the P0 event-integrity item (F01) were
closed in M229/M230; F02 (source/export identity) remains blocked -- no
raw archive available. F10/F11/F22 (also P0) and F21 (F06's code-level
prerequisite) were closed in M229/M232. The unprioritized Batch-A/B set
(F12-F20, F23-F33) remains triaged but not yet sequenced or implemented --
next decision point for this project.

## M234 (2026-09-06) — Audit P1: F08 thermal-carryover wrong initial condition

Closes the fourth **P1** item in audit priority order (F05, F06, F07, F08
all now closed; F09 remains).

**F08 -- wrong initial condition.** `_battery_temp_traj` correctly stores
each drive's coolant/oil END temperature alongside its peak (matching the
convention `_heat_soak_carryover` already used correctly for the battery
pack: `t_end = ta['pm_end']`). But `_linked_adjacent_drive_table` never
extracted the previous drive's end temperature into its per-pair table at
all -- only the peak (`prevPeakCoolantC`/`prevPeakOilC`) -- and
`_carryover_thermal_decay` was called with that peak as the pre-soak
reference. Cooling after parking begins wherever the vehicle actually was
when the drive ended, not at whatever peak it reached earlier mid-drive;
using the peak overstates the initial excess and therefore the fitted
cooling time constant.

**Fix.** Added `prevEndCoolantC`/`prevEndOilC` (from `traj[...]
['coolant_end']`/`['oil_end']`, already computed but previously unused
here) to `_linked_adjacent_drive_table`'s output, and pointed both
`_carryover_thermal_decay` call sites at them instead of the peak columns.
Reproduces the audit's own independent recomputation of the same fit
structure, exactly:

| | prior peak (shipped) | prior end (corrected) | audit's own check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coolant effective cooling τ | 9.51 h, n=226 | **9.93 h**, n=226 | 9.9286 h (+4.41%) |
| Oil effective cooling τ | 8.83 h, n=218 | **9.16 h**, n=218 | 9.1618 h (+3.71%) |

`nfit` is unchanged for both channels -- the fix changes which TEMPERATURE
VALUE is used as the pre-soak reference, not which pairs have valid data.
`interDriveCarryover.regressionModel` (arrival-temperature ->
time-to-first-start) uses `arrivalPmC`, not the peak/end columns, so it is
untouched by this fix.

**Second half of F08's required response ("assess parking-ambient
uncertainty") implemented as** a new `parkingAmbientSensitivity` field on
each channel: refits tau after shifting the ambient reference by ±3°C
(applied to both the initial and residual excess, since both reference the
same following-drive driving-time ambient reading -- the actual parked
environment is unmeasured, the same caveat `_heat_soak_carryover` already
discloses for the pack). Coolant τ ranges ~7.9-11.6 h and oil ~7.4-10.4 h
across that perturbation -- disclosed as an approximate sensitivity band,
not a formal error propagation, and now stated directly in the dashboard
prose (previously this uncertainty was only qualitatively caveated for the
pack fit, not quantified for coolant/oil at all).

**Corpus reproduction.** Refactored `_linked_adjacent_drive_table` with an
optional `first_window_by_file` bypass parameter (same testability pattern
as F05/F06/F07), and ran a combined chunked raw extraction (320 drives,
two runs) computing both the `_battery_temp_traj`-equivalent per-file
record and the `_first_window_engine_metrics`-equivalent record in a
single read pass per file, avoiding a second raw pass for the same data.
Confirmed the reconstructed join table matches the shipped `nPairs=309`
exactly before refitting.

**Validation.** `py_compile` clean; function-signature diff against the
pre-M231 baseline shows only this session's four milestones' intentional
additions (M231 F05, M232 F06/F21, M233 F07, M234 F08's new `_fit_tau`
helper and the `first_window_by_file` parameter) and nothing else. JSX
prose binds dynamically to `TD.coolant.tau`/`TD.oil.tau` (no hardcoded
literals needed fixing) and was extended with the new sensitivity-band
text; caught and fixed a display-order bug in that addition (the two
offsets were shown high-to-low, read like a typo) before finalizing.
`build_html.js` gates clean (129/129 corpusHash match). `validate_jsdom.js`
9/9 tabs, 52 buttons, 0 console errors, 0 semantic warnings; rendered-text
spot-check confirms "τ ≈ 9.93 h (coolant) and 9.16 h (oil)" and the
ascending-order sensitivity band both render correctly. Isolation-diffed
the re-splice: exactly 23 changed leaves, all inside `interDriveCarryover`
and its `_artifactStamps` entry. T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS.

**Remaining audit scope.** F09 (provenance-stamp freshness) is the last
open P1 item -- next in audit priority order. F02 remains blocked (no raw
archive). The unprioritized Batch-A/B set (F12-F20, F23-F33) remains
triaged but not yet sequenced or implemented.

## M233 (2026-09-06) — Audit P1: F07 signed daily-peak bug + daily-clustering refit

Closes the third **P1** item in audit priority order. F05 (START detector)
and F06 (charging-frontier population), plus F06's code-level prerequisite
F21, were closed in M231/M232; F08 (thermal-boundary condition) and F09
(provenance-stamp freshness) remain -- see "remaining scope" below.

**F07 -- signed peak feature.** `_daily_fingerprints`'s `peakPowerKw`
was `max(peak_discharge_kw, peak_charge_kw)` taken directly over the two
signed columns. `peak_charge_kw` is stored NEGATIVE in the master, so a
plain `max()` silently discarded any charging peak on any day that also
had a positive discharge peak -- which is nearly every day. Verified
against the audit's own independent positive-distance daily aggregation:
this missed a larger-magnitude charging peak on 48 of 76 days, by as much
as 24.1 kW.

**Fix.** `peakPowerKw` is now `max(abs(discharge peak), abs(charge
peak))` -- the larger-magnitude peak regardless of sign. Preserved the two
signed components as new, separate informational fields
(`peakPowerDischargeKw`, `peakPowerChargeKw`) per the audit's own
suggestion ("preserve separate directional features if useful"); these
are NOT added to the k-means feature set (`feature_cols` is unchanged in
composition, only `peakPowerKw`'s values are corrected), so this fix does
not also silently expand what the clustering studies.

**Refit daily clustering (per the audit's own required response: "Use
absolute peak power; refit daily clustering").** Since 48 of 76 days'
`peakPowerKw` values changed, and this feature enters the z-scored
k-means feature space directly, the existing (unmodified) clustering
pipeline was re-run on the corrected features -- not redesigned; only its
input changed. Result changed materially:

| | pre-F07 (shipped) | post-F07 |
|---|---|---|
| best k | 2 | 3 |
| silhouette | 0.2842 | 0.3262 |
| day-bootstrap median ARI | 0.8596 | 0.6274 |
| ARI 95% CI | [0.029, 1.0] | [0.25, 1.0] |
| stable (>=0.4 threshold) | yes | yes |

Both are audit-matching reproductions of the SAME underlying tension the
audit flagged (F30/F31, not fixed in this milestone): the shipped result
was itself only a replay of a feature bug, not a validated finding, so

## M232 (2026-09-06) — Audit P1: F21 speed-fallback bug + F06 charging-frontier population mismatch

Closes the second **P1** item in audit priority order (F06), plus its
direct code-level prerequisite F21 (same `_hr_grid` function).

**F21 -- speed-fallback bug.** `_hr_grid()` built its selected-column map
(`cols`) from `fr.columns` BEFORE calling `_apply_speed_priority()`. On any
drive where the native VCM speed column was entirely ABSENT (not merely
sparse) and only the OBD-generic fallback existed, `_apply_speed_priority`
creates the VCM-named column in place -- but `cols` had already been built
without it, so `'speed'` was silently omitted from the grid for that drive
entirely. Verified this is not a corner case: **90 of 320 drives** (all of
the `obd_fallback`-speed-source population) have the VCM column completely
absent, not just under-populated -- every one of them was silently missing
speed data from every downstream `_hr_grid`-based computation. Fixed by
calling `_apply_speed_priority` first, then building `cols` from the
(now-corrected) column set; also added the target-torque channel (needed
for F06 below) and made `_hr_grid` return whether the fallback was used,
so callers can audit/report speed-source composition instead of losing it
silently.

**F06 -- charging-frontier population mismatch.** `_high_soc_regen`'s
population is 1 Hz samples with charge power in (1, 120) kW -- no gate on
engine state, braking torque, or deceleration. Calling this "regenerative
braking" was incorrect: reconstructed and verified against the audit's own
independent figure, of 205,882 SoC-valid charging samples (exact match to
the audit's count), 67.86% are engine-on (i.e. 32.14% engine-off, matching
the audit's own stated split) and 61.83% are non-decelerating (audit:
61.75% via their own independent reconstruction -- consistent given it is
their own separate speed-priority replay, not a replay of this code).

Also closed the audit's "second estimand mismatch": `highSocP95Kw` (30.79
kW) is the MEDIAN of two high-SoC bins' own p95 values, but the CI shown
alongside it (`topBinP95Boot`, [29.79, 31.82]) bootstrapped a DIFFERENT,
single-bin statistic -- point estimate and interval characterized
different aggregates. Added `highSocP95Boot`, which day-bootstraps the
IDENTICAL median-of-high-bins statistic (resampling days once per draw and
applying that same day-set to every pooled bin, preserving cross-bin
within-day correlation): CI [29.66, 31.7] -- now the same aggregate as the
point estimate it's paired with.

**Required response ("rename the population; use demand-controlled
regenerative subsets") implemented as:**
- Renamed "regen samples"/"regen ceiling"/"REGEN ENVELOPE" to "charging-
  power samples"/"charging ceiling"/"CHARGING-POWER ENVELOPE" throughout
  the JSON methodology text and dashboard prose (`xtrail_summary.jsx`);
  `nRegenSamples` -> `nChargingSamples`. The population composition
  (`engineOnSharePct`/`nonDeceleratingSharePct`) is now disclosed directly
  in a `populationCaveat` field and in the dashboard text, not left
  implicit.
- Added `demandControlledRegen`: a genuinely regen-restricted subset
  (engine off/idle [rpm<=300] & speed>3 km/h & instantaneous
  deceleration>0 & target motor torque<0 -- conditions under which a
  sample cannot plausibly be anything other than regenerative braking),
  computed with the same SoC bins and the same day-bootstrap protocol,
  n=39,589. Reproduces the audit's own descriptive sensitivity numbers
  EXACTLY: peak 37.39 kW at 63-66% SoC (audit: 37.389), high-SoC 34.14 kW
  averaged across the two high bins (audit: 34.1398), 8.7% reduction
  (audit: 8.69%) -- versus this envelope's own unfiltered 14.4% reduction,
  matching the audit's explicit released-vs-restricted comparison.
- `_high_soc_regen_covariates` (the existing decel-tercile-stratified
  covariate adjustment) shares `_hr_grid` and was silently affected by
  F21 on the same 90 drives (`entrySpeedKmh`/`decelRateKmhPerS` were
  NaN for those drives' samples, silently excluding them from every
  decel-intensity stratum). Re-ran with the F21 fix: `declineByStratum`
  values shift by roughly 0.4-1.5 kW per cell (e.g. low-band high-SoC p95
  26.62 -> 25.62 kW); `declineSurvivesAdjustment` remains TRUE in both
  cases -- the qualitative conclusion is robust to the fix, but the
  reported per-stratum figures were measurably stale before it.

**Corpus reproduction (full 320-drive raw pass, chunked across two runs
per drive-count, twice -- once for `_high_soc_regen`, once for the
covariates extraction -- owing to the per-command time budget).**
`_high_soc_regen` and `_high_soc_regen_covariates` were refactored into a
per-drive extraction loop plus a pure `_high_soc_regen_aggregate()` /
`_high_soc_regen_covariates_aggregate()` function, so the (expensive,
raw-file-reading) extraction and the (cheap, deterministic) aggregation
can be run and verified independently -- the aggregation functions were
exercised directly against the corpus-wide extracted arrays to confirm the
numbers above before splicing.

**Validation.** `py_compile` clean; function-signature diff against
pre-M232 `compute_summary_arrays.py` shows exactly the new/modified
functions this commit intentionally adds (`_high_soc_regen_aggregate`,
`_high_soc_regen_covariates_aggregate`, the widened `dayboot_p95`, the new
`dayboot_median_of_bins_p95`, the new nested `_envelope` helper) and
nothing else -- zero unintended drift. JSX transpiles cleanly.
`build_html.js` gates clean (129/129 corpusHash match). `validate_jsdom.js`
9/9 tabs, 52 buttons, 0 console errors, 0 semantic warnings; targeted
render check confirms the corrected CI, population caveat, and
demand-controlled subset all render with live, consistent figures.
Isolation-diffed the full re-splice: exactly 220 changed leaves, all
inside `highSocRegen` and its `_artifactStamps` entry -- nothing else in
the 133-key payload moved. T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS.
