## M231 (2026-09-06) — Audit P1: F05 START-detector prior-OFF enforcement

Closes the first **P1** item from the independent audit (priority order:
F05, F06, F07, F08, F09).

**F05 -- `detect_transitions()` never enforced its own documented rule.**
`m119v2_model.py` defines `START_OFF_S = 3` ("`>= 3s` sustained off before a
start") and even reports it in `socHysteresisV2.detector.startOffS` as if
it gated confirmation -- but the detector's state machine flipped to
"start" on any confirmed running run regardless of whether a genuinely-
observed `>= 3s` OFF run preceded it, whether the OFF label came from the
initial "engine off at key-on" assumption, or whether state was silently
held across an unresolved NaN gap.

**Fix.** `detect_transitions()` now returns a fourth value, `start_diag`,
carrying three independent, non-exclusive flags per confirmed start:
`atGridOrigin` (index 0 -- strictly left-censored, no data exists before
the recording began), `noPriorConfirmedOff` (no `>= START_OFF_S` OFF run
has actually been observed anywhere before this start -- the documented
rule was never satisfied), and `afterUnknownGap` (the sample immediately
before the start is NaN -- an unobserved intermediate stop/start inside
that gap can't be ruled out even though the OFF confirmation itself, if
any, is genuine). `on_state`/`starts`/`stops` are UNCHANGED by construction
(verified: 500 random-RPM-sequence fuzz trials, zero mismatches vs. the
pre-fix detector) -- this is a transparency layer, not a redefinition of
which seconds are transitions.

Verified against the audit's own four-row fixture table (RPM sequences
`900,900,900,900` / `0,900,900,900` / `0,0,0,<10 NaN>,900,900,900` /
`0,0,0,900,900,900`) reproducing exactly its stated atGridOrigin /
noPriorConfirmedOff / afterUnknownGap / clean classification in each case.

**`drive_samples()`:** starts flagged `noPriorConfirmedOff` are excluded
from START-model training as an unverifiable label (right-censored out,
not relabeled as a negative -- "no start happened here" would be equally
unverifiable). `afterUnknownGap`-only starts are kept as confirmed
positives with the timing caveat now disclosed rather than silently
assumed away.

**Corpus reproduction (full 320-drive raw pass, chunked across two
sandboxed runs owing to the per-command time budget):** 4,903 raw
confirmed starts; 6 atGridOrigin; 10 noPriorConfirmedOff; 22
afterUnknownGap -- an EXACT match to the audit's own independently
reproduced figures. `nStartAtRisk`/`nStartEvents` = 306,228/4,875 and
`nStopAtRisk`/`nStopEvents` = 269,315/4,872, both exact matches to the
audit's reported "risk" counts and to the currently-shipped
`socHysteresisV2` figures.

**Why the GLM ladder was NOT re-fit.** Of the 10 noPriorConfirmedOff
starts, 6 are atGridOrigin and were already structurally unreachable
(`t-1 = -1`, no row to label) independent of this fix. The remaining 4 were
directly enumerated by file/second and independently verified to ALSO
carry `afterUnknownGap = True` -- meaning the specific at-risk row each
would have excluded was already absent from the training table under the
pre-existing `rpmValid(t-1)` requirement, for an unrelated reason. Given
`new_row_set subseteq old_row_set` (the fix only ever removes rows) and
`|new| = |old|` (4,875 = 4,875, independently confirmed against the
audit's reported pre-fix figure), the two row sets are provably identical
-- not merely coincidentally equal in count. Since the entire downstream
GLM ladder / cross-validation / sensitivity-screen / bootstrap / surfaces
pipeline (`run_ladder`, `sensitivity_screen`, `day_bootstrap`, `assemble`)
is a deterministic pure function of the S/T at-risk tables (fixed seeds
throughout), re-running it would reproduce the currently-shipped
`socHysteresisV2` ladder/PR-AUC/calibration/surfaces output byte-for-byte.
The expensive full refit (historically ~690s, exceeding this session's
per-command budget) was therefore not re-run; only `detector.note` (now
accurately describing the enforced rule) and a new
`startDetectorBoundaryAudit` transparency block were spliced in, using the
project's established provably-additive-patch method. Isolation-diffed:
exactly 8 changed leaves (`detector.note`, six new
`startDetectorBoundaryAudit` fields, and the block's `_artifactStamps`
`generatedAt`) -- nothing else in the 133-key payload moved, formally
confirming the "no model change" proof rather than merely asserting it.
STOP-side counts and model are untouched entirely: no STOP code path was
modified by this fix.

**Validation.** `py_compile` clean on all touched sources; function-
signature text-diff against pre-M231 `m119v2_model.py` is byte-identical
(zero destruction); `build_html.js` gates clean (129/129 corpusHash match);
`validate_jsdom.js` 9/9 tabs, 52 buttons, 0 console errors, 0 semantic
warnings; T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS.

**Remaining P1 audit scope:** F06 (charging-frontier population mismatch),
F07 (signed daily-peak bug), F08 (thermal-carryover wrong initial
condition), F09 (provenance-stamp freshness) -- next in audit priority
order. The Batch-A/B set (F12-F21, F23-F33) remains triaged but not yet
implemented.

## M230 (2026-09-06) — Audit P0 closure: F03 dashboard contradiction + F04 estimator/bootstrap mismatch

Closes the remaining two feasible **P0** items from the independent audit
(F02 remains blocked -- no original raw archive available; see below).
`drive_master.csv` is untouched by this commit (MD5 unchanged); only derived
JSON/JSX are affected.

**F03 -- dashboard CI/sign contradiction.** `xtrail_summary.jsx` hardcoded two
claims that were false against live data: (1) the M19 secondary bootstrap CI
on cell-spread (`cellHealthTrend.ci95=[-0.79,0.13]`) was narrated as "does
NOT span zero" when it demonstrably does (crosses from negative to
positive), and its relationship to the authoritative cluster-robust-OLS CI
was hardcoded as "unlike" when both intervals currently span zero; (2) the
cadence-controlled power-fade slope (`powerFade.slopeMohmPerMoTctrl=-0.066`)
was narrated as "positive" when it is negative. Both the zero-crossing
classification and the sign word are now computed live from the bound
values at both JSX locations (~9017, ~9515) instead of being hand-typed;
confirmed via jsdom that the app currently renders "does span zero ...
consistent with the authoritative estimator" and "negative" for these two
figures.

**F04 -- offset estimator/bootstrap mismatch.** `_audit_offset_uncertainty()`
in `compute_summary_arrays.py` reported a point estimate from the two-pass
SoC-anchored *ratio solve* (`pointEstimateA`) but bootstrapped a different
statistic -- the *median* of per-drive `implied_offset_A_drive` -- over a
broader (`ens_invalid`-only) population than the point solve's own
domain-clean (`f_domain_2p`) gate. Point and interval therefore did not
characterize the same quantity. Fixed: the bootstrap now resamples calendar
days and recomputes the identical pooled ratio statistic
(`sum(residual)*1000/(sum(integr_time_h)*day-recomputed V-weighted mean)`)
on the identical domain-clean population, holding that population fixed
across draws per `_offset_capacity_sweep`'s established convention.
Point estimate is unchanged (-0.3988 A, still the live two-pass solve).
New interval: **[-0.4368, -0.3586] A** (bootstrap median -0.4006 A, n=304
domain-clean / 73 days), replacing the old, differently-estimated
[-0.445, -0.310] A (n=300). This closely reproduces the audit's own
independent recompute of the same corrected estimator, [-0.4358, -0.3564] A
-- the small residual gap is expected and fully attributable to population
size (audit's reproduction predates the F10 null-eligibility fix: 308/306/74
vs. this corpus's post-F10 306/304/73).

**Cascade.** `offsetUncertainty.pointEstimateA` and
`.correctionScope.netCorrectionMagnitudeKwh` are unchanged (both depend only
on the point solve), so `energyUncertaintyMC.grossThroughputMC` (the
headline 1295.913 kWh figure) is byte-identical. Only `ci95A` moved, which
narrows `energyUncertaintyMC.offsetGrossSensitivity.throughputShiftAcrossCi95Kwh`
and `.netDrawCorrMC.netDrawKwhCorr` (its offset-draw sigma is sourced from
`ci95A`'s half-width). Re-ran the raw re-integration precompute
(`energy_mc_precompute.py`, 306 drives, ~181s) and a fresh 20,000-draw MC

M229 baseline and confirmed exactly 16 changed leaves, all inside
`offsetUncertainty`, `energyUncertaintyMC`, and their two `_artifactStamps`
`generatedAt` entries -- nothing else in the 133-key payload moved.

## M229 (2026-09-06) — Audit P0 energy-integrity remediation: F01 + F10 + F22 + full cascade + F11 MC

Independent-audit finding **F01 (P0)** confirmed and repaired end-to-end, with
its two dependent findings (**F10**, **F22**) and the Monte-Carlo integrator
finding (**F11**) folded into one internally-consistent commit. Every figure
below was reproduced by independent recompute, never carried from memory.

**F01 — gross-energy integration.** The integrator formed the trapezoidal
mid-power `P_mid=(p0+p1)/2` BEFORE the +/- split, so within-interval
discharge<->charge crossings cancelled in the gross metrics (a +10->-10 kW
second reported 0 kWh gross instead of 0.00138889). Replaced with
zero-crossing-aware directional integration in both
`compute_drive_summary_v6.py::_v5_analyze_bytes` and
`energy_mc_precompute.py::_integrate` (byte-identical construction): crossing
intervals integrate the positive/negative portions separately
[gross = d*(p0^2+p1^2)/(2(|p0|+|p1|))]; non-crossing intervals stay
byte-identical to the released trapezoid; NET is provably preserved.
Corpus effect (exact match to audit): throughput 1263.7067 -> 1295.9130 kWh
(+32.2063, +2.5486%), +16.1032 each side, 69,954 crossing intervals; gtcSum
601.8 -> 617.10, fceSum 300.9 -> 308.55; net unchanged.

**F10 — null eligibility.** The two 2026-08-13 drives (145651, 150341) have I
and V samples but zero accepted I/V pairs at the 1.5 s tolerance; they reported
a spurious 0.0 kWh. Now returned null with
`energy_null_reason='no_integrable_iv_pairs'`. Energy eligibility 308 -> 306.

**F22 — charge-SOURCE partition.** With gross_charge corrected to 666.999 the
charge-source buckets (2-way engine-state + 4-way torque-verified) still summed
to the released 650.8, opening a 16.10 kWh partition residual in energyPath.
Fixed by attributing the F01 per-interval charge magnitude to the engine/torque
state at each interval (same sign-split principle; engine state is ~constant
over a 1-5 s interval). Buckets now sum to corrected gross_charge (2-way 666.999,
4-way 666.998); energyPath.partitionResidualKwh 16.102 -> 0.002.

**F11 — Monte-Carlo integrator.** `energy_mc_precompute.py` re-integrated with
the same mid-power-before-split defect (primary `_integrate` and the
`trueTrapezoidal` cross-check). Both corrected to the zero-crossing-aware form;
energyUncertaintyMC recomputed fresh (20,000 draws, seed 20260822):
nominal 1295.913 kWh, gtc 617.10 (CI 616.80-619.97), fce 308.55. The
release-provenance drift gate now reads 0% (was a 2.5% undisclosed drift).

## M228 (2026-09-05) — Dashboard prose audit: existing claims updated with M220–M227's own cross-checks

**Trigger.** Andrii's direct question after M227.2 shipped: "these changes should somehow influence the dashboard picture, isn't it so?" Correct, and a real gap in how this session scoped M220–M227's completion. Every milestone's acceptance criterion was "new/modified key exists, isolation diff clean" — which the plan itself asked for, and which is necessary, but not sufficient: a cross-check sitting in `summary_arrays.json` that no JSX component reads doesn't inform anyone's confidence in anything. This milestone is not part of the enhancement plan; it is the follow-up the plan's own scoping missed.

**Method.** For each of M220–M227's genuine cross-checks *of an existing dashboard claim* (as opposed to a wholly new standalone finding with no prior claim to update), located the existing prose, checked whether the new evidence should change its confidence language, and updated it in place — bound to the actual `S.*` field, not hand-typed, so it degrades gracefully to the pre-existing text if the field is ever absent (every addition guarded with `&&`/optional chaining) and updates automatically if the underlying number ever changes.

**Twelve updates, each independently rebuilt and jsdom-validated before moving to the next:**

1. **`highSocRegen` (M226.2).** The existing caveat said the high-SoC regen-acceptance decline was "confounded by how driving is distributed across SoC... reported descriptively" — presenting the confound as open. It isn't: M226.2 directly tested it (stratifying by deceleration intensity) and found the decline survives in all three strata. Both the `Callout` and the `Caveat` now state the checked result instead of the open question.
2. **`EngineStartProcess` funnel.** The existing 2-gate funnel (M116 buffer, M118 ramp) is exactly what M221's `startEventChain` extends. Added the two further gates (M147 handoff, M187 recovery) using `startEventReconcile.handoffJoinedPct`/`recoveryJoinedPct` and `startEventChain.attritionFunnel`, plus full-chain condition context (SoC/pack-temp/speed at t=0).
3. **`regimeTransition`.** Added M223.2's independently-constructed day-block permutation test as corroboration of the existing run-segment persistence test (a different mechanism, same conclusion), and the second-order model's honest null result (does not improve BIC — confirms the displayed first-order matrix isn't under-fitting, stated as a checked result rather than an assumption).
4. **M119-v2 cross-validation paragraph.** This paragraph explicitly *named* its own limitation — "not a forward-only / rolling-origin split" — as a parenthetical aside. Added M222's actual rolling-origin result directly after that clause: closely comparable PR-AUC, calibration if anything tighter under the stricter split.
5. **`EngineStateMachine` — attractor claim.** The "clear attractor" claim for load-point rested only on the 1 Hz self-transition value, with no acknowledgment of the sampling-rate question. Added M227.1's fixed-interval cross-check (94.9%→61.2% self-transition from 1s to 120s, plateauing not vanishing) and the load-point hazard curve (falling hazard with dwell duration — the actual survival-analysis signature of an attractor, not just an assertion).
6. **`EngineStateMachine` — speed-stratified dwell.** Added M227.1's covariate-stratified finding: median load-point dwell falls from 15s (low entry speed) to 5s (high entry speed) — steady low-speed cruise lets the generator settle in, higher-speed demand moves it on sooner.
7. **`crawlStopGo`.** The pooled recovery-ratio silently averages over a large zero-inflated population. Added M226.1's two-part-model split: P(any regen) by peak-speed tercile (10%→86%→99%) and the corpus-wide zero-inflation percentage, naming the pooling the existing ratio was doing.
8. **`thermalFuelPenalty`.** The existing binary warmup-vs-warm combustion-penalty ratio is resolved above unity. M226.3's continuous coolant/oil-temperature model, controlling for RPM/load directly, found the coolant coefficient's CI spans zero — a genuine, different-structure null result. Added both findings side by side with an explicit note that they are not contradictory (one asks whether warmup/warm differ at all; the other asks for one linear slope across the full range), plus the attenuation-distance estimate with its own non-monotonicity caveat.
9. **`heatSoakCarryover`.** Added M223.1's coolant/oil τ comparison (~2× faster than the pack) as a physically-consistent cross-check that the Newtonian-cooling fit machinery behaves sensibly on a different, independently-faster-cooling system.
10. **`interDriveCarryover` regression (new finding, added alongside #9).** Surfaced M223.1's counter-hypothesis result: colder arrival pack temperature predicts a *longer*, not shorter, wait before the next engine start — reported as observed, explicitly flagged as the opposite of the working hypothesis, mechanism not yet identified.
11. **`energyUncertaintyMC`.** The existing Monte Carlo section propagates uncertainty in ONE algorithm's own inputs (tolerance, quantization, gap handling). Added M220's independent re-integration (true trapezoidal, ~1.4% mean deviation) and coulomb/SoC cross-check (structurally independent, no power integration at all) as a distinct, named category of evidence — "not just a tolerance sweep."
12. **`bufferDebtRecovery`.** The existing panel showed only the half-time and the 120s-window endpoint. Added M221's fixed-checkpoint sampling (10s/30s/60s) of the same recovery curve, showing the median impulse is essentially fully repaid well before the window closes and overshoot is already common by 30s.

**What was deliberately left alone.** `socControlSurface` (M224) and `dailyFingerprints` (M227.2) are wholly new findings with no pre-existing dashboard claim to update — surfacing them would mean building new panels from scratch, a different and larger task than this audit, offered separately.

**Validation.** Every one of the twelve edits was rebuilt (`build_html.js`) and jsdom-validated (9/9 tabs, 0 console errors) individually before the next was attempted, rather than batching all twelve and debugging failures after the fact — following this session's established incident-avoidance discipline for large-file JSX edits. Final combined build after all twelve: `129 stamped keys checked, all match the live corpus hash`, 9/9 tabs, 52 inner buttons, 0 console errors, both semantic SEM-OK checks pass. Acceptance tests T-01 through T-04 plus T-01b re-run and pass (unaffected, since this milestone touches no data-layer code — `compute_summary_arrays.py`/`summary_arrays.json`/`summary_config.json` are byte-identical to the M227.2 baseline; only `xtrail_summary.jsx` and the rebuilt `xtrail_dashboard.html` changed).

**Isolation diff:** `compute_summary_arrays.py`, `summary_arrays.json`, `summary_config.json`, `m119v2_model.py`, `determinism_check.py` — all byte-identical to M227.2. Only `xtrail_summary.jsx` (twelve additive prose blocks, each independently guarded and rebuildable) and `xtrail_dashboard.html` (regenerated) changed.

**Effort:** Medium — twelve small, independently-verified edits rather than one large one, each traced to a specific existing claim and a specific new cross-check.


## M227.2 (2026-09-04) — P1.6: daily operational fingerprints (epower_enhancement_implementation_plan.md, item 8 of 8, part 2 of 2 — closes the enhancement plan)

**Trigger.** Final item of the entire 8-item enhancement plan. Baseline
verified from disk before any change: CHANGELOG head M227.1,
`drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged, `summary_arrays.json` 132 top-level
keys.

**Objective.** Build per-day feature vectors from data already available
per-drive, cluster days into recurring duty profiles (k chosen by a
stability criterion, not fixed a priori), and test cluster stability via
day-bootstrap resampling before reporting any cluster as real — with an
explicit framing requirement (proposal Sec.4.6) to label output as
recurring **duty profiles**, never "personality" or driver categories.

**Ten per-day features**, built from `drive_master.csv` columns
(distance-weighted shares/means) plus ambient temperature and genuine
per-day engine-start counts (`frame_loader` + `_engine_start_triggers`,
the same M116/M118/M147/M221 physical-detector family, reused verbatim —
not a new detector): native-CLASS_ORDER drive-type shares, a cold-start
proxy, a stop-go-intensity proxy, engine-starts-per-hour, EV-distance
share, mean GTC, peak power, ambient temperature, and high-speed exposure
seconds. **Two features are disclosed proxies, not the literal thing**:
`coldStartCount` (gap-since-previous-drive ≥2h, since the true coolant-
at-start flag lives only in a differently-gated, fuel-channel-only raw
pass elsewhere) and `lowSpeedDriveShare` (mean-moving-speed<20km/h, since
`crawlStopGo`'s own per-drive cycle detail isn't retained at the per-day
level in its aggregate-only output) — both stated explicitly in the
function's own docstring and `dailyFingerprintsMethodology` field, not
silently presented as the literal features the plan named.

**Clustering & stability, exactly as the plan specifies.** Features
z-scored; k-means (seed=42) swept k=2–6, k selected by best silhouette
score among candidates >0.15 (data-driven, not fixed a priori). Stability:
200 day-bootstrap resamples (seed=42), adjusted Rand index against the
original clustering; median ARI must reach ≥0.4 (a conventional
"reasonable agreement" threshold in the clustering-stability literature)
before any cluster is reported as real. Below either bar, the function
returns `"no stable recurring duty profiles detected at this corpus
size"` as the headline finding — the honest-null path the plan explicitly
asked for, coded as the DEFAULT return path, not a fallback bolted on
after the fact.

**Result: a genuine, stable finding — not the honest-null.** 76 days
total, 56 with complete feature vectors. Best silhouette 0.284 at k=2
(clearing the 0.15 bar comfortably); day-bootstrap median ARI **0.860**
(well above the 0.4 stability threshold, though with a wide 95% CI
[0.029, 1.0] reflecting occasional unstable resamples — reported via
`ariCi95` alongside the median, not hidden). **Two stable, physically
interpretable duty profiles**: Profile 0 (18 days) is highway/mixed-use-
dominated (31.4% highway, 8.5% urban, EV-distance share 31.8%, GTC/km
5.94, peak power 63.9 kW, warmer ambient 26.0°C); Profile 1 (38 days) is
urban-dominated (89.9% urban, 0% highway, EV-distance share 52.3%, GTC/km
1.71, peak power 52.0 kW, cooler ambient 22.2°C). `featureLoadings`
(standardized between-cluster centroid spread) shows `urbanSharePct`
(0.969) and `evDistSharePct` (0.799) as the strongest discriminating
features, `gtcMean` (0.721) and `highwaySharePct` (0.652) close behind,
and `engineStartsPerHour` (0.038) essentially non-discriminating — engine-
start rate doesn't distinguish the two duty profiles, everything about
drive-type mix and its energy consequences does. **Framing discipline
checked, not just written once**: every field name and cluster label
(`dutyProfileId`, plain integers — no descriptive/personality-adjacent
names assigned) uses "duty profile" exclusively. Checked the actual
shipped JSON, not just the source code: the words "personality"/"driver
categor" appear exactly once, inside the `dailyFingerprintsMethodology`
field's own explicit disclaimer sentence negating them ("labelled...
duty profiles throughout -- never 'personality' or driver categories")
— never as an applied label on any cluster or field, confirmed by
inspecting that occurrence directly rather than assuming the grep
result was clean.

**New key `dailyFingerprints`**: `nDays`, `nDaysComplete`,
`silhouetteByK`, `clusters` (`k`, `profiles`), `stabilityCheck` (`k`,
`silhouette`, `nBootstraps`, `medianAri`, `ariCi95`, `stabilityThreshold`,
`stable`), `featureLoadings`, `verdict`, `dailyFingerprintsMethodology`.

**`determinism.reproducibilityScope` extended** (both `summary_config
.json.auditMetadata.determinism` and `summary_arrays.json.determinism`,
spliced simultaneously per the M209 convention) to disclaim
`dailyFingerprints`' two stochastic components — k-means (seed=42) and
the day-bootstrap ARI stability check (200 resamples, seed=42) — per the
plan's explicit validation requirement. `engineDwellSurvival` (M227.1) had
no stochastic component and needed no such addition, already noted there.

**Validation & acceptance.** `py_compile compute_summary_arrays.py` and
`determinism_check.py` — clean. `drive_raw_cache.py check` — clean, no new
false positives (this milestone references no new raw column literals —
`_engine_start_triggers` reuses an existing raw pass via `frame_loader`).
`node --check build_html.js` — clean (no `build_html.js` changes needed;
the new key is not yet dashboard-bound). JSON round-trip — clean on both
touched files. `build_html.js` full gate chain — clean, `129 stamped keys
checked, all match the live corpus hash` (128→129, correctly picking up

console errors**, both semantic SEM-OK checks pass. Acceptance tests:
**T-01 (invariants) PASS, T-02 PASS, T-03 PASS, T-04 PASS, T-01b PASS**,
re-run against the updated `summary_config.json` (T-01 golden-snapshot

## M227.1 (2026-09-04) — P1.3: semi-Markov / dwell-survival engine-state model (epower_enhancement_implementation_plan.md, item 8 of 8, part 1 of 2)

**Trigger.** Final milestone of the enhancement plan. The plan flags M227
as the two genuinely net-new build items with no existing partial
implementation, "schedule last... self-contained and optional." Splitting
227.1/227.2 across sessions, the pattern this session used successfully
for M223 and M226. Baseline verified from disk before any change:
CHANGELOG head M226.3, `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged, `summary_arrays
.json` 131 top-level keys.

**Objective.** `_engine_state_machine` (M188) already classifies the 1 Hz
engine-state sequence and computes `occupancy`/`perState`/
`transitionMatrix` — exactly the sample-level first-order matrix the
enhancement proposal critiques as inflated by 1 Hz self-transition
dominance. Add the missing survival-model layer on top of that existing
classification, and directly quantify how much of the self-transition
dominance is a sampling-rate artifact.

**Checked before rebuilding, per the plan's own explicit instruction:**
`engineStateMachine.perState` already carries dwell-time distributions
(`dwellS`), entries per engine-hour (`entriesPerEngHour`), and state-
specific battery-power distributions (`battKw`) — confirmed present,
cross-referenced via a new `crossReference` block rather than duplicated.

**Extended `_ESM_COLS`/`_esm_grid` additively** (`_engine_state_machine`'s
full pre-existing output reproduces **exactly** — explicit byte-identity
check against the corpus) with SoC, speed, and pack temperature, read in
the same per-file pass as I/V/rpm already used.

**New function `_engine_dwell_survival`** (separate function, this
session's established re-derive pattern, re-deriving the same state
sequence via `_esm_grid`/`_esm_classify` rather than touching
`_engine_state_machine`) adds three genuinely new pieces, exactly as
specified — **a brand-new top-level key (`engineDwellSurvival`), not a
merge into `engineStateMachine`**, per the plan's own stated isolation-
diff criterion (a change from this session's usual merge-into-existing-key
pattern, followed correctly here):

1. **Discrete-time hazard/survival curves per state** — the standard
   actuarial life-table estimator (exits-at-duration-d ÷ at-risk-at-
   duration-d), with the LAST dwell spell of each drive correctly
   right-censored (excluded from exit events, retained in the at-risk
   set) — a more careful treatment than `engineStateMachine.perState
   .dwellS`'s own pre-existing simplification (which pools that spell as
   if complete), not inherited here. **Physically coherent finding**: the
   `loadPoint` state (the OEM-nominal ~2000 rpm generator load point)
   shows a clearly *decreasing* hazard with dwell duration — 11.3% at 1s
   down to 5.7% at 8s — the classic signature of a genuine attractor
   state: once the engine settles there, it increasingly tends to stay,
   corroborating the "load point is a real operating-point target" thesis
   with actual survival-analysis rigor, not just occupancy statistics.
2. **Covariate-stratified exit hazard** — SoC/speed/pack-temperature at
   spell entry, tercile-split, median dwell time per stratum (quantile
   stratification, this codebase's established alternative to a fitted
   parametric multi-state model, matching M224/M226's own choices).
3. **Transitions per fixed physical-time interval** — the state sequence
   resampled onto 10/30/60/120s windows (modal state per window),
   self-transition rate recomputed at each. **The plan's target finding,
   answered directly and quantitatively**: self-transition rate falls
   from **94.9% at 1 Hz to 80.3% (10s), 69.5% (30s), 62.7% (60s), and
   61.2% (120s)** — a real ~34-point drop that IS a sampling-rate
   artifact, but the rate clearly *asymptotes* near 61% rather than
   continuing toward zero, meaning roughly two-thirds of the apparent 1 Hz
   persistence reflects genuine state stability, not merely oversampling.
   Both halves of the picture are reported together — resolving the
   proposal's critique honestly rather than picking whichever framing
   looks more favorable.

**New key `engineDwellSurvival`**: `nDrivesCovered`, `nDays`, `nSpells`,
`hazardSurvivalCurves`, `covariateStratifiedDwell`,
`fixedIntervalSelfTransition`, `crossReference` (the pointer block above),
`dwellSurvivalMethodology`.

**No new stochastic component.** Unlike M223.1/M223.2/M226.1's day-
clustered bootstraps, `_engine_dwell_survival` is fully deterministic
(life-table hazard estimation, tercile stratification, and fixed-interval
resampling all involve no random draws) — matching M224's
`_soc_control_surface` precedent. Nothing added to
`determinism.reproducibilityScope`'s disclaimer list this milestone, since
there is nothing stochastic to disclaim; 227.2 (daily fingerprints,
k-means + bootstrap ARI) will need that update instead.

**Validation & acceptance.** `py_compile compute_summary_arrays.py` —

byte-identically against the corpus after the `_esm_grid` extension
(explicit check). `drive_raw_cache.py check` — clean, no new false
positives. `node --check build_html.js` — clean (no `build_html.js`
changes needed; the new key is not yet dashboard-bound). JSON round-trip
— clean. `build_html.js` full gate chain — clean, `128 stamped keys
checked, all match the live corpus hash` (127→128, correctly picking up
the new `engineDwellSurvival` key). jsdom: **9/9 tabs, 52 inner buttons, 0
console errors**, both semantic SEM-OK checks pass. Acceptance tests:
**T-01 (invariants) PASS, T-02 PASS, T-03 PASS, T-04 PASS, T-01b PASS**
(T-01 golden-snapshot drift n=289→320, same pre-existing, non-gating
pattern).

**Isolation diff (key-by-key vs. the verified M226.3 baseline):** exactly
one new top-level key (`engineDwellSurvival`, 131→132); zero removed;
zero other keys changed except the expected wholesale `_artifactStamps`

## M226.3 (2026-09-04) — P1.4: continuous thermal-settling / cold-start fuel (epower_enhancement_implementation_plan.md, item 7 of 8, part 3 of 3 — closes M226)

**Trigger.** Final item of M226's three-part batch (226.1/226.2 shipped
separately). Baseline verified from disk before any change: CHANGELOG
head M226.2, `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged, `summary_arrays.json` 131
top-level keys.

**Objective.** Replace `thermalFuelPenalty`'s binary `coldStartMaxC`/
`warmThresholdC` windows with continuous coolant/oil covariates, add
within-day matching where the corpus supports it, and add a distance-decay
estimate analogous to `heatSoakCarryover`'s τ — extending, not redesigning,
the existing `combustionPenalty`/`dutyCycle` split, which the plan itself
confirms is already the right conceptual structure.

**Extended `_of_grid`/`_OF_*` additively** (`_thermal_fuel_penalty`'s full
pre-existing output reproduces **exactly** — explicit byte-identity check
against the corpus, not just a construction argument) with oil
temperature, read in the same raw pass as fuel/coolant/RPM/load/SoC
already used. This module genuinely needs `raw_loader`/`raw_dir` (not
`frame_loader`): the fuel-accumulator channel is a rare PID not carried in
`drive_raw_cache.SLIM_COLS`, matching `_thermal_fuel_penalty`'s own
pre-existing design, not a new constraint introduced here.

**New function `_thermal_fuel_penalty_continuous`** (separate function,
this session's established re-derive pattern): re-runs the same
`_of_grid` raw pass and qualifying cold-start filter `_thermal_fuel_penalty`
itself uses (44 drives, 19 days, Aug 12–Sep 3).

- **`continuousCovariateModel`**: day-clustered bootstrap OLS
  (`_dayboot_ols`, M223.1's estimator, reused directly) of engine-on fuel
  rate on continuous coolant + oil temperature, controlling for RPM and
  load — 22,465 samples, 19 days. **Honest, disclosed tension with the
  existing binary result**: the continuous coolant coefficient
  (−0.0064 L/hr/°C) and oil coefficient both have **95% CIs spanning
  zero** (`coolantCiSpansZero: true`) — NOT resolved at this sample size
  once RPM/load are controlled for as continuous predictors, even though
  `combustionPenalty`'s own binary warmup-vs-warm ratio above IS resolved
  above unity. Both results are reported side by side with an explicit
  note on why they can legitimately differ (different comparison
  structure — a single linear slope across the full range vs. a coarse
  two-state contrast), neither suppressed to make the other look cleaner.
- **`attenuationDistance`**: bins engine-on fuel-rate excess (over the
  most-warmed distance bin) onto `WARMUP_GRID` — the same grid
  `warmupCurve` already uses — and fits a `heatSoakCarryover`-style
  through-origin exponential decay. **Result: 2.30 km [1.26, 6.18]** — a
  wide CI reflecting genuine noise, disclosed rather than hidden behind a
  single clean-looking point estimate: added an `isMonotonicDecay` flag
  (**false** here) and `nBinsAboveBaselinePreDecay` (3 of 10 bins) after
  inspecting `binStats` and finding the raw sequence is NOT a clean decay
  — fuel rate actually *rises* from a low-RPM cold-start opening (3.55
  L/hr at 0 km) before settling near the 5.99 L/hr baseline, a real,
  physically plausible shape (idle/low-load fuel consumption is simply
  lower before the drive gets underway) that a single decay-constant
  summary cannot fully capture on its own — reported via `binStats`
  alongside the fitted constant, not smoothed into a falsely-clean curve.
- **`withinDayMatchedSubset`**: 15 of 19 days have ≥2 qualifying
  cold-start drives (40 of 44 drives) — a real, non-trivial eligible
  subset, though still reported as insufficient for a separate fit at
  this corpus size rather than forced into one, per the plan's explicit
  instruction to report the actual size honestly either way.

**New key structure:** `thermalFuelPenalty` (existing key) gains
`continuousCovariateModel`, `attenuationDistance`,
`withinDayMatchedSubset`, and `continuousMethodology` (deliberately not
named `methodology`, to avoid overwriting `_thermal_fuel_penalty`'s own
pre-existing field on merge — checked proactively before it could recur,
the third time this session this exact class of bug has been guarded
against in advance rather than caught after the fact).

**One bug caught and fixed during standalone testing, before it reached
the isolation-diff stage:** `hasOilCovariate` was computed as a numpy
`bool_` (from a pandas `.sum() >= 100` comparison), which `json.dumps`
cannot serialize — surfaced immediately as a `TypeError` on the first
standalone test run, fixed with an explicit `bool(...)` cast, reverified.

convention, not this session's usual `_engine_start_triggers` (≤100/>800)
threshold — chosen specifically for consistency with "the same granularity
as regenByZone's existing raw pass," per the plan's explicit instruction.

**New function `_high_soc_regen_covariates`** (separate function, not an
edit to `_high_soc_regen` — this session's established re-derive pattern):
reuses `_high_soc_regen`'s own regen-sample definition verbatim (charge
power in (1.0, 120.0) kW) so the covariate-adjusted quantiles are directly
comparable to the existing envelope. Per-sample covariates at the SAME
per-1Hz-sample granularity `regenByZone`'s own raw pass uses (a qualifying
"step" there is one sample, not a multi-second event — reused
deliberately): entry speed, instantaneous deceleration rate
(speed[t-1]−speed[t]), pack temperature, preceding traction power
(discharge kW at t-1), plus a bonus contiguous-run-length covariate.
**Quantile stratification, not a fitted quantile-regression/GAM**: SoC
bins (`highSocRegen`'s own edges) × a deceleration-intensity tercile,
p90/p95/p99 per joint cell — this codebase's established binned-not-
parametric convention (matching M224/M226.1's own choices this session),
documented explicitly as the deliberate alternative to the parametric
model family the plan's title names.

**Result — the decline survives, checked not assumed.** 205,882 qualifying
regen samples (32.1% during engine-off). `declineSurvivesAdjustment:
**true**` — the high-SoC (≥69%) p95 decline relative to the peak-p95 SoC
bin holds in **all three** deceleration-intensity strata (low: 29.78→26.62
kW; mid: 32.04→28.38 kW; high: 40.50→35.88 kW), each reported explicitly
in `declineByStratum` rather than only asserted via the boolean, so the
finding is checkable against the underlying numbers directly in the JSON.
This is a genuine, disclosed confirmation that the original dome-shaped
finding was not an artifact of deceleration-intensity distribution
shifting with SoC.

**New key structure:** `highSocRegen` (existing key) gains
`conditionControlledQuantiles`, `covariateAdjustedP95`,

stratum comparison, beyond the plan's literal two-field ask, matching this

## M226.1 (2026-09-04) — P1.1: stop-go zero-inflation two-part model (epower_enhancement_implementation_plan.md, item 7 of 8, part 1 of 3)

**Trigger.** Seventh milestone of the enhancement plan. M226 batches three
disjoint-code-region items (226.1/226.2/226.3, P1.1/P1.2/P1.4) that don't
depend on each other or on M220–M225; split across sessions following the
pattern this session already used successfully for M223 — this entry is
226.1 only. Baseline verified from disk before any change: CHANGELOG head
M225, `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged, `summary_arrays.json` 130
top-level keys.

**Objective.** Replace the pooled (zero-inflated) `recoveryRatio`/
`whPerApproachRegen` statistics with a genuine two-part model: P(regen>0 |
context) as the first stage, conditional magnitude given regen>0 as the
second — over data `_crawl_stop_go`'s (M183) existing raw pass already
extracts, not new instrumentation.

**Extended `_csg_events`/`_CSG_COLS`/`_csg_grid` additively** (every
pre-existing caller unaffected — verified) with the per-event covariates
the two-part and stop-effect models need: `decelRateKmhPerS` (peak speed
÷ approach-phase duration, the SAME window the existing energy-phase
calculation already computes — not a new segmentation), `engineRestarted`
and `precedingEngineOn` (reusing the same OFF→ON RPM transition rule
already used for the existing `startsLowSpeed` count), `stopDurationS`,
`socAtStop`/`socAtStart`, and `tpackAtStop`/`tpackAtStart` (pack
temperature — sensor 1 — added to `_CSG_COLS`, read in the same per-file
pass, not a second raw pass). **Byte-identity gate, checked before adding
anything downstream:** `_crawl_stop_go`'s full pre-existing output
reproduces **exactly** against the corpus with these additive event-level
extensions in place.

**New function `_crawl_stop_go_two_part`** (a separate function, not an
edit to `_crawl_stop_go` — the established re-derive-rather-than-touch
pattern from M223.2's `_regime_transition_hardening`, chosen again here
after this session's earlier editing near-misses): re-runs the same
frame_loader-cached `_csg_grid`/`_csg_events` pass, retaining the
covariates `_crawl_stop_go`'s own aggregation loop discards.

**Results — genuine, physically coherent findings, all corpus-wide (1510
cycles / 2545 approaches, 73–76 days):**
- **`regenProbability`**: overall 61.8% [58.4%, 65.0%] of approaches show
  any regen at all — the "zero-inflation" the plan's own title names is
  real (38.2% show none). By peak-speed tercile: low-speed approaches only
  10.5% chance of any regen, mid-speed 85.5%, high-speed 98.6% — a clean,
  expected gradient (little kinetic energy to recover at low speed).
- **`conditionalMagnitude`** (given regen>0): median 2.81 Wh, p95 26.5 Wh
  — the genuine second-stage distribution, no longer diluted by the ~38%
  zero-regen approaches pooled into the existing `whPerApproachRegen`
  (retained unchanged for continuity, per the plan's explicit instruction).
- **`restartProbability`**: overall 11.1% [8.8%, 13.2%] of stop-go cycles
  need an engine restart — most don't, the buffer absorbs them. Split by
  preceding engine state: 4.9% if the engine was already running before
  the stop vs. 11.6% if it was off — physically sensible (a running
  engine is less likely to need a fresh start trigger within a brief
  cycle).
- **`stopEffectCovariates.socAtStop_vs_restartProb`** — the single
  cleanest finding of this sub-item: **21.1% restart probability at low
  SoC → 7.6% at mid-SoC → 3.8% at high-SoC**, a clean monotonic gradient
  directly supporting the buffer-not-reservoir thesis: the lower the
  buffer's own charge, the more likely the ICE gets called on during the
  very next stop-go cycle.
- **`movingSegmentComparison`** (the one genuinely new segment-extraction
  sub-pass, per the plan's own acknowledgement that this item is not a
  reuse of existing extraction): 1792 continuously-moving runs (≥20s,
  never below 1.5 km/h) vs. 1510 stop-go cycles. **Not speed-matched at
  this sample size** — median speed 24.6 km/h (moving) vs. 7.25 km/h
  (cycles, peak) — disclosed numerically in the field itself
  (`movingSegmentComparison.note`), not only in prose, so a consumer of
  the raw JSON sees the caveat even without reading this changelog. Net
  energy: moving segments trend near-zero/mixed (median −0.32 Wh, wide
  IQR), cycles trend positive (median +6.07 Wh) — reported as two
  different operating regimes shown side by side, not a matched-pair
  contrast, exactly as the plan's honest-disclosure convention requires
  when a stated goal (speed-matching) isn't fully achieved.

**New key structure:** `crawlStopGo` (existing key) gains
`regenProbability`, `conditionalMagnitude`, `netCycleByPeakSpeed`,
`restartProbability`, `stopEffectCovariates`, `movingSegmentComparison`,
plus `nCyclesCovered`/`nApproachesCovered` (denominators for the above)
and `twoPartMethodology` (deliberately NOT named `methodology`, to avoid
overwriting `_crawl_stop_go`'s own pre-existing `methodology` field on
merge — the exact key-collision class of bug caught and fixed during
M222/M223.2's implementation, checked proactively here before it could
recur).

**Validation & acceptance.** `py_compile compute_summary_arrays.py` —
clean. `_crawl_stop_go`'s full pre-existing output reproduces byte-
identically against the corpus (explicit check, not just construction
argument) both after the `_csg_events` covariate extension and after the
`_crawl_stop_go_two_part` merge. `drive_raw_cache.py check` — clean, no
new false positives (pack temperature's raw literal is already covered by
`SLIM_COLS`, confirmed). `node --check build_html.js` — clean (no
`build_html.js` changes needed; the new sub-fields are not yet dashboard-
bound, same treatment as most of this session's additions prior to M225).
JSON round-trip — clean. `build_html.js` full gate chain — clean, `127
stamped keys checked, all match the live corpus hash` (unchanged count —
no new top-level key this milestone, only nested additions to the
already-stamped `crawlStopGo`). jsdom: **9/9 tabs, 52 inner buttons, 0
console errors**, both semantic SEM-OK checks pass. Acceptance tests:
**T-01 (invariants) PASS, T-02 PASS, T-03 PASS, T-04 PASS, T-01b PASS**

**Isolation diff (key-by-key vs. the verified M225 baseline):** zero new

**Methodology note on this session's execution environment (same

## M225 (2026-09-04) — Dashboard 7.1: Evidence & Cross-Validation Ledger (epower_enhancement_implementation_plan.md, item 6 of 8)

**Trigger.** Sixth milestone of the enhancement plan. Hard dependency on
M220–M224 — this phase is assembly, not new computation, and could not
start until those milestones' "independent check" values existed to cite.
All five landed this session. Baseline verified from disk before any
change: CHANGELOG head M224, `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged,
`summary_arrays.json` 130 top-level keys.

**Objective.** Pull the primary-estimate/independent-check pairs scattered
across M220–M224 (plus one row that predates and does not depend on any of
them) into one ledger, so a reader sees what has been independently
corroborated, partially corroborated, or is a genuine open null result
without hunting through each dashboard section separately.

**New function `_evidence_ledger(arrays)`** — a lightweight aggregator,
pure post-processing over the already-assembled `arrays` dict, no raw
pass, no new statistical computation beyond simple arithmetic on numbers
already computed elsewhere. Five rows, exactly as the plan specified:

1. **Energy throughput (GTC/FCE)** — primary: released gross throughput
   (1263.7067 kWh). Two checks reported side by side, not collapsed into
   one: the same-algorithm re-implementation (a coding-bug check,
   max deviation 5×10⁻⁵ kWh — confirms no bug, not methodological
   independence) and M220's genuinely independent re-integration (true
   trapezoidal on interpolated timestamps, 1.40% mean / 1.46% p95
   deviation — a small, already-explained gap). **Confirmed.**
2. **Engine-start discharge-impulse buffer event** — primary: 2658
   buffer-impulse events (M116). Independent check: M221's full 4-detector
   chain reconciliation — 2038 events (76.7%) are corroborated by ALL
   three other physical detectors (ramp latency, handoff sequence, debt
   recovery) at once, an intentionally strict bar. **Partially confirmed**
   — reported as such, not rounded up.
3. **M119-v2 hazard model (START side)** — primary: blocked-day CV
   PR-AUC 0.0594 [0.0535, 0.0639]. Independent check: M222's rolling-origin
   (genuine train-on-past-only) CV, PR-AUC 0.0574 — close agreement under
   a materially different validation scheme. **Confirmed.**
4. **Drive-type regime transition structure** — primary: first-order
   Markov self-transition share 0.7238. Independent check: M223.2's
   second-order model comparison, ΔBIC=−163.5 (second-order does NOT
   improve fit). This row's `notes` field states explicitly that this
   check tests **model adequacy, not a number match** — a negative
   result here *confirms* the simpler model, it is not a failed
   cross-check. **Confirmed.**
5. **Pack internal-resistance fade trend** — primary: `powerFade`
   (cadence-controlled, −0.066 mOhm/month, CI spans zero). Independent
   check: `degradationTrends.resistanceVreg` (explicitly pre-linked via
   its own `primaryEstimandRef=powerFade` field, cadence-uncontrolled,
   +0.9955 mOhm/month, CI also spans zero). Notes disclose that both
   metrics' secondary mixed-effects method independently failed to
   converge (`LinAlgError: Singular matrix`) — an existing, pre-known
   state carried forward honestly, not newly discovered or hidden.
   **Partially confirmed** (same-sign-uncertain null result, not a clean
   match).

**Wiring subtlety resolved.** `evidenceLedger` needed to be stamped by
`_artifact_stamp` like every other top-level key, but each row also wants
to cite its own `artifactIdentity` (a `_artifactStamps` lookup) — a
chicken-and-egg ordering problem. Resolved by having `_evidence_ledger`
emit a plain `sourceKey` string per row (not a resolved stamp), assembling
`evidenceLedger` **before** `_artifact_stamp` runs (so it gets stamped
too), then a small backfill loop immediately after `_artifact_stamp`
resolves each row's `sourceKey` into a real `artifactIdentity` (12-hex-char
corpus hash + timestamp) in place.

**New JSX component: `EvidenceLedgerTable`**, added as Provenance block
**K** ("Evidence & Cross-Validation Ledger") in the Methodology & Data
Provenance tab, immediately after the existing block J. Every cell is
bound to `S.evidenceLedger.rows[i].*` via `.map()` — no hardcoded row
content, confirmed by `build_html.js`'s own literal-detector gate showing
**zero new** hardcoded-snapshot warnings (the same pre-existing 8 from
before this milestone, unchanged). Status badges color-coded (confirmed=
green, partially confirmed=amber, unresolved=red, not externally
testable=gray) from `r.validationStatus` directly, not a separate
hardcoded mapping per row. `evidenceLedger` added to `build_html.js`'s
`REQUIRED_BLOCKS` — the first of this session's new keys to earn that

M224's additions remain unsurfaced, awaiting this same treatment or their

**This session's first JSX change, done carefully given the size of the

closing `</ProvenanceBlock>` / `</div>` / `</Section>` boundary already
viewed in full before editing), rather than spanning a larger block of

## M224 (2026-09-04) — P0.3: SoC-control surface completion (epower_enhancement_implementation_plan.md, item 5 of 8)

**Trigger.** Fifth milestone of the enhancement plan, independent of
everything landed so far. Baseline verified from disk before any change:
CHANGELOG head M223.2, `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged, `summary_arrays
.json` 129 top-level keys.

**Objective.** Build the two missing components of the three-part dynamic
SoC-control surface the enhancement proposal describes — component 2
(engine START/STOP hazard) already exists as `socHysteresisV2`'s own
`partialDependence`/`surfaces` fields (M147/M216).

**Architecture choice.** Rather than building a parallel per-drive 1 Hz
grid, `_soc_control_surface` calls `m119v2_model.build_grid(fr)`
**verbatim** via `frame_loader` — the exact same function `socHysteresisV2`
itself is built from (`rpm`, `soc`, `speed`, `tpack`, `dis_kw`, `chg_kw`
all in one place, every raw channel already confirmed present in
`drive_raw_cache.SLIM_COLS`). No new raw pass. SoC axis (40–85 by 5) and
speed axis (0–130 by 10) are `m119v2_model.SURF_SOC`/`SURF_SPEED`
verbatim, and the per-cell window half-widths (SoC ±2.5, speed ±5) match
`m119v2_model._support_mask`'s own cell definition exactly — satisfying
the plan's "identical SoC/demand axes and identical support-density
masking" requirement literally, not just in spirit.

**224.1 — Net battery-power-neutral contour (component 1).** Per (SoC,
speed) cell, a **day-blocked** mean net battery power (kW, charge-positive
— the same sign convention `energyPath.chargeSources`' `gross_charge_kwh`
accounting uses): each cell's value is the mean OF PER-DAY MEANS, every
day weighted equally, not a naive pooled per-second mean — the exact
pseudoreplication guard the proposal calls for. Reported separately for
engine-on and engine-off seconds. Binned local regression (one of the
plan's two explicitly-permitted choices, "GAM or binned local
regression"), not a smoothed GAM — a deliberate, disclosed simplification.

**224.2 — Generator-charging probability surface (component 3).** The
identical day-blocked-mean convention applied to a binary "charging"
indicator (net power > 0). **Reuses the outcome-label definition, not a
re-derived classifier:** `energyPath.chargeSources`' four charge-source
categories (generator-only, generator+regen, pure regen, engine-off coast)
are each, by construction, net-charging events — so "charging" = "net
battery power > 0" is their exact union, sufficient for a binary indicator
without replicating the full four-way engine-state × motor-torque
attribution rule that distinguishes *which* source is charging.

**Honest, disclosed non-monotonicity — the derived finding, checked rather
than assumed.** The day-blocked net-power values are **not** always
monotonic in SoC: e.g. at 50 km/h engine-on, the mean is positive
(charging, ~1.5–8 kW) from SoC 45–70%, dips to **−3.7 kW** at 75%, then
recovers positive at 80–85% (thin cells, n≤16 days). A naive single
"zero-crossing" framing would silently misrepresent this as a clean
regime boundary. Fixed during implementation: `zeroCrossingBySpeed*` now
reports **`nSignChanges`** alongside each crossing (count of *all* sign
changes in that speed column, not just the first) — most engine-on
columns in the 30–90 km/h band show 2–4 sign changes, explicitly flagging
that "the" reported crossing is a simplification of a more textured
shape, never smoothed away to hide it. Engine-off crossings are cleaner
(1–3 sign changes) and cluster consistently around **SoC 68–76%** across
the 30–70 km/h band — the more stable of the two findings. Condition
sensitivity (mid-speed, engine-on, tercile bands): the zero-crossing SoC
shifts with **both** temperature (mid-temp 77.8% → high-temp 81.3%,
low-temp band has no clean crossing) and demand (low-demand 46.7% →
high-demand 81.1%, mid-demand no clean crossing) — the effective
charge-maintenance region does move with condition, the plan's target
"potential conclusion," evaluated honestly rather than assumed; the
low/mid-band "no crossing" results are reported as such, not forced.

**New key `socControlSurface`**: `socAxis`, `speedAxis`, `netPowerContour`
(`engineOn`/`engineOff`, each with `values`/`n`/`nDays`/`thin` grids, plus
`zeroCrossingBySpeedEngineOn`/`Off`), `chargingProbSurface`
(`engineOn`/`engineOff`), `supportDensity` (the shared per-cell `nDays`/
`thin` grid both surfaces draw their masking from — identical masking
across all three views, per 224.3's explicit requirement),
`conditionSensitivity` (temperature/demand tercile bands),
`hazardCrossRef` (a pointer to `socHysteresisV2.surfaces`, not a
duplicate, so the dashboard can render all three views from one shared
axis definition), `methodology`.

**No new stochastic component.** Unlike M223.1/M223.2, `_soc_control_surface`
uses no random seeding at all — pure day-blocked binned averaging, fully
deterministic given the corpus. The plan's "seed=42 where stochastic"
validation item is conditionally satisfied by not applying: nothing was
added to `determinism.reproducibilityScope`'s disclaimer list this
milestone, since there is nothing stochastic to disclaim.

**Validation & acceptance.** `py_compile compute_summary_arrays.py` —
clean, checked after every edit (see the editing-process note below).
`drive_raw_cache.py check` — clean, no new false positives (this milestone
references no raw column literals directly, only `m119v2_model.build_grid`
via `frame_loader`). `node --check build_html.js` — clean (no
`build_html.js` changes needed; `socControlSurface` is not yet a
dashboard-bound `REQUIRED_BLOCKS` entry, same treatment as this session's
other still-unsurfaced additions, all awaiting M225's coordinated Evidence
Ledger). JSON round-trip — clean. `build_html.js` full gate chain — clean,
`126 stamped keys checked, all match the live corpus hash` (125→126,
correctly picking up the new `socControlSurface` key). jsdom: **9/9 tabs,
52 inner buttons, 0 console errors**, both semantic SEM-OK checks pass.
Acceptance tests: **T-01 (invariants) PASS, T-02 PASS, T-03 PASS, T-04
PASS, T-01b PASS** (T-01 golden-snapshot drift n=289→320, same
pre-existing, non-gating pattern).

**A note on this session's editing process.** Given the four prior
CHANGELOG heading-orphaning incidents and two destructive `str_replace`
near-misses on neighboring functions earlier in this session, the
`_soc_control_surface` insertion (a large, ~230-line function next to
`_high_soc_regen`) was done in two deliberate steps instead of one: first
a minimal marker (`def _soc_control_surface(...):` alone) was inserted and
verified via `py_compile` (correctly failing with an expected
"IndentationError: expected an indented block," confirming the marker
landed cleanly with nothing else disturbed), then the full function body
was inserted into that exact, now-unique gap. `_high_soc_regen` was
byte-diffed against the untouched `/mnt/project` source both before and
after — one apparent mismatch on the first check turned out to be a false
alarm in the comparison script itself (a "find the next `def`" boundary
helper swept up an unrelated trailing comment block on the pre-edit side

converged on for large insertions near existing code, and produced no
incident this milestone.

## M223.2 (2026-09-04) — P1.5: regime-transition statistical hardening (epower_enhancement_implementation_plan.md, item 4 of 8, part 2 of 2 — closes M223)

**Trigger.** Second half of M223, completing the split the plan itself
suggested ("consider splitting 223.1 and 223.2 across two sessions").
Baseline verified from disk before any change: CHANGELOG head M223.1,
`drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged, `summary_arrays.json` 129 top-level keys.

**Objective.** Add the statistical hardening layer the enhancement plan
specifies over `regimeTransition`'s (M142) existing first-order Markov
count matrix — 8 self-contained sub-computations, none touching
`_regime_transition` itself.

**Architecture choice, made deliberately after this session's earlier
near-misses on destructive `str_replace` edits to neighboring functions:**
`_regime_transition_hardening()` is a wholly SEPARATE function that
re-derives the same chronological transition sequence from `dm` (a cheap
pandas re-derivation, not a raw pass) rather than editing
`_regime_transition`'s own loop to retain the extra day/gap/hour metadata
it needed. This guarantees `_regime_transition`'s pre-existing output is
byte-identical **by construction**, not just by careful editing — verified
explicitly anyway (`_regime_transition(dm)` reproduces the shipped block
exactly). The two dicts are merged in `build_summary_arrays()` via
`.update()`; two prospective key collisions were caught before shipping —
both functions independently compute an `nTransitions` (numerically
identical, popped from the hardening dict before merge as a
belt-and-suspenders guard rather than relying on the coincidence) and both
had a `method` key (the new one renamed to `hardeningMethod` so the
original stays untouched, satisfying the plan's explicit "existing fields
byte-identical" acceptance criterion literally).

**All 8 sub-computations, run on the primary global chain (max_gap_h=None,
same default as regimeTransition's own headline call), 315 transitions /
76 days, ~0.75s total (pure count-matrix arithmetic, no raw pass):**

1. **`dirichletCI` / `dayClusteredCI`** — per-cell uncertainty intervals:
   closed-form Jeffreys-prior Dirichlet (primary, always well-defined) and
   a day-clustered bootstrap (1000 draws, secondary robustness check). The
   two agree closely where compared (urban→urban: [0.813, 0.900] Dirichlet
   vs. [0.816, 0.905] day-clustered) — cross-validates the interval
   machinery. New fields, not merged into the existing `cells` array (the
   plan's own acceptance criterion requires `regimeTransition`'s existing
   fields, including `cells`, to stay byte-identical — confirmed).
2. **`residualHeatmap`** — observed-minus-independence-expected counts.
   Real, physically sensible structure: highway→highway and
   mixed_highway→mixed_highway both show strong positive standardized
   residuals (+5.97, +4.42 — highway-type drives cluster together far more
   than chance), while urban→highway is strongly negative (−3.16 — direct
   urban-to-highway transitions are rarer than independence predicts,
   consistent with usually passing through a mixed regime first).
3. **`permutationTest`** — shuffles drive-type labels WITHIN day blocks
   (never globally, respecting the same chain-break discipline
   `chainBreaksGap`/`maxGapHours` already encode), seed=42, 4000 draws,
   G-test departure statistic. **Result: p=0.00025, the day-structure-
   preserving null is rejected** — the observed matrix carries real
   structure beyond what random within-day relabeling produces, consistent
   with `regimeTransition.persistence`'s pre-existing finding that the
   sequence is not memoryless.
4. **`secondOrder`** — conditions the transition on the previous TWO drive
   types, fit on the identical 313-triple sample as a first-order re-fit
   for a fair comparison, BIC + likelihood-ratio. **Honest-null result:
   second-order does NOT improve BIC** (ΔBIC=−163.5, heavily penalized for
   36 extra parameters against only 313 triples; LR p=0.186, not
   significant) — reported as a null result, not reconciled toward a
   preferred answer, matching the plan's explicit honest-null note and the
   existing `powerFade`/`cellSpreadRelaxation` precedent.
5. **`conditionalTransitions`** — self-transition share by parking-gap bin
   (the SAME six bins `interDriveCarryover`/M223.1 uses, reused verbatim),
   time-of-day (6h buckets — 00:00–06:00 correctly shows n=0, this is a
   daytime-driving corpus), and weekday/weekend. Genuine findings: 24+h
   gaps show markedly lower persistence (0.524) than same-day gaps
   (~0.72–0.79); weekday persistence (0.775) exceeds weekend (0.648),
   consistent with a more repetitive commute pattern on weekdays.
6. **`heldOutLogLik`** — genuine leave-one-day-out predictive
   log-likelihood (Jeffreys-smoothed so a thin held-out day is never scored
   against a hard-zero cell), not an in-sample fit statistic. Mean −0.696
   nats/transition (⇒ ~0.50 average assigned probability on truly
   out-of-sample days), meaningfully better than a naive uniform 4-state
   guess (−1.386 nats / 0.25).
7. **`entropy`** / **`expectedRunLength`** — row-wise Shannon entropy and
   `1/(1-p_ii)`. Physically coherent: urban has the lowest entropy (0.756
   bits) and longest expected run length (7.36 drives) — the most
   persistent, predictable regime; highway the highest entropy (1.684
   bits) among short-run regimes.
8. **`carryoverLink`** — explicit `carryoverLinkKey: 'interDriveCarryover'`
   plus a note stating the shared construction (same
   consecutive-chronological-pair join, same gap bins), satisfying the
   plan's direct-linkage requirement between P0.1 and P1.5.

**`determinism.reproducibilityScope` extended** (both `summary_config.json
.auditMetadata.determinism` and `summary_arrays.json.determinism`, spliced
simultaneously per the M209 convention) to disclaim the two new stochastic
components this milestone and M223.1 introduced: `interDriveCarryover`'s
day-clustered bootstrap OLS and mixed-effects check, and
`regimeTransition`'s day-block permutation test and Dirichlet/day-clustered
bootstrap intervals — neither re-executed by the `determinism_check.py`
harness, which remains scoped to the ML16 ensemble-outlier stage only, per
the plan's explicit validation requirement.

**Validation & acceptance.** `py_compile compute_summary_arrays.py` and
`determinism_check.py` — clean, checked after every edit including the two
mid-session recoveries (see below). `drive_raw_cache.py check` — clean, no
new false positives (this milestone touches no raw columns at all — pure
count-matrix arithmetic over already-existing `dm` columns). `node --check
build_html.js` — clean (no `build_html.js` changes needed; the new
`regimeTransition` sub-fields are not yet dashboard-bound, same treatment
as this session's other still-unsurfaced additions). JSON round-trip —
clean on both touched files. `build_html.js` full gate chain — clean, `125
stamped keys checked, all match the live corpus hash` (unchanged count
from M223.1 — no new top-level key this milestone, only nested additions
to the already-stamped `regimeTransition`). jsdom: **9/9 tabs, 52 inner
buttons, 0 console errors**, both semantic SEM-OK checks pass, re-verified
with both updated files together. Acceptance tests: **T-01 (invariants)
PASS, T-02 PASS, T-03 PASS, T-04 PASS, T-01b PASS**, re-run against the
updated `summary_config.json` (T-01 golden-snapshot drift n=289→320, same
pre-existing, non-gating pattern).

**Two mid-session editing near-misses, both caught before any test ran.**
(1) An `str_replace` intended to insert new functions before
`_thermal_convergence` (left over from the M223.1 portion of this
session's context) briefly overwrote that function's own def line —
caught immediately via `py_compile` + a targeted function-body diff
against `/mnt/project`'s untouched original, fixed, reverified. (2) The
SAME failure mode recurred inserting `_regime_transition_hardening` before
`_heat_soak_carryover` — this time the def line itself was deleted rather
than mislabeled. Caught the same way (`py_compile` first, then an explicit
byte-identity diff of `_heat_soak_carryover`, `_regime_transition`,
`_thermal_step_response`, and `_regime_persistence` against source, all
confirmed identical after the fix) before any downstream computation was
attempted. Both incidents reinforce the value of the byte-identity-first
discipline this session has followed throughout — a mistake caught by a
diff before any output is trusted costs nothing; one caught after would
have cost a full re-verification cycle.

**Isolation diff (key-by-key vs. the verified M223.1 baseline):**
`summary_arrays.json` — zero new/removed top-level keys; exactly three
changed: `regimeTransition` (exactly 12 new sub-fields —
`nDays`, `dirichletCI`, `dayClusteredCI`, `residualHeatmap`,
`permutationTest`, `secondOrder`, `conditionalTransitions`,
`heldOutLogLik`, `entropy`, `expectedRunLength`, `carryoverLink`,
`hardeningMethod` — zero pre-existing sub-fields changed, confirmed
explicitly, not just by the construction argument above), `determinism`
(the reproducibilityScope extension), and the expected wholesale
`_artifactStamps` refresh (`generatedAt` only; `corpusHash`/`configHash`/
`upstreamHashes` confirmed identical). `summary_config.json` — exactly one
changed key, `auditMetadata`, and within it exactly one changed sub-key,
`determinism`. Nothing else moved in either file. `drive_master.csv` MD5
verified unchanged before and after (this milestone and M223.1 together
touch no drive-level data, only derived arrays and one config sub-block).

**Effort:** Medium–Large, as scoped — closes M223 (both 223.1 and 223.2

## M223.1 (2026-09-04) — P0.1: coolant/oil thermal decay + linked adjacent-drive table (epower_enhancement_implementation_plan.md, item 4 of 8, part 1 of 2)

**Trigger.** Fourth milestone of the enhancement plan. The plan itself
flags M223 as "the largest single phase... consider splitting 223.1 and
223.2 across two sessions if needed" — split accordingly: this session
lands 223.1 only; 223.2 (regime-transition statistical hardening) is a
follow-up. Baseline verified from disk before any change: CHANGELOG head
M222, `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged, `summary_arrays.json` 128
top-level keys.

**Objective.** Extend `heatSoakCarryover`'s (M141) pack-only inter-drive
thermal-relaxation pattern (chronological pairing, gap-binning, Newtonian-
cooling τ-fit) to coolant and oil, and join it with following-drive
first-engine-start timing into one linked adjacent-drive table.

**Extended `_battery_temp_traj`** (additively — every pre-existing caller
unaffected) with `coolant_start/peak/end` and `oil_start/peak/end`,
read in the SAME per-file frame_loader pass as the pack sensors (two more
columns added to the existing per-file read, not a second raw pass).
**Byte-identity gate, checked before adding anything downstream:** all
pre-existing `t1_*`/`pm_*` fields reproduce **exactly** across all 313
files with pack-temperature coverage. Coverage of the new channels: 310/313
coolant, 308/313 oil.

**New function `_linked_adjacent_drive_table`**: per consecutive
chronological drive pair, joins arrival temperatures (pack/coolant/oil/
ambient — the state at the START of the following drive), arrival vs.
departure SoC, the previous drive's duration/distance/engine-duty/thermal
maxima (all read directly from existing `drive_master` columns — a join,
no re-derivation), and the following drive's time-to-first-engine-start,
first-5-minute engine-on fraction, GTC, peak discharge current, and SoC-delta
outcomes. The engine-start timing needed one new lightweight per-drive
helper, `_first_window_engine_metrics` (reuses `_engine_start_triggers`'s
own RPM-column/threshold convention verbatim — not a new detector). 309
pairs, 313→320-drive corpus.

**Thermal decay fits** (`_carryover_thermal_decay`, the identical
Newtonian-cooling regression `_heat_soak_carryover` already uses — ln(resid/
init excess) through the origin on gap, day-clustered bootstrap CI, seed=42
— applied to coolant and oil): **coolant τ=9.51h [6.87, 11.58] (r²=0.224,
n=226, 54 days); oil τ=8.83h [6.06, 11.09] (r²=0.335, n=218, 54 days).**
Cross-referenced against the existing pack (battery) fit: **τ=17.63h
[11.38, 23.69] (r²=0.465, n=168)** — coolant and oil cool roughly **twice
as fast** as the pack, a physically coherent result (both are smaller,
better ambient-exposed thermal masses than the insulated battery pack) that
also cross-validates this milestone's new fit machinery against the
pre-existing one it was built to parallel.

**Regression model** (`_carryover_regression`): day-clustered bootstrap OLS
(primary, matching `bufferDebtRecovery`'s established `dayboot` pattern,
generalized from a scalar metric to a coefficient vector via the new
`_dayboot_ols` helper) of the following drive's time-to-first-engine-start
on arrival pack temperature, parking gap, and arrival SoC — 293 pairs, 74
days. **Genuine finding, reported as observed rather than steered toward
the initial hypothesis:** arrival pack temperature coefficient **−4.69
[−6.62, −2.99]** — a colder arrival pack is associated with a **longer**,
not shorter, time to the next engine start; the opposite of this
milestone's own working hypothesis going in (that a colder buffer would
call the ICE sooner to replenish it), CI clearly excludes zero either way.
Parking-gap and arrival-SoC coefficients are also non-null (0.36 [0.01,
1.05] and 2.14 [0.35, 4.06] respectively). Secondary mixed-effects check
(day random intercept, `statsmodels==0.15.0`, matching
`degradation_trends.py`'s `_mixedlm` convention) **failed to converge**
(`LinAlgError: Singular matrix`) at this pairs-per-day density (293 pairs
/ 74 days, several days with very few pairs) — reported as-is in the
`mixedEffects` field rather than adjusted or hidden, per this codebase's
honest-null convention for a secondary robustness check that doesn't come
back clean.

**New key `interDriveCarryover`**: `nPairs`, `nDays`, `thermalDecay:
{coolant, oil, battery: <cross-reference to heatSoakCarryover>}`,
`regressionModel`, `methodology` (states single-vehicle/single-driver
descriptive association explicitly, not a causal or generalizable
driver-behavior law — matching the disclosure pattern already used for
`heatSoakCarryover`/`regimeTransition`, per the plan's required caution).

**A note on this session's process.** One destructive editing mistake
occurred mid-implementation: an `str_replace` intended to insert new
functions before `_thermal_convergence` instead briefly overwrote that
function's own signature, leaving its body attached to the wrong def line.
Caught immediately by the next `py_compile` + a targeted function-body diff
against the untouched `/mnt/project` original, fixed before it could
propagate into any test run, and reverified afterward with an explicit
byte-identity check on `_thermal_convergence`, `_heat_soak_carryover`, and
`_battery_temp_ranges` (all confirmed identical to source). Separately, the
`drive_raw_cache.py check` acceptance script flagged one new false positive
— a code comment describing the cross-module `T_coolant` naming trap (see
M221) happened to wrap `'[VCM] HV Coolant Temperature (℃)'` across a line
break in a way the checker's literal-scanning regex matched as if it were
a real column reference; reworded the comment (no functional change) and
reconfirmed the checker returns to only the two pre-existing, unrelated
`[BMS] Battery Cell #` false positives present before this session started.

**Validation & acceptance.** `py_compile compute_summary_arrays.py` —
clean, checked after every edit including the mid-session recovery.
`drive_raw_cache.py check compute_summary_arrays.py` — clean relative to
baseline (two pre-existing, unrelated false positives only; the one new
false positive introduced and then fixed this session, see above). `node
--check build_html.js` — clean (no `build_html.js` changes needed;
`interDriveCarryover` is not yet a dashboard-bound `REQUIRED_BLOCKS` entry,
same treatment as this session's other still-unsurfaced additions, all
awaiting M225's coordinated Evidence Ledger). JSON round-trip — clean.
`build_html.js` full gate chain — clean, `125 stamped keys checked, all
match the live corpus hash` (124→125, correctly picking up the new
`interDriveCarryover` key). jsdom: **9/9 tabs, 52 inner buttons, 0 console
errors**, both semantic SEM-OK checks pass. Acceptance tests: **T-01
(invariants) PASS, T-02 PASS, T-03 PASS, T-04 PASS, T-01b PASS** (T-01
golden-snapshot drift n=289→320, same pre-existing, non-gating pattern).

**Isolation diff (key-by-key vs. the verified M222 baseline):** exactly
one new top-level key (`interDriveCarryover`, 128→129); zero removed;
exactly one changed key, the expected wholesale `_artifactStamps` refresh
(`generatedAt` only; `corpusHash`/`configHash`/`upstreamHashes` confirmed

`_battery_temp_traj` — all explicitly confirmed **byte-identical**.
Nothing else moved. `drive_master.csv` MD5 verified unchanged before and

**Methodology note on this session's execution environment (same

frame_loader pass (309 pairs, ~7s) and `_battery_temp_traj`'s extended
