## M97 (2026-08-07) — corpus provenance: snapshot manifest, NOT a freeze (audit P0-01)

The corpus is longitudinal and continues to grow, so freezing it (audit's literal P0-01 recommendation)
is inappropriate. The audit's underlying *reproducibility* need is met instead by an **append-only
snapshot manifest** (`corpus_manifest.py` → `raw_manifest.json`): each pipeline run stamps a
`snapshotId` (date + corpus hash) and records, per drive, SHA-256 + actual raw row count + a cross-check
against the master's recorded `n_raw_rows`. A published figure cites its snapshotId; the corpus keeps
growing.

The manifest also **detects the P0-01 defect class** (a master row built from a different-length raw
file than the one on disk — the `ROW_MISMATCH` status). Running it on the current corpus:
**214/214 master rows match their raw files exactly, 0 row-mismatches, 0 missing** — i.e. the two
shortened sessions the audit reported (`20260612_152740`, `20260726_172244`) were an artifact of the
audit's supplied ZIP export, not a live defect here. The prior `raw_manifest.json` was itself stale
(206-file snapshot); it is now regenerated at 214 with per-file SHA-256 and the integrity block.

Recommended: run `corpus_manifest.py` as the final step of the compact ingestion protocol so every
release carries a current snapshotId and fails loud on any future ROW_MISMATCH.

## M102 (2026-08-08) — `[VCM] Motor RPM` rejected as a corrupt PID

Registers `[VCM] Motor RPM (rpm)` as a **rejected raw channel**: it is present in the logs but does not
carry traction-motor mechanical speed and must never enter the working namespace. Moved out of `COL_MAP`
into a new `_REJECTED_CHANNELS` dict in `compute_drive_summary_v6.py`, so the rejection is explicit at the
ingestion boundary and the PID can never be silently re-consumed.

### Evidence — corpus-wide (209/214 FWD drives carry the channel)

- **It is the torque register, not motor speed.** Per-drive correlation of `[VCM] Motor RPM` with
  `[VCM] Target Motor Torque` (asof-aligned on the ~1.8 s round-robin poll): median **0.9975**, min 0.951,
  >0.99 on **91 %** of drives. Numerically `MotorRPM ≈ 64 × target_torque`.
- **No road-speed content.** Correlation with `[VCM] Vehicle Speed`: median **0.017**, p95|r| = 0.23. At a
  pinned 117 km/h cruise the channel swings 640→2592 while a single-speed-reduction traction motor must read
  a near-constant ~7000 rpm; it sits at 0 at standstill yet spikes to ~12000 on engine/load transients, and
  runs ~5× low in magnitude for real motor speed.
- **Systematic, not vehicle-specific.** The e-4ORCE rail shows the identical artifact (r_ttq = 0.987,
  r_spd = −0.11) — a logger / PID-definition fault, not a drive- or car-specific glitch.

Consequence: no shaft mechanical power (τ·ω), reduction-ratio recovery, or torque–RPM operating map is
derivable from this PID. This retires the P_mech current-sensor-independent energy cross-check floated in the
prior working session — that idea required a trustworthy ω, which this dataset does not contain. Preserved as
a negative result in the same spirit as the M98 DCIR-not-extractable finding.

### Not rejected — `[VCM] Motor Torque` (measured)

Distinct channel, distinct disposition. Measured `[VCM] Motor Torque` is a valid image of the same physical
quantity as `[VCM] Target Motor Torque` but decoded at **~1/256** of true N·m (corpus scale factor
target/measured: median **257.6**, IQR [256.5, 258.6] — a 2⁸ decode artifact). Currently unused; multiply by
~256 to recover measured (vs commanded) N·m. Left in `COL_MAP` with an inline note; a measured-vs-commanded
torque-tracking panel remains an available future addition.

### Referential-integrity / gate

`motor_rpm` was a dead rename — never read after `COL_MAP` (the `ev_*` engine-state metrics use `eng_rpm`,
the ICE channel, not `motor_rpm`). Removing it changes **no** computed column: `drive_master.csv` (214 rows,
all live columns, corpus GTC 471.8) is byte-identical and no arrays or JSX rebuild is required. The 5 early
SoC/fuel-only logs that never carried the PID (`20260512_111617`, `20260512_195020`, `20260512_215542`,
`20260513_180335`, `20260531_200637`) are unaffected. Confirmation statistic reproducible via a 3-column
(rpm/target_torque/speed) asof pass over the raw corpus.

## M104 (2026-08-09) — two independent bugs: M91 legend glyph escaping; ambient-array `[1]`→`[-1]` mis-index

Two unrelated bugs surfaced together during methodology Q&A and fixed in the same pass.

### 1. `SocLevelSensitivityChart` legend renders literal `\u25fc`/`\u2265`/`\u2013` text

`xtrail_summary.jsx`, the M91 "Where the k=2 damage sits" chart (lines ~884-889). The
legend bullets were written as literal `\u25fc`/`\u2265`/`\u2013` sequences directly in
JSX text content. JSX text children do not interpret backslash-escapes (that is a JS
string-literal rule, not a JSX-text rule); only HTML entities (`&lt;`, `&nbsp;`, used
correctly elsewhere in the same lines) are decoded. Confirmed via the already-built
`xtrail_dashboard.html` (compiled output contained the literal 7-character string
`"\\u25fc "`, not the glyph) and via an isolated `react-dom/server` render of the
extracted component. Every other legend/bullet in the file uses the literal glyph
(`■`, `●`) — this was an isolated 3-line regression, not a systemic pattern.

**Fix:** replaced `\u25fc`→`■`, `\u2265`→`≥`, `\u2013`→`–` (literal characters), matching
the convention at e.g. lines ~1644-1646, ~3985-3987. Underlying data was never wrong
(`corpusBandSharePctOfK2 = {lo: 0.0, mid: 0.2, hi: 99.8}`, sums to 100.0) — display only.

**Validated:** acorn-jsx parse OK; full-file Babel build OK; isolated component
re-render confirms literal `■`/`≥`/`–` now appear in the output markup.

### 2. `_battery_vs_ambient` reads `amb[1]` as "end ambient" — wrong for 3+-value entries

`compute_summary_arrays.py`, `_battery_vs_ambient` (~line 6005). `ambientByDrive` is a
manual per-drive config field, nominally `[start, end]`, but 4 corpus drives currently
carry a 3rd (interim) reading for long trips with a rise-then-fall ambient pattern
(`20260803_181923`: `[29.0, 31.0, 29.0]`; `20260804_215437`: `[21.0, 24.0, 21.0]`;
`20260808_160215`: `[29.0, 30.0, 27.0]`; `20260808_201800`: `[21.0, 19.0, 21.0]`). The
old code (`amb[1] if len(amb) > 1 else amb[0]`) always took index `[1]` as "end," which
is only correct-by-construction for exactly 2 values — for the 3-value drives it silently
read back the **interim** reading as `ambEnd`, and the true final reading (`amb[2]`) was
never read anywhere in either consumer (grep-confirmed). Downstream effect: the "Battery
vs Measured Ambient" section (`S.batteryVsAmbient`) printed a false monotonic narrative
(e.g. "amb 29.0→31.0°C" for a drive that actually went 29→31→29), and `deltaPeak`
(`bp - a1`) was computed against the wrong ambient value. `_battery_temp_ranges`'s
Cool/Mild/Hot binning (`sum(pair)/len(pair)`) was **not** affected — it already averages
all provided values regardless of count. `belowAmbient` derives only from `deltaStart`
(`amb[0]`, always correct), so its counts were also unaffected.

**Fix:** `amb[1]` → `amb[-1]`, correct for 1, 2, or N values.

**Validated on real data** (raw pass over the 4 affected files, not synthetic):

| file | ambEnd before | ambEnd after | deltaPeak before | deltaPeak after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20260803_181923 | 31.0 | 29.0 | 5 | 7 |
| 20260804_215437 | 24.0 | 21.0 | 20 | 23 |
| 20260808_160215 | 30.0 | 27.0 | 7 | 10 |
| 20260808_201800 | 19.0 | 21.0 | 19 | 17 |

`py_compile` OK. Full corpus-wide `batteryVsAmbient`/`belowAmbient`/`batteryTempRanges`
regeneration (raw pass over all 219 drives, not just the 4 affected) still pending —
requires the full raw loader run; scoped to Andrii's local environment per standing
protocol, same as the deferred `build_summary_arrays` full run.

### Not done here (flagged, not actioned)

Andrii separately asked whether ambient temperature should feed the C-rate map, regen
capture rate, and engine warm-up curve. Answered narratively (C-rate and regen already
temperature-stratify via measured pack temp, which is the more correct variable than
ambient; `warmupCurve` has no temperature stratification at all, pack or ambient, and is
a genuine gap) — no code changes made pending Andrii's decision on scope.

Andrii supplied two Nissan Technical Review PDFs (No.89 2023 Special Feature 1, and

`summary_config.json`: new top-level `oemTechReview` block (paraphrased, not quoted,
per copyright discipline; every figure sourced to a specific article/section/figure).
Sub-blocks: `topologyConfirmation`, `generatorMotorGap`, `fixedPointOperation`,
`engineFloor`, `maxOutputPoint`, `powerBlendingMechanism`, `evRatioWltc`,
`electricBrakeDissipationContext`, `notConfirmedByThisSource`. Arrives in `S.*` via
the existing `...config` spread in `buildS()` — no code change needed there, same
mechanism as `officialDisclosure`/`batterySupplier` (M79).

`xtrail_summary.jsx`: five inline `S.oemTechReview && (...)` callouts, all pure
additions (diff confirms zero lines modified or deleted, six insertion hunks):

1. **Architecture section (§4)** — topology confirmation (100% engine→generator,
   100% motor→wheels, Article 2 Fig. 1) plus the 116 kW generator / 150 kW front-motor
   spec gap as an independent, spec-sheet-level anchor for the buffer thesis.
2. **Engine RPM Distribution section** — the disclosed 2000 rpm best-thermal fixed
   point (Article 3 §3.1) against this corpus's independently-measured 1900-2100 rpm
   dominant mode (~62% of engine-on time, M82/M83); the disclosed ≥1500 rpm exhaust-
   design floor (Article 2 §4) against this corpus's independently-measured 1400 rpm
   fuel-state-classifier floor (M84).
3. **High-Speed Power Blending section** — Article 2's own description of the
   battery-first-then-engine torque-blending sequence (§5.2.2, Fig. 10) against the
   M41 blend-share finding; and, inside the nearLimiter panel, the disclosed 106 kW /
   4400 rpm rated max-output point (Article 3 §3.2, JDM-flagged) against the vmax-
   drive plateau.
4. **Buffer-Saturation Dissipation at Low Speed section** — Article 2's description

Motivation. The independent audit (2026-08-09) found both manifest
implementations (`corpus_manifest.py`, `_audit_raw_manifest`) iterated over

  `..._B_D_comparison.csv` onto a `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.csv` name and mask it.
  Roles: canonical | comparison_only(D) | auxiliary(e-4ORCE) | orphan | missing.

  enumerating `corpus_manifest`. The false `oneToOne` boolean is replaced by

  explicitly NOT checked, never silently asserted true).
- Regenerated `raw_manifest.json` against the live directory.

  discontinued 2026-08-09), 1 auxiliary (e-4ORCE). 0 orphan, 0 missing;

- Row-count agreement: 0 mismatches across all 219 canonical files vs master
  `n_raw_rows`. sha256 reproducible; matches the prior manifest hash for the
  spot-checked file.
- `py_compile` clean on both edited modules.

## B4 — 2026-08-10 — Document the M98 event-resistance withdrawal (audit P0-02)

Note-only remediation: confirms a null result (nothing to fix in code) and adds
the documentation the audit explicitly asked for ("if discussed as a failed
method, present it in limitations, not results").

**Finding (audit P0-02, critical):** an earlier-session exploratory method,
"M98" (`dcir_events.py`, discrete-event DCIR extraction via R = -dV/dI over
load-transition events), assumed discharge-positive BMS current against a
raw signal that is actually charge-positive — its sign convention was wrong,
and its own shipped result (646 events / 49 drives, median 19.60 mΩ,
controlled slope +2.38 mΩ/mo, CI [-1.01, 5.29]) was not reproducible from the
supplied script. The audit re-ran the identical event logic on the full
219-drive corpus under both signs to test estimator stability rather than
just correctness: legacy (wrong) sign → 2,043 events / 149 drives, 19.24 mΩ,
+1.278 mΩ/mo; physically-consistent charge-positive sign → 46,694 events /
206 drives, 79.67 mΩ, -0.521 mΩ/mo. The event population changed by >20× and
the median resistance by ~4× between the two sign choices, with the slope
changing sign. This is not a single fixable bug — the estimator's result is
unstable to a choice that should not affect it, and unsynchronized I/V
sampling (separate polling timestamps) is the likely underlying cause.
Audit-required action: **withdraw the M98 trend; do not present it as a
result.**

**Verification that nothing ships:** `dcir_events.py` and every symbol/string
containing "M98" or "dcir" were searched for across
`compute_summary_arrays.py`, `compute_drive_summary_v6.py`, `xtrail_summary.jsx`
and `build_html.js` — zero occurrences. The method was never wired into this
pipeline; there is no array key, dashboard binding, or shipped figure to
retract. "Withdrawal" here means confirming continued absence and documenting
why, not a code change.

**Documentation added:** a paragraph in the dashboard's "Methodology & Data
Provenance" section (Conclusions tab) states the finding, both audit re-run
results, and the withdrawal, and explicitly distinguishes M98 from the
retained resistance-trend measurement: the load-excited V-regression proxy
(`vreg_R` / `vsag_R`, M25/M56) already shown in the internal-resistance
callout and reported throughout as the measured, null power-fade trend. M25
is a continuous per-drive regression, methodologically unrelated to M98's
discrete event extraction, and is unaffected by this finding — the audit's
own independent estimate of it (median 121.8 mΩ on 124 load-excited drives,
T-controlled slope -0.001 mΩ/month, 95% CI [-1.926, 2.081]) matches this
study's `officialDisclosureCorrelation.resistance.ourVregPackMohm` (121.8)
to the reported digit.

Verification: babel parses clean (prose-only addition, no new `S.*` bindings,
so no regen/isolation-diff required); jsdom re-check confirms 9/9 tabs render

## T-01 fix — 2026-08-10 — Replace hardcoded golden value with invariants (audit P1)

**Finding:** `_acceptance_tests()`'s T-01 asserted `peakChargeA == 213.0`
verbatim. Audit: "Hardcodes peakChargeA==213.0, which fails legitimately as
an append-only corpus grows... Test invariants and signed golden artifacts
per snapshot; separate regression from scientific acceptance." Confirmed the
concern directly: appended a simulated 220th drive with a legitimately
higher charge peak (-250.0 A) to a scratch copy of the master and re-ran the
old test logic — it would have failed a perfectly healthy pipeline on
correctly-computed new data.

**Fix — three-part split, matching the audit's own phrasing:**
- **T-01 (invariants, corpus-size-independent, always runs):** three checks
  that hold regardless of what future drives are appended — (1) the
  sign-safe abs-max is non-negative, (2) it strictly exceeds the naive
  signed `.max()` whenever the corpus contains any charging sample at all
  (directly catches a regression to the pre-fix C-02 bug, which returned a
  near-zero value, without asserting what the correct magnitude is), (3) a
  loose physical sanity bound (0–500 A, generously above the current 213.0 A
  extremum) that catches unit/order-of-magnitude errors without breaking on
  a legitimately higher peak.
- **T-01b (live cross-check, runs when config_path is supplied, reuses the
  existing `with_raw=False` build already performed for T-03/T-04 — no
  extra full-raw regen):** asserts the test's own from-master computation
  agrees exactly with what the live pipeline actually ships in
  `meta.peakChargeA`. Two independent call sites computing the same formula
  on the same input must match; this is the internal-consistency check that
  substitutes for a hardcoded value.
- **Golden-snapshot regression (informational only, never gates the
  suite's return value):** a module-level `_T01_GOLDEN = (219, 213.0,
  '2026-08-10')` tuple, printed as an `[INFO] MATCH` / `[INFO] DRIFTED` note
  on every run. A maintainer doing a same-corpus regression check sees
  immediately if something changed; a legitimate new-drive append that
  correctly shifts the peak no longer fails the suite — it prints
  `DRIFTED -- if expected, update _T01_GOLDEN` and the run still passes.

**Verification:** py_compile clean. Ran the corrected suite against both the
real 219-drive master (PASS, golden MATCH) and the simulated 220-drive
scratch master with the injected higher peak (PASS, golden correctly
reports DRIFTED) — confirming the fix resolves the exact failure mode the
audit described. Full regen + build + jsdom (9 tabs, 0 errors) confirm this
is a test-harness-only change: isolation diff vs. the M106+M107 baseline is
byte-identical to the pre-fix checkpoint (60 changed / 28 added / 65
removed leaves, all already accounted for by M110/M111/M112/M113/M114 — zero
new deltas from this fix, as expected since `_acceptance_tests` is not part
of `build_summary_arrays`). `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged.

## M116 — 2026-08-10 — Buffer impulse energy and duration (audit §10, "Feasible now")

First of the audit's three "Feasible now" §10 items. Ask: "Integrate battery
power during engine power-ramp intervals; summarize peak, area and recovery.
Quantifies the battery's transient support role without calling it generator
deficit."

**Method.** An engine-start is the cleanest, most unambiguous power-ramp
interval in this telemetry: RPM crosses from a sustained-OFF state to
running within a single ~1.3s sample step, giving an unambiguous trigger
time. Battery current is charge-positive raw (M11); flipped to
discharge-positive throughout, confirmed against a hand-inspected sample
event before writing any detection code — right at an RPM 0→1548 crossing,
discharge current visibly spikes from a ~6A baseline to ~15A over 1-2
samples, then flips to ~-13A (charging) as the engine catches up and repays
the borrowed energy: a direct telemetry illustration of this study's central
"battery as power buffer" thesis. For each detected start: `baseline` =
median discharge current in [t0-8s, t0-2s); `excess(t)` = discharge current
above that baseline in [t0-1s, t0+8s]; the impulse is the FIRST contiguous
run where excess exceeds 1.5A (not the window's global max — see below);
`peak`/`area`/`recovery` are read off that run (peak kW, dt-aware
trapezoidal Wh, peak-to-run-end seconds). Requires ≥2 above-threshold
samples and peak ≥3A to count.

**Two real bugs caught and fixed while prototyping** (validated first on a
hand-inspected event, then 4 sample drives, then 18 random drives, then the
full corpus, at each stage before trusting the numbers):
- Initial version took the window's global-max excess as the peak, which
  could — and did, on the very first test drive — pick an unrelated later
  current spike from ordinary driving instead of the actual ramp response.
  Fixed by taking the *first* above-threshold run following the trigger,
  which recovered the hand-verified sample event's own numbers
  (baseline≈6A, peak≈8.5A excess) that the global-max version had missed
  entirely.
- The engine-off confirmation check treated an *empty* pre-event RPM
  lookback (no samples in the window, not samples-that-are-zero) as
  "confirmed off," which is backwards — insufficient evidence should reject
  the candidate, not accept it. Fixed to require actual samples, all ≤100
  rpm.

**Corpus result** (`_buffer_impulse_summary`, frame_loader-only — the slim
raw cache already carries every column needed; no raw_loader fallback,
consistent with the existing `_k_ladder_scenarios` pattern): 2,211 events
across all 219 drives (33.76/100km, 6,548.5 km), median peak 35.54 kW (p95
71.94 kW), median duration 5.64s, median recovery 3.69s, median energy
26.22 Wh (p95 102.66 Wh) — 2.49% of total corpus driving time. Summed across
every event: 82.5 kWh of measured transient buffering, ~39× the pack's own
2.1kWh (unverified) rated capacity, delivered as small repeated draws rather
than any single deep discharge. Runtime: 23.5s standalone for the full
corpus (95s inside the full `_regen.py` pipeline run).

**Known limitation, documented in the block's own `methodology` string and
in the dashboard prose:** baseline is local to each specific restart and can
itself be negative (net charging) in stop-start driving following a prior
cycle's recharge tail — a real driving-pattern feature, not an artefact —
but it means an individual outlier event (max: 196.84 Wh, baseline -188A on
20260610_105454.csv) can partly reflect a coincident driver-demand
transition (e.g. braking into the restart) rather than engine-lag buffering
alone. Median/p95, not max, are the reported headline figures for exactly
this reason.

**Dashboard:** added as its own independent conditional block (`{S.bufferImpulse
&& S.bufferImpulse.nEvents > 0 && (...)}`), NOT nested inside the existing
`{S.oemTechReview && (...)}` M105 manufacturer-cross-check block it sits
next to — caught during jsdom verification that `oemTechReview` is absent
in this build environment, which would have silently hidden this new,
self-contained finding along with the unrelated OEM section if left nested.
Placed directly after the M105 paragraph (Highway vs city tab): M105 gives
the OEM's own qualitative account of the same battery-buffers-the-ramp
mechanism; this is the first quantification of it from this study's own
telemetry, framed explicitly as complementary to, not dependent on, M105.

established frozen-ML-column restoration step — see reasoning below):
- Row count 219/219, all columns present both sides.

**Why the frozen-column restoration step was correctly skipped here, not a
gap to fix.** The established "restore 16 frozen ML/domain columns
byte-exact" convention exists to stop an ordinary new-drive APPEND from
perturbing existing rows' ML outputs when nothing about those existing
rows' underlying features changed. This is the opposite case: `pct_highway`
and `pct_urban` are themselves inputs to the `drive_cluster_k3` KMeans
features, so they genuinely changed for every one of the 219 rows (not just
the 8 reclassified ones), and forcing the old cluster assignments back
would have made the corpus internally inconsistent -- new feature values
feeding a clustering result overridden to pretend they hadn't changed. The
canonical outlier-exclusion sets, which is what the "don't let unrelated
appends perturb old exclusions" guarantee actually protects, are confirmed
unchanged; that is the correct invariant to hold here, not byte-identical
component scores.

## M118 — 2026-08-10 — Generator ramp latency / load-point dwell (audit §10, "Feasible now")

Second of the audit's three "Feasible now" §10 items. Ask: "Segment engine
starts and RPM/load plateaus; estimate transitions conditional on speed
demand." "Direct control-strategy characterization."

**Method.** Reuses M116's engine-start trigger (RPM sustained-off ->
running within one ~1.3s sample) but asks a different question: not how
much the battery buffered, but how the generator's RPM actually settles
once it responds. RPM is quantized into 250 rpm bins — matching the
discrete-operating-point structure the M41 finding already established (the
generator steps between a handful of load-points, it does not hold a
continuously variable RPM) — and grouped into "plateaus": maximal runs of
consecutive samples in the same bin lasting >=3s. Ramp latency = time from
the trigger to the first qualifying plateau. Load-point dwell = each
plateau's own duration. A transition is the boundary between two
consecutive qualifying plateaus within the same engine-on cycle; vehicle
speed in a +-2s window around it answers "conditional on speed demand."

Deliberately no current-based eligibility gate (unlike M116) — this
detector counts every RPM-observable engine-start regardless of whether it
produced a measurable buffering signature, so its event count (3,728) is
larger than and not directly comparable to M116's (2,211); documented
explicitly in both the block's own `methodology` string and the dashboard
prose to head off a natural but wrong assumption that the two counts should
match.

**Corpus result** (`_ramp_latency_summary`, frame_loader-only, same
rationale as M116): 3,728 events across all 219 drives. Median ramp latency
1.13s (p95 10.72s); 41.8% of events register exactly 0.0s. This is a
resolution floor, not a physical claim: RPM is polled asynchronously at
native ~1.3s intervals, and the mechanical ramp can complete within a
single sample step — reported explicitly as such rather than silently
filtered out, since discarding zero-latency events would bias the reported
distribution upward. 9,197 qualifying plateaus, median dwell 8.61s (p95
56.77s). 5,469 plateau-to-plateau transitions, 5,457 with a matched speed
sample: median 101.0 km/h — transitions concentrate at highway pace,
consistent with load-point stepping being chiefly a highway-speed control
behaviour rather than a low-speed idle artefact. Runtime: 16.9s standalone
for the full corpus (102s inside the full `_regen.py` run).

**Dashboard:** added as its own independent conditional block
(`{S.rampLatency && S.rampLatency.nEvents > 0 && (...)}`), a sibling to
(not nested inside) the M116 buffer-impulse block, in the same Highway vs
city tab section — cross-references the M41 load-point-quantization finding
and explicitly flags the M116-vs-M118 event-count difference to the reader
rather than leaving it as an apparent inconsistency.

**Bug caught mid-edit, same class as M116's:** inserting the two new
functions ahead of `_dissipation_census` again accidentally dropped that
function's `def` signature line (the `old_str`/`new_str` boundary ended
right at that line and the replacement didn't re-include it) — identical
failure mode to the one caught and fixed during M116. Caught immediately
this time by grepping for the target signature right after the edit,
before running anything else; `py_compile` again did not flag it. Restored
and re-verified before proceeding.

Verification: babel + acorn-jsx parse clean; full regen (102s, 219 drives,
95 top-level keys, +1 from M117's 94); build 1211 KB; jsdom PASS (9 tabs, 0
errors); rendered-DOM text check confirms the paragraph renders on the

## M119 — 2026-08-10 — SoC hysteresis state machine (audit §10, "Feasible now")

Third and last of the audit's "Feasible now" §10 items. Ask: "Estimate
state-dependent start/stop probabilities versus SoC, speed, temperature and
recent demand." "Replaces fixed threshold narrative with probabilistic
control map."

**Method — different shape from M116/M118.** Those are per-EVENT
(engine-start-triggered). This is per-SECOND: a 1 Hz resampled grid
(soc/speed/rpm) is built for every drive; every second the engine is off is
an "at-risk" sample for a start in the following second, every second it's
on is at-risk for a stop. Empirical P(start)/P(stop) is tabulated by 5-point
SoC bin (marginal), then stratified by a speed band (stationary <5, low
5-60, high >=60 km/h) to test whether SoC alone actually sets the trigger
point, or whether demand matters more once SoC is known.

**Corpus result** (`_soc_hysteresis_summary`, frame_loader-only): 219 drives,
234,607 at-risk-start seconds (5,645 starts observed), 208,734 at-risk-stop
seconds (5,644 stops). Marginal: P(stop) rises with SoC as expected (~0.4%
at 45%, ~9% at 75%); P(start) is noisier but roughly stable through the
mid-band. The stratified result is the actual finding: at matched SoC,
P(start) differs by up to <strong>300×</strong> between stationary and
highway speed (SoC~60%: stationary 0.04%, highway 13.2%; SoC~55%: 0.07% vs
16.7%). Demand dominates over SoC once both are known — exactly the
"replaces fixed threshold" result the audit asked for, and a clean
quantitative complement to the M41 finding that engine-on discharge in the
80-120 km/h band is control strategy, not generator saturation.

**Reliability discipline, caught and fixed before shipping:** the first
pass filtered only the *stratified* table to n>=30 per cell; the *marginal*
table was unfiltered and included bins with n=7 and n=1 sitting alongside
bins with n>80,000 — a 71%-probability figure from 7 samples would have
rendered with the same apparent weight as a well-supported one. Applied the
same n>=30 filter to both tables before regenerating; every bin now shipped
carries at least a few hundred samples.

**Scope, disclosed rather than silently narrowed:** the audit's covariate
list is SoC, speed, temperature AND recent demand. This delivers SoC
(primary axis) and speed (the one stratifying secondary axis). Temperature
and a recent-demand proxy were prototyped but not shipped — a full 4-way
split fragments the ~235k/~209k at-risk samples into cells too sparse to
trust with binned tables; that needs a regression-style model (e.g.
logistic), which is future work, not this pass. Stated explicitly in the
block's own `methodology` string and in the dashboard prose.

**Dashboard:** added as its own independent conditional block, a sibling to
(not nested inside) the M118 ramp-latency block, in the same Highway vs
city tab section, directly following the existing "SoC hysteresis loop"
fixed-threshold chart it complements — framed explicitly as answering "does
this depend on anything besides SoC" rather than replacing the chart
outright.

Verification: babel + acorn-jsx parse clean (insertion done via precise
line-index manipulation rather than str_replace, after a non-unique-match
error on the first attempt — the ramp-latency/M105 section has several
structurally-identical `)}`/`</div>` closings, so a short anchor string
matched more than one location); full regen (119s, 219 drives, 96 top-level
keys, +1 from M118's 95); build 1222 KB; jsdom PASS (9 tabs, 0 errors);
rendered-DOM text check confirms the paragraph renders on the "highway vs
city" tab with every figure matching the pipeline output exactly.
T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS. `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged
(`48035ad3...`) — frame_loader-only, no master-file columns touched.
`bufferImpulse` (M116) and `rampLatency` (M118) confirmed unchanged;
`socHysteresis` is the sole new top-level key — a clean, isolated addition.

This closes the audit's three "Feasible now" §10 items (M115 coverage map

## M108 (completion) — 2026-08-11 — Lock the equivalence bounds; wire into the dashboard

Closes the last item that had been sitting open all session: TOST equivalence
testing (mixed-effects + cluster-robust OLS, previously built) was blocked on
an equivalence bound — a pre-registration decision that has to be fixed
before the result is inspected, not chosen to fit it. Andrii delegated the
specific bound selection; picked from the already-scoped candidate list with
the following reasoning, recorded here and in `degradation_trends.py`'s
module docstring for anyone re-auditing the choice:

- **Cell-spread: 0.2315 mV/month** (`reach50mV_over14yr`) — the only
  candidate anchored to a named, domain-meaningful consequence (the level at
  which BMS cell-balancing becomes a concern), not an arbitrary round number
  or an unjustified "stricter" alternative with no independent grounding.
- **Resistance: 0.5439 mΩ/month** (`oem75pct_over14yr`) — anchored to the
  same externally-sourced EU Battery Regulation Article-10 disclosure (M79)
  already cited elsewhere in this study, using the 14-year of the two offered
  horizons since it yields the *stricter* (smaller) monthly bound — consistent
  with this study's general preference for conservative, not permissive,
  equivalence criteria.

**The 14-year figure is a rate-derivation device only, not a life claim.**
Both bounds derive from "what monthly rate would carry a domain-meaningful
cumulative threshold to its consequence over a notional horizon" — the
horizon itself is never asserted as this vehicle's validated service life,
which is exactly the framing M113/M114 retracted elsewhere for the cycling
axis. TOST here tests monthly-RATE equivalence to zero; it makes no
calendar-life claim.

**Result, honestly reported:** under the locked bounds, equivalence is NOT
established for either metric at the current ~2.79-month window (cell-spread
p=0.4672, resistance p=0.3011) — the confidence intervals are still wider
than the bounds. This was already the expected outcome (flagged when the
bounds decision was first raised) and is reported as "inconclusive, window
too short," not reframed as either a drift finding or a disguised null
result. All three candidates per metric are retained in the output for
transparency; only the released one is offered as a result.

**Bug caught and fixed while wiring this in:** the degenerate resistance
mixed-effects model (day random-effects covariance singular — too few
drives per calendar day) returns `se=NaN`. Python's `json.dump` silently
emits bare `NaN`/`Infinity` tokens by default (`allow_nan=True`), which is
not valid JSON; `build_html.js`'s strict `JSON.parse` choked on it, the
build script crashed, and — because the crash happened before a new
`xtrail_dashboard.html` was written — `_jsdom_check.js` silently validated
the *previous, unrelated* M119 build instead of catching the problem,
reporting a false PASS. Caught only because the build's own exit output was
checked directly rather than trusting the jsdom PASS in isolation. Fixed
with a `_jround()` helper that maps non-finite floats to `null` at every
point a degenerate model's `se`/`ci95`/autocorrelation can produce one
(`_mixedlm`, `_cluster_ols`); re-verified zero bare `NaN` tokens in both the
standalone `degradation_trends.json` and the full `summary_arrays.json`
before re-running the build. A general lesson for this pipeline: a
raw-dependent regen success plus a jsdom PASS is not sufficient evidence a
build actually reflects new content — the build script's own exit status
must be checked, since a crash mid-chain can leave a stale-but-valid prior
artifact in place for every downstream check to pass against.

**Wired into the pipeline for the first time.** `degradation_trends.py` was
a fully standalone script all session (confirmed by grep: zero references
from `compute_summary_arrays.py` or the dashboard before this entry).
Refactored `build()` to accept an already-loaded DataFrame (not just a CSV
path), imported the module into `compute_summary_arrays.py`, and call it
inside `build_summary_arrays` right after `eligibility` — master-derived
only, no raw pass needed, so it's safe under arrays-only regeneration and
guaranteed to use the exact same `drive_master` snapshot as the rest of the
pipeline rather than a possibly-stale independent CSV re-read. Added
`degradationTrends` to `build_html.js`'s `REQUIRED_BLOCKS`, matching the
other `dm`-only always-present blocks (`eligibility`, `observedMix`).

**Dashboard:** added a paragraph in the Methodology & Data Provenance
section (Conclusions tab), directly after the M98 withdrawal writeup it
sits next to thematically (both are resistance-measurement methodology) —
states the released bounds, their rationale, the honest inconclusive
result, and the degenerate-model caveat already established for the vreg
proxy elsewhere on the page.

Verification: babel + acorn-jsx parse clean; full regen (95s, 219 drives, 97
top-level keys, +1 from M119's 96); build exit-status confirmed 0 (not just

errors) against the actually-rebuilt HTML; rendered-DOM text check confirms

MD5 unchanged (`48035ad3...`) — this is an arrays-side-only addition, no

## M120 — 2026-08-13 — I×V timestamp-alignment gap: a newly documented
zero-throughput failure mode (found during the Aug9–13 ingestion batch)

Motivation. Routine ingestion of 16 new drives (Aug 9–13; 219→235 drives,
+36.4km, GTC 482.2→486.6) surfaced two files — `20260813_145651.csv` and
`20260813_150341.csv` — that compute EXACTLY `gross_throughput_kwh=0.0`,
`gtc=0.0`, `fce=0.0`. Distance (2.2km / 4.6km) and SoC deltas (−1.575% /
+0.630%) confirm both are genuine short trips, not empty logs, so a zero
integral needed explaining before acceptance, per the standing "empirical
verification before pipeline changes" discipline.

Finding. Both files carry non-trivial `[BMS] HV Battery Current (A)` and
`[BMS] HV Battery voltage (V)` samples (72 and 238 valid I samples
respectively, plausible magnitude, e.g. −89.35..112.35A on the first file),
so the channels are not missing — but on both files the two PIDs are
polled on offset schedules with a **uniform 1.7–2.7s gap** between any I
sample and its nearest V sample (verified by direct nearest-neighbor
timestamp-gap computation: min/median/max gap 1.69/1.85/2.67s on
145651.csv, 1.54/1.72/2.69s on 150341.csv; 0% of I samples fall within
1.5s of any V sample on either file). `_v5_analyze_bytes`'s I×V alignment
step (`pd.merge_asof(..., tolerance=V_ALIGN_TOL)`, `V_ALIGN_TOL='1500ms'`)
therefore returns a zero-row frame on both files — every candidate I×V
pair sits just outside tolerance — and the trapezoidal energy integral
correctly sums to 0.0 over an empty index. This is deterministic, correct
behaviour of the existing v5/v6 code given its stated tolerance; it is NOT
an integration bug and nothing in `compute_drive_summary_v6.py` was
changed to produce or investigate this. It is best read as a third failure
mode alongside the two already on record: M18's "current-PID starvation"
domain rule (too few I samples full stop) and ordinary short-trip
denominator inflation (M35) — this one is specifically an I/V CO-TIMING
gap, present even when both channels individually have enough samples.

Disposition (this batch). Neither file trips `f_domain`
(`|energy_residual_kwh_corr2p|` = 0.1575 / 0.0630 kWh, both under the
0.35 kWh `RESIDUAL_MAX_KWH` rule) or `ens_outlier_v2`, so both are
retained, unmodified, as valid-but-throughput-blind rows in group
statistics — consistent with this study's practice of disclosing rather
than silently patching or excluding boundary cases (cf. M88, M98). No
change was made to `V_ALIGN_TOL`, `_asof`, or any other extraction logic:
widening the tolerance would alter every historical drive's I×V-aligned
columns, which needs its own byte-exact regression pass and is explicitly
OUT OF SCOPE for a routine ingestion batch. Flagged here as an open
methodology item for a future dedicated pass (candidate: either widen
`V_ALIGN_TOL` with full regression verification, or add a
`iv_alignment_gap_s` diagnostic column so files like these are
distinguishable from genuinely current-starved ones without re-deriving
the timestamp gap by hand each time).

Ingestion mechanics (this batch, for completeness). Standard protocol:
`analyze_bytes` ×16 → append/sort → `postprocess_master` on the full
235-row frame → freeze/restore the 16 ML/domain columns for the 219
pre-existing rows (restore diff counts on the continuous score columns —
`iso_score`/`lof_score`, 218/218 — are run-to-run float jitter, expected
per M47; `f_domain_2p` showed 0 diff, also as M47 predicts) → raw slim
cache rebuilt from scratch for all 235 files (no `raw_cache.tar` was
present in Project Knowledge this session) → `summary_config.json`
updated (`ambientByDrive` ×16, `vehicle.odometerKm` 42,403→42,538 as of

`[VCM] HV Battery Available Charge Display (%)`, and `[VCM] Motor Torque
(N.m)` (actual, not target); ADDS `[BMS] Input possible power (hp)`,

Turbo`, `G05 Throttle`, `G06 Additional`, `G07 BMS Power Limits`, `G08 BMS

alignment tolerance, since both remain far below every relevant threshold.

Disposition. NO CODE CHANGES were required. `COL_MAP` in
`compute_drive_summary_v6.py` is a positive whitelist: any raw column not
named in it (including all nine `G0X` group columns and the two new BMS
possible-power channels) is parsed by pandas but never entered into the

optional inputs consumed only by the socVcmMapping raw-frame chart, which
degrades to fewer points, not an error, for these 4 rows.

New-parameter opportunity (not implemented this batch, per "parsimony over
infrastructure"). `[BMS] Input/Output possible power (hp)` is the BMS's own
real-time dynamic power-limit computation -- an OEM-native capability
envelope, distinct from and more authoritative than the M14
`deficit_80_120_pct` generator-saturation proxy this study currently relies
on. A future M-pass could compare measured `P` (already computed per-drive)
against `Output possible power` to derive a genuine headroom-utilization
metric (fraction of BMS-declared capability actually drawn), directly
extending the buffer-not-reservoir thesis with a manufacturer-provided
reference rather than an inferred one. Flagged as a candidate, not
scheduled: needs its own validation pass (units check hp->kW, alignment
tolerance choice, and confirmation the channel is populated broadly enough
across the corpus to be useful) before it can enter COL_MAP.

## M122 — 2026-08-14 — Rework M116/M118 charts from RangeBar summaries to
distributional views + explicit start-event reconciliation (audit §10
follow-up; supersedes the charts shipped in M120 2026-08-14)

Motivation. Andrii flagged the M116 (buffer impulse) and M118 (ramp
latency) charts — added in the same-dated M120 entry above — as hard to
understand: each was four `Kpi` cards plus two `RangeBar` components (a bar
spanning median→p95), which communicates a spread but nothing about
distribution SHAPE, and gave no indication that the two censuses measure
the same underlying engine-start events. Requested: reconcile the charts to
add more meaning, and have the graphics explain both the findings and the
process.

Root-cause finding. `_buffer_impulse_events`/`_ramp_latency_events`
(compute_summary_arrays.py) already compute rich per-event data — energies,
peaks, durations, latencies, dwells, plateau RPMs, transition speeds — but
`_buffer_impulse_summary`/`_ramp_latency_summary` discarded everything
except mean/median/p95/max before it ever reached the JSX, so no chart
could have shown more than two range bars regardless of front-end effort.
Separately, the M116 prose computed `totalWh/1000/2.1*100` and labelled the
result "×" — rendering "3940×" against a true capacity-turnover multiple of
39.4×; a units bug (percent computed, "×" printed), not a data error, fixed
in this pass.

Method. Added `_start_event_analytics` (new M122 block in
`compute_summary_arrays.py`, after `_ramp_latency_summary`): one
`frame_loader` pass that RE-RUNS the canonical `_buffer_impulse_events` /
`_ramp_latency_events` detectors verbatim (no re-derivation of trigger or
eligibility logic) and a new `_engine_start_triggers` helper sharing their
exact sustained-off→running trigger definition, then aggregates per-event
output into histograms, percentile ladders, and a trigger-level
reconciliation. Verified canonical-faithful before any enrichment: an
offline replay of the two existing detectors over all 239 raw files (same
`format='%H:%M:%S.%f'` time-parse as `drive_raw_cache.py`, no midnight-wrap
handling needed) reproduced the shipped `nEvents` (2224/3754), `totalWh`
(82,747.3... — see below), and every percentile in the current
`summary_arrays.json` exactly, confirming the offline frame_loader is
equivalent to the pipeline's own for these two detectors.

New data (merged additively; no existing key removed or renamed).
`bufferImpulse` gains `energyHist`, `peakKwHist` (10-Wh / 10-kW bins + a
closed overflow tail), `energyLadder`/`peakKwLadder`/`durationLadder`/
`recoveryLadder` (p10–p99), `capKwhAssumed` (2.1, unverified — disclosed
inline) and `capacityMultiple` (39.4, replacing the buggy inline
computation). `rampLatency` gains `latencyHistPos` (latencies >0s only; the
exactly-0.0s resolution-floor population is kept separate as `nZero` so it
is never conflated with the measured distribution), `dwellHist`,
`firstPlateauRpmDist` (integer-RPM counts — the discrete M41 load-point
set-points), `transitionSpeedHist`, `plateausPerEventDist`, and matching
percentile ladders. New top-level `startEventReconcile`: `nStartTriggers`
(4304, shared by both detectors by construction), `nBufferEvents`/
`nRampEvents`/`nBoth`/`nBufferOnly`/`nRampOnly`/`nNeither` (2224/3754/1901/
323/1853/227), `bufferGatePct`/`rampGatePct` (51.7%/87.2%), and a
`methodology` string stating the two eligibility gates explicitly (M116:
discharge excess ≥3A; M118: ≥1 RPM plateau ≥3s).

Findings surfaced by the new data (previously invisible behind
mean/median/p95). Per-event buffer energy is sharply right-skewed — 596 of
2224 events sit in the 0–10 Wh bin, decaying smoothly to a 131-event ≥100Wh
tail — the buffer signature the thesis argues for, now visible as a shape
rather than asserted from two numbers. `firstPlateauRpmDist` is strongly
quantized: 3125/3754 (83%) of starts land their first stable plateau at
EXACTLY 2000 rpm, a direct visual tie-in to the M41 load-point-quantization
finding. `transitionSpeedHist` concentrates at 90–120 km/h, supporting
load-point stepping as a highway control behaviour rather than a low-speed
artefact. Reconciliation quantifies what "2224 vs 3754 events" actually
means: both counts descend from the same 4304 triggers; 1901 events pass
both gates, 323 buffer-only (current spike without a sustained plateau),
1853 ramp-only (a plateau forms without tripping the 3A current gate), 227
neither.

Dashboard (`xtrail_summary.jsx`). Two new chart primitives:
`MiniHist` (categorical histogram from `{edges,counts}`, with an optional
muted `floor` bar for the ramp-latency 0.0s population) and `CatBars`
(categorical bars for the first-plateau RPM distribution). New
`EngineStartProcess` component — inserted as its own "Two views of one
event" block immediately before the existing M116 detail block, guarded by
`S.startEventReconcile && S.bufferImpulse && S.rampLatency` — rendering (a)
the reconciliation funnel as three proportional bars (triggers → ramp-gated
→ current-gated, each annotated with its %-of-triggers) plus a
both/buffer-only/ramp-only/neither breakdown, and (b) a data-bound SVG
timeline schematic of ONE median event on a shared clock: a generator-RPM
lane (latency → plateau at ~2000rpm → dwell) directly above a battery-kW
lane (impulse rise/peak/decay → recovery, with energy/peak/duration
labelled), both keyed to a single t=0 engine-start-trigger marker — this is
the "explain the process" graphic Andrii asked for, distinct from the
existing distributional charts which explain the "findings." Both
`BufferImpulseChart` and `RampLatencyChart` (the M120 RangeBar
implementations) were REPLACED, not extended: `BufferImpulseChart` now
shows the 4 KPIs + `energyHist` + a log-scale capacity-turnover strip (1
pack → 39.4×, replacing the buggy inline "×" computation with the
`capacityMultiple` binding); `RampLatencyChart` now shows the 4 KPIs +
`latencyHistPos` (0.0s floor rendered as a separate muted bar) +
`firstPlateauRpmDist` via `CatBars` + `transitionSpeedHist`.

Verification. `ast.parse` clean on `compute_summary_arrays.py`.
`summary_arrays.json` regenerated via the validated frame_loader (indent=1,
ensure_ascii=False): diffed against the pre-M122 file — every pre-existing
scalar key in `bufferImpulse`/`rampLatency` (nEvents, energyWh, peakKw,
durationS, impulseTimeFractionPct, zeroLatencyPct, rampLatencyS,
plateauDwellS, transitionSpeedKmh) is byte-identical; every OTHER top-level
key in the file is byte-identical; only the 3 intended keys
(`bufferImpulse`, `rampLatency`, `startEventReconcile`) changed. Corpus
totals unaffected (239 drives / 6,591.7 km). `build_html.js`:
`REQUIRED_BLOCKS` gate and M94 stale-key gate both clean; wrote
`xtrail_dashboard.html` 1279KB; identical pre-existing hardcoded-literal
WARN list (9 items — "93 drives" etc., all pre-existing prose in unrelated
sections, none introduced by this pass). Render validation used
`renderToStaticMarkup` (synchronous SSR) rather than the jsdom harness this
session, per the project's own documented "`createRoot` stalls under
jsdom" convention: 11 targeted checks against `App`, `BufferImpulseChart`,
`RampLatencyChart`, and `EngineStartProcess` all PASS with 0 render
errors — App renders (9/9 tab buttons present), both rewritten charts
render ≥10/≥15 histogram bars respectively and bind the correct headline
figures (39.4× capacity multiple; 2000-rpm plateau spike), and the new
process schematic renders its SVG with the reconciliation figures (4304
triggers, 1901 both-gate) and both Gen./Batt. lanes present. Built HTML
confirmed to embed all three new keys (`startEventReconcile` ×4,
`capacityMultiple` ×3, `firstPlateauRpmDist` ×3).

Not run this session (flag for next full-chain pass in Andrii's
environment): the project's own jsdom 9-tab click-through harness
(`_jsdom_check.js`) and the T-01–T-04 acceptance-test suite — this
session's SSR-equivalent checks are a substitute, not a replacement, for

band time (488.1 s / 420.2 s, `deficit_80_120_valid=True`).

(n=2 domain-excluded). Degradation trending remains statistically null:

T-controlled (CI [−1.503, 2.626], P(slope>0)=0.696, n_clean=128) — both

### Ingestion provenance / invariants

  archive 16 ML/domain columns → `analyze_bytes` × 2 → append+sort →
  `postprocess_master` → restore ML16 byte-exact for the 239 pre-existing

- **Pre-existing per-drive physical invariants: ALL ZERO** (distance,
  gross/net throughput, GTC, FCE, rf_efc, SoC, peaks, resistances,
  temperatures unchanged on all 239 rows).
- **ML16 restore byte-exact** (0 NaN-aware diffs on pre-existing rows).
- The only pre-existing-row changes are the 12 corpus-dependent columns
  that recalibrate by design with every ingestion: `I_offset_A_applied` /
  `I_offset_2p_A_applied` and their derived `offset_kwh_removed` /
  `net_draw_kwh_corr(2p)` / `energy_residual_kwh_corr(2p)` /
  `net_draw_per100km_corr(2p)`, plus the corpus-regression
  `cell_spread_loaded_p95_adj_mv` / `_adj_hub_mv`.
- Config: `vehicle.odometerKm` 42,545 → 42,614 (dash reading, Aug 14);
  `ambientByDrive` +2 (D5 [23,23]; D6 [16,15]); the "Aug 14" session /
  sessionGroup updated 4 → 6 drives, 6.8 → 75.1 km, type urban → mixed,
  so the ledger reconciles on-date (shortfall unchanged at 1 — the
  pre-existing multi-date grouping).

### Fourth raw-logging PID configuration

The two files carry **77 columns** — a fourth distinct logger set. Vs the

columns are excluded from all calculations; the `Input/Output possible
power` channels remain unconsumed (candidate for a future BMS-envelope
headroom-utilisation analysis — see M121). `[VCM] Vehicle Speed` and
`[VCM] HV Battery Available Charge Display` remain absent, so obd_fallback
speed is engaged automatically (as designed) and `soc_vcm` is unpopulated.

### Polling-frequency step-up

Row-union logging cadence rose to **~14 Hz** (median inter-row dt 0.071 s),
the union of interleaved PID groups. The per-PID cadences that actually
drive the metrics: BMS current/voltage/SoC and VCM speed/RPM at
**~1.28–1.32 Hz** (0.76 s period; `I_sample_period_s` 0.759 / 0.779 s vs
the corpus median 1.266 s — a ~1.7× finer current-integration step),
and the pack-temperature PID at ~0.16 Hz (6.16 s). The finer current step
tightens the rectangular coulomb-integration quantisation and improves
capture of sub-second buffer transients (M116-class events); it does not
alter any cross-drive comparison, since all coulometric columns already
integrate on each drive's own native Δt.
